records.title: VP, Production - Soft Accessories
records.description:
About Us:

Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. Centric Brands is focused on our customers and our brands that will drive the company’s future growth. We are defined by innovation as we seize new opportunities and thrive in an environment informed by creativity and thinking that is both analytical and outside the box. Centric Brands reflects a team built on respect, for others and for the hard work it takes to achieve our goals and build our bright future together.

**Production**

From sourcing raw materials to manufacturing, order placement, pricing and quality control and getting the finished product where it needs to be, our production team is responsible for ensuring we keep our standards high and our business profitable at every step of the journey. If you are a focused, results -driven, tenacious and highly flexible team player, we’ll give you every opportunity to build a rewarding career with one of the world’s foremost major lifestyle brand collectives.

Specific Responsibilities Would Include:

Centric Brands is looking for a dynamic, creative and resourceful Vice President of Production, Soft Accessories, to join its team. This individual must be a self-starter and collaborative leader who takes initiative, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and is excited to accelerate transformation across Centric Brands. The Vice President of Production, Soft Accessories, oversees all facets of global development, manufacturing and supply chain operations for cold weather accessories, including scarves, gloves, hats, beanies and related knit accessories. This leader will identify and manage the appropriate vendors and factories, negotiate manufacturing orders, and ensure the timely delivery of high-quality, profitable goods.

**ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategy & Innovation**

 

* Partner with corporate resources to achieve global production efficiencies across divisions and groups
* Lead ongoing market and competitive research to identify innovations in leather, knitwear, yarns, fibers, fabrications, construction, trims and finishing techniques. Translate relevant developments into actionable recommendations for Merchandising and Design, and maintain a current archive of yarns, materials, hardware and production techniques.

**Operations and Results**

* Oversee and continuously evaluate the approved vendor matrix for cold weather accessories, with particular focus on factories with strong technical capabilities in knit scarves, gloves (knit & leather), hats, beanies and related accessories. Review costing, capacity, quality and production standards.
* Lead high-level negotiations on yarn, material, trim and finished-goods pricing to ensure profitability. Approve final buys; oversee production from development samples through final delivery; resolve vendor non-compliance, claims and chargebacks; and coordinate customs classification requirements with Imports.
* Partner with Merchandising, Design and Sales throughout product development to ensure accurate execution of cold weather accessories, including stitch, gauge, yarn, handfeel, fit, construction, color and finishing. Deliver agreed-upon margin goals and development-calendar milestones across the assortment.
* Review production standards and brand consistency across categories and vendors. Oversee quality-control initiatives, including testing and corrective action plans for yarn performance, pilling, shrinkage, colorfastness, seam strength, embellishments, trims and overall product durability.
* Lead high-level troubleshooting of quality and technical issues. Guide special product development and modifications to designs, materials, stitches and constructions while protecting the intended aesthetic, performance and financial goals.
* Oversee capacity planning and vendor performance by sourcing office, region, country and factory. Define accurate costing models; partner with Sales and Planning to project production needs; make yarn and raw-material commitments when appropriate; allocate production; and reserve factory capacity for seasonal peaks.
* any issues

**Customers & Relationships**

* Partner with customers, Sales, Merchandising and Operations, as well as vendors and factories to ensure adequate flow of goods relative to orders and anticipated demand criteria
* Oversee interoffice communication and follow-up with internal and external customers and contacts regarding production, including suppliers and vendors
* Delegate special projects as assigned
* Travel regularly to factories and international trade shows

**Leadership & Teams**

* Lead, train and motivate global team of full-time and part-time personnel as well as factory and independent agents; strategize staffing needs across categories and brands, where appropriate
* Contribute positively to team dynamic and manage up where necessary
* Attract, develop and retain talent; create appropriate succession plans
* Monitor and evaluate performance of individuals and team(s)

Our Best Fit Candidate Would Have:

* Superior organizational skills and excellent communication skills; team oriented
* Ability to multi-task and meet deadlines, highly detail oriented and meticulous
* Creativity, technical capability and sensibility for merchandising/design
* Required hands-on production and sourcing experience in cold weather accessories, including scarves, gloves (knit & leather), hats, beanies and related knit accessories.
* Bachelor’s Degree
* 10+ years’ experience in production and sourcing; significant relevant experience in category

records.title: Corporate Director of Quality
records.description:
Take the next step with an exciting and growing company
 
As the only fully integrated maker of premium quality wire, rope, and assemblies, Loos & Co holds a leading position in the global aerospace sector.
 
A division of the Central Wire (CWI) Group of Companies encompassing 12 locations in three countries, 750+ employees, and over six decades of excellence, Loos & Co solutions are found in mission critical flight control applications. Our precision-manufactured components are also used for defense, med tech, and heavy industry purposes around the world, in large part because of the people behind our products.
 
Do you have a strong work ethic? Take pride in a job well done? Are you passionate about contributing to individual and team, company and customer successes? If you’re interested in joining a dynamic work environment that offers opportunities to reach your full potential, we want to hear from you.
 
 
Position Summary / Essential Function
 
The Corporate Director of Quality is CWI’s senior enterprise Quality leader and is responsible for establishing and sustaining a culture of quality excellence, accountability, customer focus, product safety, and continuous improvement across aerospace, commercial, medical, metal rope, and assembly facilities. Based in Pomfret Center, Connecticut and reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director leads the enterprise Quality function, develops high-performing teams of Quality professionals, and establishes the governance, systems, standards, metrics, and decision rights required for consistent execution across all locations.
 
A central responsibility of the role is to create a results- and data-driven culture in which decisions are based on objective evidence, process capability, customer and regulatory requirements, risk, and measurable business outcomes. The Director advances the organization from reactive inspection and problem resolution toward prevention, disciplined problem solving, statistical thinking, robust corrective action, and sustained operational excellence.
 
The Director maintains the effectiveness and certification readiness of applicable quality management systems, including AS9100D and ISO 9001 for aviation, space, defense, and commercial operations; ISO 13485 for medical-device operations where applicable; and customer-, product-, and facility-specific requirements for metal rope, wire rope, cable, and assemblies. The role ensures that customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements take precedence where they exceed or conflict with general quality-system requirements.
 
Key Responsibilities
 

* Build, lead, develop, and retain a high-performing organization of Quality professionals across CWI, with clear roles, decision rights, measurable objectives, development plans, succession pipelines, and performance expectations.
* Create a results- and data-driven culture of Quality excellence in which teams use objective evidence, trend analysis, statistical methods, and risk-based thinking to identify priorities, prevent defects, and verify sustained improvement.
* Establish and execute the enterprise Quality strategy, organizational design, staffing plan, technical roadmap, and resource priorities in alignment with CWI business and operating objectives.
* Own enterprise governance for quality management systems and maintain certification readiness for applicable aerospace, commercial, medical, metal rope, and assembly facilities, including registrar, customer, regulatory, and internal audits.
* Ensure aerospace quality controls address AS9100D requirements, including operational risk management, configuration management, product safety, counterfeit-parts prevention, special-process control, production process verification, foreign-object damage prevention, traceability, and awareness of ethical behavior.
* Ensure first article inspection and production process verification practices align with AS9102 when contractually applicable, and ensure special processes are qualified, controlled, and approved to customer, regulatory, or other requirements where applicable.
* Ensure medical quality-system controls align with ISO 13485 and applicable regulatory and customer requirements, including risk management, validated processes, traceability, complaint handling, CAPA, change control, and record retention.
* Establish common standards for document and record control, calibration, inspection and test, nonconforming output, CAPA, root-cause analysis, internal auditing, management review, supplier quality, customer complaints, product and process change control, and continuous improvement.
* Establish an enterprise Quality performance-management system with leading and lagging indicators for customer complaints, escapes, first-pass yield, scrap and rework, cost of poor quality, supplier defects, audit findings, process capability, CAPA aging, recurrence, and corrective-action effectiveness.
* Lead monthly operating reviews and formal management reviews that convert Quality data into executive-level insights, identify systemic and emerging risks, assign accountable owners, and track actions through verified closure.
* Develop Quality leaders who can influence Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Commercial teams; make risk-based decisions; escalate product-safety or conformity concerns; and hold the organization accountable for results.
* Serve as the senior Quality escalation point for significant customer complaints, product escapes, product-safety events, audit findings, systemic nonconformances, supplier-quality issues, and certification or regulatory risks.
* Ensure robust containment, root-cause analysis, corrective action, effectiveness verification, and lessons-learned deployment for significant or recurring failures, including consideration of human factors where relevant.
* Provide enterprise oversight for supplier-quality strategy, supplier qualification, risk-based surveillance, source inspection, flow-down of customer and regulatory requirements, and supplier corrective action.
* Partner with the Chief Operating Officer, Plant Managers, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Commercial, and other leaders to integrate Quality into operational performance, new-product introduction, manufacturing transfers, and change management.
* Communicate Quality-system health, certification status, customer performance, material risks, resource needs, and improvement results clearly to executive leadership and the Board or ownership group when requested.
* Perform other related duties consistent with the role, grade, and business needs.

Required Qualifications
 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy, Quality, Manufacturing, or a closely related technical discipline.
* Twelve or more years of progressive Quality, manufacturing, engineering, or operational leadership experience in regulated or high-reliability manufacturing.
* At least seven years of direct people-leadership experience, including leadership of Quality managers and professionals, performance management, coaching, organizational design, and succession planning.
* At least five years of multi-site or enterprise Quality leadership experience with accountability for common systems, audits, metrics, and cross-site standardization.
* Demonstrated responsibility for an AS9100D-certified quality management system and successful participation as the senior Quality leader in at least one third-party certification or recertification cycle.
* Demonstrated experience with internal and external audit programs, management review, CAPA, root-cause analysis, configuration and change control, supplier quality, product safety, traceability, nonconformance control, and customer complaint resolution.
* Demonstrated use of Quality data and statistical methods to improve performance, including examples of measurable reduction in defects, escapes, cost of poor quality, or recurring corrective actions.
* Ability to travel approximately 25% to 40% to CWI facilities, customer sites, supplier sites, and audit locations, with additional travel during significant launches, audits, or quality events.
* Ability to communicate technical and business risk, priorities, decisions, and performance clearly to plant, functional, customer, registrar, and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications
 

* Experience in specialty metals, wire, cable, wire rope, aircraft cable, mechanical cable, swaging, metal assemblies, or other highly engineered metal products.
* Experience leading Quality in aerospace and defense manufacturing, including customer flow-downs, AS9102 first article inspection, source inspection, special processes, counterfeit-parts controls, configuration management, product safety, and foreign-object damage prevention.
* Experience with ISO 13485-certified medical-device manufacturing and risk-management practices aligned with ISO 14971 where applicable.
* Experience with Nadcap-accredited special processes, Defense Contract Management Agency oversight, Federal Aviation Administration-regulated products, or major aerospace prime and Tier 1 customer requirements, as applicable to CWI’s business.
* Advanced degree in Engineering, Operations, Quality, or Business Administration.
* Experience using an electronic QMS, ERP, business-intelligence, and statistical software to manage Quality performance and traceability.

Preferred Certifications
 

* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE) or equivalent senior Quality leadership credential.
* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or AS9100 Lead Auditor certification.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt.
* Certified Manufacturing Engineer, Professional Engineer, Project Management Professional, or comparable technical credential as relevant.

Key Leadership Competencies
 

* Enterprise Quality leadership and culture building
* Leadership, development, and retention of Quality professionals
* Results orientation and measurable accountability
* Data-driven decision making and statistical thinking
* AS9100D, ISO 9001, and regulated quality-system leadership
* Product safety, compliance, and risk-based judgment
* CAPA, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action effectiveness
* Customer quality and executive escalation
* Cross-functional influence and change leadership
* Continuous improvement and operational excellence
* Executive communication and management review
* Multi-site governance and standardization

Leadership Standard
 
Success in this position is measured not simply by maintaining certifications or passing audits, but by the Director’s ability to build capable Quality leaders and teams, establish measurable accountability, improve the effectiveness of CWI’s quality systems, reduce recurring failures and customer escapes, strengthen process capability, protect product safety and conformity, and demonstrate sustained improvement through objective performance data.
 
Physical and Work Environment Requirements
 
The role operates in office and active manufacturing environments and requires regular interaction with plant operations. It may require walking or standing on production floors, observing machinery and manufacturing activities, using a computer and quality information systems, and communicating in areas where hearing protection or other personal protective equipment is required. Travel among company locations, customer sites, supplier sites, and audit locations is expected. Reasonable accommodations will be considered in accordance with applicable law. This description identifies the essential functions of the position but is not intended to list every physical activity or working condition.
 
Base Salary Range
 
$142,000-$204,500
 
Benefits
 
Subject to the terms, eligibility requirements, and amendment provisions of the applicable plans and policies:
 

* 401(k) with matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Pre-Employment Drug Testing
 
All applicants who are offered a position with the Company will be required to successfully complete a post-offer drug screening, where permitted by applicable law and in accordance with Company policy.
 
At-Will Employment
 
Employment with the Company is at will. Either the employee or the Company may terminate employment at any time, with or without cause or notice, subject to applicable law. Nothing in this job description creates a contract of employment or alters the at-will employment relationship.
 
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
 
The Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination or harassment based on any protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law.
 
 
**Benefits:** 

* Health, Dental and Vision insurance options
* Life insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Employee assistance program
* Employee Referral program
* Tuition reimbursement

**Shift:** 8-hour shift
 
**Work Location:** In person, Company does not provide relocation assistance.
 
Central Wire Group of Companies is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability status, or any other applicable characteristics protected by law.
 
Central Wire Group of Companies is a Drug-free workplace and pre-employment drug tests and background checks are required.

records.title: Director, Quality
records.description:
**Job Details**
---------------

**Job Title: Director, Quality**

**Location: Meriden, CT**

**Work Arrangement:** Onsite

**About the Role**
------------------

**The Director of Quality** provides leadership, direction, and support to the Quality team, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer focus. This role is responsible for ensuring the safe, compliant, and consistent manufacture, validation, and delivery of chemical products while maintaining the highest standards of quality and operational excellence. As a leader of the Quality Team, the Director coaches, develops, and empowers team members to achieve individual and departmental goals, build technical expertise, and drive continuous improvement across the organization. The Director also ensures timely and effective management of quality-related communications, processes and programs that support both customer satisfaction and business growth. Working closely with colleagues across Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Sales, and Customer Service, the Director of Quality establishes and maintains robust quality systems, drives regulatory compliance, and identifies opportunities to improve processes, reduce risk, and enhance product integrity. Through strong leadership and partnership, this role helps ensure customer requirements are met, supports the company's commitment to safety and quality, and contributes to the organization's long-term success and reputation in the marketplace.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Provide leadership for functional area
* Establish and ensure Quality policies, standards, and objectives ensuring best practices through benchmarking and collaboration with regional and corporate colleagues
* Drive overall compliance ensuring on-time completion of key deliverables
* Responsible for document control, SOP’s, master training schedule, Certificates of Conformance, review and approve relabel PITAs etc.
* Review and approve all quality reports such as annual product review, temperature mapping, validation, internal audit, etc.
* Conducting timely audits, management reviews batch review and release, supply chain, supplier and product qualification
* Advises leadership on quality risks, compliance matters, and strategic quality improvement opportunities
* Driving continuous improvement and risk assessment initiatives
 

**Decision-Making and Problem Solving**

 

* Establishes and approves quality policies, procedures, standards, and quality objectives
* Makes final decisions regarding product release, product disposition, and quality-related exceptions
* Determines appropriate corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) in response to quality events, customer complaints, audit findings, and nonconformances.
* Decides when production processes, materials, or products fail to meet quality or regulatory requirements and may halt production or shipment when necessary
* Evaluates and approves supplier quality programs, qualification processes, and remediation plans
* Recommends investments in quality systems, laboratory capabilities, technology, staffing, and continuous improvement initiatives
* Serves as the organization's lead authority during regulatory inspections, customer audits, and significant quality incidents

**Skills**
----------

* Ability to drive Quality focus throughout the organization
* Strong strategic thinking and problem solving skills
* Experience in developing and maintaining Quality Management Systems
* Expertise in Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP)
* Demonstrated ability in leading and managing audits and regulatory inspections
* Strong leadership and decision-making capabilities
* Ability to manage large teams and projects
* Strong communication and influencing skills
* Change management

**Job Requirements**
--------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biology, Engineering, Quality Management, or a related scientific discipline required
* Master's degree in a related field preferred
* 7 - 10 years of progressive experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Quality Systems, or Regulatory Compliance within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, or regulated chemical manufacturing industry
* 5+ years of people leadership experience managing and developing professional teams
* Experience leading Quality Management Systems (QMS) within a cGMP-regulated environment
* Demonstrated experience interacting with regulatory agencies, customers, and external auditors

**About Caldic**
----------------

At BrandNu, a Caldic Company, we’re a global leader in distribution solutions, serving diverse markets across the world. Joining us means becoming part of an entrepreneurial, collaborative, and innovation-driven team.

 

**We offer:**

* Competitive benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, legal, 401(k) with company contributions, paid time off and more
* An inclusive, diverse, and dynamic work environment
* The chance to shape the future of specialty ingredient solutions across industries like food, pharma, personal care, and more

We operate in 43 countries around the world. Our innovative solutions are tailored to meet the needs of industries such as food, pharma, personal care, and industrial markets, ensuring sustainable success for all stakeholders. To learn more, visit: www.caldic.com

 

**Ready to Join Us?**

If you're ready to take your career to the next level and join a global leader, apply now at BrandNu Laboratories, a Caldic company!

**Equal Opportunity Employer**
------------------------------

Caldic celebrates diversity and is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, gender, or any other characteristic.

records.title: Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing
records.description:
Bold Thinking. World Changing. At SkyWater, our ingenuity helps improve lives around the world by manufacturing U.S. made semiconductors that are essential ingredients of modern life. Automotive safety enhancements, life-saving medical devices, consumer electronics and American security require semiconductors. Working in our Minnesota headquarters, Florida, or Texas location — employees join together to improve the world.
 
 
Explore what’s possible. Joining our U.S. - based team means contributing to and learning about the commercialization of some of the most exciting technologies the world has ever seen. We are turning “science fiction” into everyday reality through technologies such as superconducting, 3D integrated circuits or computer chips, carbon nanotubes, photonic logic devices, micro electro-mechanical systems and other emerging device topologies. We manufacture products for aerospace and defense, medical, automotive, consumer and industrial markets, to name a few. Our customers include emerging leaders who rely on our intellectual property security and quality manufacturing services.
 
 
Step into the future. SkyWater’s values of Integrity, Excellence, Collaboration, Empowerment and Growth Mindset guide us to cultivate an empowered, learning environment. We also invest in developing highly skilled, dedicated employees — and employees who are entering the workforce for the first time, from the military, and a variety of educational backgrounds.
 
 
Are you bold thinking? Find your place on our team and help us change the world!
 
 
**Primary Objective:** 
Join an innovative semiconductor manufacturing organization at the forefront of advanced technology and manufacturing excellence. The Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing owns the operational, financial, and strategic leadership of the Bloomington fabrication facility, including the Advanced Technology Services (ATS) Process Engineering Technician team. This role ensures the factory achieves world-class safety, quality, output, cycle time, and cost performance while directing a 24/7 organization and partnering across engineering, planning, and quality teams to meet all customer and business commitments.
 
In this role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end operational execution, strategic planning, budgetary ownership, and leadership to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient semiconductor manufacturing. You will be responsible for driving absolute excellence across safety, quality, output, cost optimization, and ensuring smooth production flow to consistently meet internal and external customer quality and on-time delivery (OTD) commitments, and fab velocity metrics / key performance indicators (KPIs).
 
The successful candidate will own the organizational design and talent strategy for their organization, serving as a role model and lead a highly matrixed organization consisting of the Manufacturing team, Process Engineering Technicians group, and Flow Engineers. This role is expected to partner closely with Program Managers, Technical Leads, Wafer Planning, Manufacturing, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development teams to improve operational performance, resolve manufacturing constraints, and deliver business objectives. This leader will play a critical role in transforming factory capabilities to meet strict customer commitments and flexible demand by influencing long-range capacity and setting standards for the MN fab operations organization.
 
 
**Major Areas of Accountability:** 

* Operations Leadership: Lead the daily and long-term operational execution in the fab, as well as the ATS technician and flow engineer teams to meet all production starts, output targets, yield expectations, cycle time goals, and quality standards, including setting clear priorities for the organization. Direct, develop, and coach the 24/7 operations teams—including Production, ATS Process Engineering Technicians, and Flow Engineers—to ensure capability, accountability, and organizational readiness.
* Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and empower the Production team, Process Engineering Technicians and Flow Engineers to provide effective manufacturing support, maintain production continuity, and resolve process and workflow issues
* Budgetary Responsibility: Own the fab operating budget, including labor, materials, maintenance, and operational spending; drive cost-reduction initiatives and evaluate capital investments using ROI-based decision-making.
* Wafer Planning and Customer Delivery: Partner with Wafer Planning and Program Management to align schedules, capacity, and customer priorities; identify delivery risks and oversee recovery plans to maintain on time delivery (OTD) performance.
* Manufacturing Performance: Partner with Industrial Engineers, and drive continuous improvement in throughput, cycle time, WIP management, yield, quality, equipment availability, and manufacturing cost using data-driven decision-making and structured problem-solving.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development to resolve production constraints, improve equipment readiness, and maintain stable manufacturing operations.
* Operational Excellence: Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), including customer OTD, cycle time, throughput, equipment availability, and quality. Promote standardization, disciplined execution, effective escalation, and continuous improvement.
* Talent Development: Build a high-performing organization through coaching, accountability, collaboration, and development of technical and operational talent. Responsible for the organizational design and talent strategy of these teams, with a focus on cultivating and retaining key talent, developing future leaders and preparing current leaders for the next level role.

**Required Qualifications:** 

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or related technical discipline.
* Experience: Minimum 12 years in semiconductor manufacturing or operations; minimum 5+ years leading fab operations in a senior manager or director capacity within a 24/7 manufacturing environment.
* Skills:
* Demonstrated ability to improve manufacturing performance (throughput, cycle time, yield, cost, and customer delivery).
* Expertise in wafer planning, WIP management, or production scheduling.
* Strong capability in statistical process control (SPC), structured problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making.
* Demonstrated leadership with large technical teams, with an ability to communicate and collaborate cross-functionally, delivering results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Proven track record of managing a 24/7 manufacturing organization and guiding cross-functional teams through technical tool or yield crises.
* Citizenship: US Citizen required.

**Physical Requirements:** 

* Ability to enter the cleanroom in full PPE to provide technical and operational support.
* Ability to navigate multi-level fab environments, including prolonged walking and standing when needed.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.
 
 
**Preferred Qualifications:** 

* Education: Master’s or PhD in a relevant technical discipline.
* Experience: Deep knowledge of advanced Complimentary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) nodes, fab toolsets (Lithography, Etch, Diffusion, Thin Films, Chemical Mechanical Polish, Metrology, Metals), and factory automation systems.
* Skills: Experience driving major manufacturing transformations, automation or digitization initiatives, or large-scale capacity improvements.

The annual salary range for this role is $159440 - $239,160. Pay offered is based on many factors, including, but not limited to, the job-related experience, skills, education, and credentials of each candidate.
 
 
SkyWater offers an exciting environment where the brightest semiconductor minds come together to achieve exceptional results. We offer competitive salary and an opportunity to participate in incentive plans as well as other employee financial benefits, including 401k match, and life insurance.
 
Additionally, SkyWater offers a comprehensive benefits package which promotes a healthy life. This includes benefit eligibility day one, medical, dental, mental health benefits, vision, legal planning, short- and long-term disability, paid time off, paid holidays, an on-site fitness facility, and an on-site self-serve market.
 
SkyWater complies with federal and state disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities unless doing so would cause an undue hardship. Alternative methods of applying for employment are available to individuals unable to submit an application through this site because of a disability. To request reasonable accommodations, to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact Human Resources at 952-851-5200 or Recruiting@SkyWatertechnology.com.
 
EOE, including disability/vets
 
We will never ask applicants to pay fees, purchase equipment or gift cards, or provide financial information before a formal offer of employment has been accepted. If you receive a suspicious communication claiming to represent our company, please verify its authenticity by contacting our recruitment team at recruiting@skywatertechnology.com before responding.

records.title: Director of Operations - Proliant Dairy Ingredients - Ankeny, Iowa
records.description:
Proliant Dairy Ingredients is committed to providing the best dairy ingredient options for enhancing the value and effectiveness of our partners’ products. We are formulating success by living our values of Continuous Improvement, Teamwork, Quality, and Leadership. 
 
The Director of Operations provides strategic leadership and oversight of the company’s manufacturing operations, quality, and process engineering functions, ensuring alignment with business objectives and supporting overall organizational performance and growth. As a member of the PDI leadership team, this position works closely with the CEO and senior leadership to drive business growth, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

**JOB QUALIFICATIONS:**
-----------------------

Education:

* Bachelor’s degree required.
* BS or MBA in operations management, engineering, or dairy and/or food science preferred.

 

Experience:

* Demonstrated leadership ability with strong interpersonal skills and a proven ability to build, develop, and motivate high-performing teams.
* Minimum eight years of experience required, with at least five years of production/operations management experience.
* Experience within dairy industry or food processing highly preferred.

**JOB DUTIES:**
---------------

* Lead the development and implementation of operational strategies, policies, and processes to drive efficiency and organizational effectiveness within manufacturing operations.
* Lead and oversee all aspects of employee management for the operations, quality, and process engineering departments, including recruiting, hiring, training, work assignment, performance management, employee development, recognition, and discipline. Foster a culture of teamwork, accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement.
* Evaluate market opportunities and develop recommendations to drive business development and company growth.
* Support raw material sourcing strategies, assist in securing reliable supply commitments, and maintain strong supplier relationships to ensure supply continuity and alignment with business objectives.
* Oversee workplace safety across all PDI U.S. production facilities, ensuring safe working conditions are maintained, and appropriate corrective actions are implemented when necessary.
* Responsible for overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of U.S. production facilities. Keep up to date on dairy processes and techniques.
* Interact, visit, and communicate with various vendors regarding necessary changes to improve operations at all plants.
* Identify areas for improvement in the plants, determine courses of action, and implement improvements and corrective actions in these areas.
* Develop plans for supply and efficient use of materials, machines, and employees.
* Review production costs and product quality, maximize yields, modify production and inventory control programs to maintain and enhance profitable operation of all U.S. Operations.
* Research and assess the viability of new technologies to improve operations.
* Participate in strategic planning process by reviewing PDI operations and recommend budgets for both raw material and capital expenditures.
* Submit necessary requests for capital investment in accordance with established budgets, process, and return-on-investment requirements; present capital investment projects to President & CEO and as necessary to the PDI leadership team.
* Ensures fundamental food safety and quality practices are maintained to achieve food safety and quality objectives and supports ongoing improvements of food safety programs.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**
---------------------

* Knowledge of manufacturing, engineering, and operations principles and ability to apply those principles to production management function.
* Ability to effectively communicate and work with management and across multiple departments, as well as with customers and other business contacts.
* Ability to maintain and manage corporate confidential information as well as confidential customer information.
* Knowledge of organizational methods and the ability to manage multiple tasks/projects simultaneously.
* Ability to assist with special or ongoing projects as instructed by senior management.
* Ability to read, analyze, and interpret professional journals, technical procedures, or government guidelines.
* Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from internal individuals/groups, suppliers, customers, and the public.
* Ability to analyze data and utilize to drive optimization and problem solving.
* Strong leadership ability in creating a team environment.
* Ability to think strategically and at the same time solve practical problems across a variety of situations.
* Ability to travel as needed to meet job duties (approximately 50%).

**BASIC PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:**
--------------------------------

Approximate: 8 - Hour Day (may be longer, dependent on business needs)

**Key:**

Occasional = 0% to 33%

Frequent = 34% to 66%

Continuous = 67% to 100%

**Hand Movements:**

Recording Data - Occasional

Rough Terrain - Occasional

Other - N/A

**BASIC MENTAL REQUIREMENTS:**
------------------------------

This position requires the mental capabilities to apply technical knowledge surrounding the production and operation of manufacturing plants. Furthermore, the incumbent must assimilate and disseminate operational information, develop plans, and forecast future supply and production trends.

**WORKING CONDITIONS AND EXPOSURES:**
-------------------------------------

Position located in Iowa. Occasional travel (international and domestic) to include spending time in two production plants and laboratory locations (Michigan and Minnesota) and headquarters in Iowa.

**COMPREHENSIVE BENEFITS:**

* A choice of three quality affordable healthcare coverage options
* Vision coverage
* Dental coverage
* Health savings account with employer contribution/flexible spending accounts
* 401(k) retirement plan
* Paid time off starting at 3 week/annual and 9 paid holidays

*All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation due to a disability at any stage of the employment application process should contact human resources (515)-289-5161.*

records.title: Senior Director, Merchandise Manufacturing & Sourcing
records.description:
**Job Description:**
====================

NOTE: This role is based in New York City and encourages a minimum of two days per week in the SoHo office. Some roles or teams may require additional in-office attendance if the essential functions of the role require it.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Senior Director, Merchandise Manufacturing & Strategic Sourcing is a key global leadership role responsible for the strategic sourcing, manufacturing, commercialization, and production execution of Scholastic's merchandise portfolio supporting Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade Publishing, Discovery Fairs, and future consumer product initiatives.

Reporting directly to the SVP Manufacturing who is responsible for Global Supply Chain and Procurement, this position serves as the critical bridge between Product Development, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Publishing, and global manufacturing partners.

This leader partners with internal stakeholders from the earliest stages of product ideation, providing expertise in product engineering, sourcing strategy, manufacturing capabilities, material selection, cost optimization, and production feasibility. The objective is to transform creative concepts into high-quality, innovative products that deliver exceptional customer experiences while achieving aggressive cost, quality, and speed-to-market objectives.

The role oversees a global sourcing portfolio exceeding $200 million annually and leads an international team of approximately 12 professionals located across the United States and India. The position may be based in the United States, China, or India and requires extensive collaboration with domestic and international suppliers and manufacturing partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES

**Product Development, Ideation & Publishing Partnership**

* Serve as a strategic partner to Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade, and other stakeholders to translate creative concepts and intellectual property into compelling, manufacturable products.
* Engage early in product ideation, bringing manufacturing and sourcing expertise to decisions around materials, formats, construction, packaging, features, price points, and production methods.
* Proactively introduce new product concepts, materials, manufacturing capabilities, and supplier innovations that expand Scholastic's product opportunities.
* Partner throughout the development cycle from concept, specification, prototyping, sampling, and costing through pproval and production.
* Challenge and improve concepts where appropriate to enhance consumer appeal, quality, manufacturability, sustainability, speed, and cost.

**Consumer Products & Sourcing Strategy**

* Lead development of the sourcing and manufacturing strategy supporting Scholastic's expanding consumer-products and merchandise initiatives.
* Partner with business and publishing leadership to identify new product categories and opportunities across Book Fairs, Discovery Fairs, retail, e-commerce, licensing, and other emerging channels.
* Develop category sourcing strategies addressing manufacturing regions, supplier capabilities, cost, lead times, minimum quantities, tooling, quality, and supply-chain risk.
* Build a proactive pipeline of product ideas and manufacturing capabilities that can be regularly presented to internal stakeholders.
* Maintain awareness of consumer trends, emerging categories, materials, and manufacturing technologies and translate those insights into actionable product opportunities.

**Global Vendor Development & Innovation**

* Proactively identify and develop innovative manufacturers and product-development partners, particularly those offering engineering expertise, rapid prototyping, unique materials, creative capabilities, and new manufacturing technologies.
* Develop suppliers that can function as extensions of Scholastic's product-development organization, proactively bringing forward new concepts and capabilities.
* Continuously evaluate the supplier portfolio to improve competitiveness, increase speed, diversify supply, reduce risk, and enable entry into new categories.

**Global Sourcing, Cost & Operational Leadership**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive global sourcing strategy supporting more than $200 million in annual product expense.
* Establish sourcing roadmaps and supplier-diversification strategies that anticipate future business requirements and reduce dependency on individual suppliers or regions.
* Ensure products consistently meet expectations for quality, safety, regulatory compliance, sustainability, cost, and on-time delivery.

**Supplier Engagement & Global Travel**

* Maintain direct senior-level engagement with strategic manufacturing partners and regularly visit supplier facilities to evaluate capabilities, innovation, quality, capacity, and operational performance.
* Significant international travel is expected, with consistent travel to Asia, particularly China and India, as well as other global sourcing markets as required.
* Use supplier visits as product-development and innovation opportunities to identify new materials, manufacturing processes, capabilities, and product concepts for Scholastic.
* Participate in relevant trade shows, sourcing events, and supplier innovation sessions to identify emerging capabilities and potential partners.

**Organizational Leadership**

* Lead and develop a global organization of approximately 12 professionals across the United States and India.
* Build a culture combining sourcing discipline with creativity, product knowledge, commercial thinking, and an entrepreneurial approach to product development.
* Develop team capabilities in product ideation, product development, supplier innovation, value engineering, and strategic sourcing.
* Build strong partnerships across Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Supply Chain, Finance, and senior leadership, positioning the organization as a strategic product-development partner.

**Key Measures of Success**

Success will be measured through product development and innovation, cost per unit and total landed-cost, speed to market, supplier innovation and diversification, quality and compliance, on-time performance.

**About Scholastic**

For more than 100 years, Scholastic Corporation (NASDAQ: SCHL) has been meeting children where they are – at school, at home and in their communities – by creating quality content and experiences, all beginning with literacy. Scholastic delivers stories, characters, and learning moments that empower all kids to become lifelong readers and learners through bestselling children’s books, literacy- and knowledge-building resources for schools including classroom magazines, and award-winning, entertaining children's media. As the world's largest publisher and distributor of children's books through school-based book clubs and book fairs, classroom libraries, school and public libraries, retail, and online, and with a global reach into more than 135 countries, Scholastic encourages the personal and intellectual growth of all children, while nurturing a lifelong relationship with reading, themselves, and the world around them. Learn more at www.scholastic.com.

Some benefits that we offer:

 

* Full suite of health and wellness benefits (including a $0 deductible Medical Plan)
* Retirement Savings Plan 401(k) with options for both Roth and Traditional Contributions
* Tuition-Free programs for undergraduate and graduate degrees
* Generous Parental Leave Program
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with opportunity for discounted stock at a 15% discount

Thank you for your consideration in choosing Scholastic.

HOW YOU CAN FIT **(Qualifications)**

A minimum of 10 years of experience as a valued member of a non-book/novelty/ merchandise development team. Proven track record working at a well established company representing a diverse product catalog consisting of products attractive to consumer interest and educationaly directed.

Comfort in travel globally and managing teams remotely and developing deep relationships with vendors in China and India along with others Asian regions.

Direct book experience and knowledge of the book publishing cycles and development timelines.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
Location:

Garden City, NY, US, 11530

Business Unit: Treitler FMH

Posting Date: Nov 20, 2026

Job Description:

**Position Summary:**

The Director of Operations is responsible for leading Hughes-Treitler operations to achieve business objectives related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and customer satisfaction. This hands-on leadership role provides strategic and day-to-day direction for manufacturing, materials, and operational excellence while ensuring the organization has the talent, capacity, processes, and resources required to support current demand and business growth. The Director establishes operating plans, drives accountability, builds organizational capability, and leads continuous improvement initiatives that improve performance, expand capacity, control costs, and strengthen customer responsiveness.

 
 

**Supervisory Responsibilties:**

The position has direct reports but must be able to work in partnership with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Production in support of the departmental objectives. 



**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Lead and develop Operations teams to effectively support day-to-day execution, strategic business objectives, customer requirements, and growth plans.
* Establish operating strategies, objectives, budgets, capital requirements, material plans, labor requirements, and organizational priorities aligned with customer and business needs.
* Ensure the organization is structured and staffed with the talent, resources, and capabilities needed to meet customer quality, technical, delivery, and turnaround-time expectations.
* Partner with business leadership to achieve key performance indicators, including safety, quality, on-time delivery, throughput, backlog reduction, customer lead time, productivity, labor utilization, cost, and profitability.
* Lead the development and execution of the site Lean and Operational Excellence roadmap, using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, TPM, SIOP and daily management practices to improve flow, yield, cycle time, productivity, and cost performance.
* Establish and monitor operating standards, performance metrics, and management routines that drive accountability, timely problem-solving, and sustained results.
* Drive capacity planning and expansion initiatives, including capital equipment, automation, facility, tooling, staffing, and process investments required to support business growth.
* Manage operating expenses and capital investments in accordance with approved budgets; identify and execute cost-reduction and productivity opportunities.
* Ensure effective planning and control of materials, inventory, suppliers, production schedules, and labor resources to support quality, cost, and delivery commitments.
* Collaborate with Quality, Engineering, Sales, Finance, and other cross-functional partners to resolve operational issues, support new product introductions, strengthen manufacturability, and meet customer requirements.
* Provide leadership for robust root cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, and customer performance.
* Participate in the development and execution of the business strategy and translate strategic priorities into actionable operating plans and measurable objectives.
* Support commercial and customer-facing activities, including operational reviews, pricing and capacity analyses, customer visits, and performance presentations.
* Recruit, develop, coach, and retain operations talent through performance management, career development, succession planning, cross-training, and ongoing capability building.
* Foster a culture of accountability, employee engagement, collaboration, innovation, safety, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* Author annual performance reviews and develop continuing education and advancement paths for entire department.
* Demonstrate the ability and willingness to use AI tools appropriately to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and cost performance, including identifying suitable use cases and critically evaluating AI-generated outputs.
 

**Required Skills and Abilities:**

* Strong leadership, project management, analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations and continuous improvement initiatives in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Proficiency with Lean, Six Sigma, 5S, Kaizen, TPM, and other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Ability to establish performance metrics, analyze operating data, prioritize competing demands, and drive accountability for results.
* Proven ability to lead change, manage multiple complex initiatives, and meet critical deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Exceptional interpersonal, written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to build effective work relationships.
* Strong customer orientation and demonstrated ability to balance customer requirements with operational, financial, and organizational priorities.
* Ability to work effectively under pressure, exercise sound judgment, and maintain a hands-on leadership presence across the operation.
* Proficiency with enterprise resource planning and manufacturing systems; experience with SIOP or related planning processes preferred.
* Demonstrated history of successful change management and implementation of operational excellence improvements.
* Strong interpersonal, leadership and organizational skills and the ability to communicate with all levels of the organization from the production floor to the executive office.
* Willingness to work a flexible schedule and travel as needed to support business requirements.
 

**Education and Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or another related technical discipline required; MBA or other relevant advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing operations leadership experience in a low-volume/high-mix, build-to-order, or engineered-products environment; experience in aerospace, defense, metal-forming, precision machining, brazing, welding, or another highly regulated industry preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading salaried and hourly employees.
* Demonstrated experience leading Lean Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, and continuous improvement programs with measurable results.
* Demonstrated experience driving operational planning, capital and capacity expansion, production and materials management, cost optimization, organizational improvements, and customer-facing operational reviews.

**Other**

* Due to the nature of Hughes-Treitler's programs and products, applicants must have the legal right to work in the US and additionally must be legally authorized to access export-controlled information and source code.

**Physical Requirements:**

* None

**Compensation**
----------------

Employee Type: Salaried

Currency: USD

Salary Minimum: 200,000

Salary Maximum: 225,000

Incentive: No

Disclaimer: Where a specific pay range is noted, it is a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. The actual salary offered will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, market / business considerations, and geographic location.

For more information on AMETEK's competitive benefits, please click here.

AMETEK, Inc. is a leading global provider of industrial technology solutions serving a diverse set of attractive niche markets with annual sales over $7.5 billion.

AMETEK is committed to making a safer, sustainable, and more productive world a reality. We use differentiated technology solutions to solve our customers’ most complex challenges. We employ 22,000 colleagues, in 35 countries, that are grounded by our core values: Ethics and Integrity, Respect for the Individual, Inclusion, Teamwork, and Social Responsibility. AMETEK is a component of the S&P 500. Visit https://www.ametek.com/careers for more information.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class. Individuals who need a reasonable accommodation because of a disability for any part of the employment process should call 1 (866) 263-8359.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
Description:

**Join Weiss-Aug – A Leader in Precision Manufacturing and Innovation**

Be part of a company that’s shaping the future of manufacturing where your ideas, skills, and passion matter.

Weiss-Aug, is a leading provider of advanced manufacturing and engineering solutions with advanced facilities across the U.S. and Mexico for over 50 years.

**Why Join Us?**

At Weiss-Aug we are driven by a commitment to excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement. As a recognized leader in the industrial and commercial sectors, specializing in high-volume metal stamping, thermoplastic molding, and value-added assembly solutions for the medical, aerospace & defense, automotive, interconnect, telecommunications and consumer goods industries, we take pride in cultivating a collaborative and forward-thinking work environment.

We're currently seeking a passionate and skilled ***Director of Operations*** to join our team and contribute to our mission of delivering high-quality, engineered solutions to our customers worldwide. In this role you will be responsible for planning and directing line management and related manufacturing support activities including manufacturing floor inspection, manufacturing engineering, materials management and safety/environmental engineering. Establishes and implements manufacturing policies, controls and procedures to further the company's interest in efficiently producing quality products. Contributes to achievement of sales objectives and to the establishment. Prepares or assists in the annual budgets for all departments and is responsible for profit and loss of the division. Manages Manufacturing Managers of Molding and Stamping, Purchasing, Warehouse, Manufacturing Engineering, Customer Service/Planning.

**Responsibilities**

* Management of manufacturing operations. Plans, schedules, organizes, and staffs manufacturing and manufacturing support functions. Assures that all groups within manufacturing organization are properly staffed and coordinated; and that personnel in each group are properly qualified, directed and trained to perform their duties effectively.
* Interprets company sales forecasts and shop orders and establishes accurate manufacturing plans to assure that our customers' requirements are met, that is, defect free product on time.
* Coordinates with Engineering, Sales and new product development engineering to maintain an awareness of current and future product plans.
* Develops and manages material control, manufacturing control, production scheduling, and planning systems to assure achievement of output schedules which will meet company sales requirements.
* Maintains material and parts inventories which are adequate to ensure the fulfillment of production schedules with minimum inventory expense.
* Plans and develops manufacturing facilities and equipment for efficient production of products.
* Works with tooling/engineering to investigate product quality and manufacturing problems and determine the most cost-efficient solutions.
* Develops and assists with the annual budget of all departments; develops and is responsible for all standard costs. Recommends pricing based on the profit objective of the company. Is responsible for the profit and loss of the division.
* Meets or exceeds all TQM measurements as agreed upon annually.
* Is a member of the executive team and steering team which are responsible for the development of company policies and plans.
* Participates with other top managers in the development of company business policies as needed.

Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree Mechanical or Industrial Engineering.
* 8-10 years precision manufacturing experience including some experience in molding. (10 years in management role).
* Strong leadership skills.
* Should have a working knowledge of computerized manufacturing systems.

This position is at our ***East Hanover, NJ*** location.

Pay Range: $150,000 - $180,000

**Other Benefits Include**

* Medical, Dental and Vision
* 401 (k) with company match
* Holiday, Vacation and Sick Time
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Health Savings Accounts (HSA)
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Cigna Wellness Incentive Program
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Short Term Disability
* Group Life and Accidental Insurance
* Sun Life – Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance
* Smoking Cessation Program
* Pet Insurance

**US Pay Transparency**

The base salary for this role will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, experience, and internal consistency.

If your salary requirements exceed the advertised range and you remain interested in Weiss-Aug, we encourage you to apply.

Weiss-Aug is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. Applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristics protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

records.title: Director, Quality GxP Vendor Management & Audit Programs
records.description:
Description:

**The Company:**

This publicly held clinical-stage biotechnology company is focused on developing treatments for patients suffering from complex rare diseases using its novel cell penetrating peptide technology platform. Their lead product candidate, nomlabofusp, is a subcutaneously administered, recombinant fusion protein intended to deliver human frataxin (FXN), an essential protein to the mitochondria of patients with Friedreich’s ataxia. Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare, progressive, and fatal disease in which patients are unable to produce sufficient FXN due to a genetic abnormality.

The company has 80 employees and has assembled an experienced management team, each of whom has over 20 years of pharmaceutical industry experience. The management team, employees, and consultants have significant expertise in discovery, nonclinical and clinical development, regulatory affairs, commercialization, and the development of manufacturing processes utilizing good manufacturing practices (GMPs).

The company’s strategy is to become a leader in the treatment of rare diseases by leveraging their technology platform and applying their team’s know-how and expertise to the development of CTI-1601 and other future pipeline programs. They are best characterized by entrepreneurial and scientific leadership and a participatory workforce committed to success.

**Position Summary:**

The Director, GxP Vendor Management is responsible for leading Larimar’s GxP vendor management and audit programs and collaborating with key functional area stakeholders to ensure vendors are selected, qualified, managed and overseen in compliance with Larimar and regulatory requirements. This role owns the full vendor lifecycle and will shape the program’s strategy as Larimar seeks BLA approval, progresses with Phase 3 trial and plans for commercialization.

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead and implement the strategic direction of the vendor management and audit programs at Larimar.
* Own the risk-based vendor qualification framework, including risk tiering and minimum oversight expectations for each tier, and manage day-to-day qualification activities through vendor audit and assessment, qualification, approval and filing of vendor-related qualification documentation.
* Maintain an approved vendor list and a master tracker of all GxP vendors (current, historic, and planned) as the single source of truth for vendor qualification/requalification, audit, and Quality Agreements.
* Partner with functional areas to develop and oversee execution of the risk-based annual external audit plan, including auditor assignments, audit tracking, follow up of audit responses and CAPAs, and filing of audit documentation.
* Manage the internal audit program including development and execution of internal audit plan to adequately assess Larimar’s internal processes.
* Manage the Quality Agreement program, including development and maintenance of Quality Agreements, and partner with Legal and functional areas to ensure Quality Agreements are in place and current with applicable vendors.
* Partner with functional areas to develop, review and maintain risk-based vendor oversight plans, including expectations for KPIs; governance meetings; issue escalation; oversight activities, frequency, responsibility, and documentation requirements; and verification that vendors and their subcontractors use qualified personnel.
* Conduct training on vendor management and audit programs to ensure functional areas understand and appropriately execute their responsibilities.
* Partner with functional areas to identify vendor deviations to assess issues potentially impacting the vendor qualification status or required oversight.
* Develop Vendor Management metrics, analyze vendor performance and compliance trends, and lead a periodic cross-functional vendor review that feeds into Quality Management Review.
* Ensure inspection readiness in the vendor management function and assist functional areas with readiness related to selection, qualification, management and oversight of their vendors.
* Evaluate and implement electronic vendor management systems, as applicable.

Requirements:

**Qualifications:**

* BS/BA in a life science or related field, or equivalent industry experience.
* 10+ years’ experience in the Pharmaceutical/Biotechnology industry, including at least 5 years leading vendor management/audit programs in a GxP environment.
* Expert knowledge of FDA, EMA, MHRA and ICH GxP regulations and guidelines, including ICH E6(R3) expectations for sponsor oversight of service providers.
* Strong GxP foundation associated with vendor oversight.
* Demonstrated experience planning and managing GxP vendor and internal audits, including follow up of audit responses and CAPAs.
* Experience developing and negotiating Quality Agreements with CROs, laboratories and other GxP service providers.
* Proficient with Veeva Systems, including Veeva Vault QualityDocs, desirable.
* Experience applying risk-based approaches to vendor tiering and oversight.
* Strong communication skills with all levels of the organization and external vendors, and the ability to influence functional areas without direct authority.
* Excellent organizational skills, analytical and problem-solving abilities, and strong verbal and writing skills.

**Benefits:**

Larimar Therapeutics offers all employees incentive stock options, a comprehensive benefits plan including 401K, and a flexible PTO policy.

***Equal Opportunity Employment***

*We are committed to equal-employment principles, and we recognize the value of committed employees who feel they are being treated in an equitable and professional manner. We strive to find ways to attract, develop and retain the talent needed to meet business objectives, and to recruit and employ highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities in which we live.*

*Employment policies and decisions on employment and promotion are based on merit, qualifications, performance, and business needs. The decisions and criteria governing the employment relationship with all employees are made in a non-discriminatory manner—without regard to age, race, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical condition related to pregnancy or childbirth), gender identity or expression, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, legally protected genetic information, marital status, veteran status, military status, sexual orientation, or any other factor determined to be an unlawful basis for such decisions by federal, state, or local statutes.*
