records.title: Sr. Manager, Quality
records.description:
At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it reality.

 

For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.

At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.

 

We are looking for a S **r. Manager, Quality** to join our team in one of today’s most exciting technologies. This role will report to **Director of Quality** and based in **Newark, Delaware. This is a fully on-site, in office role 5 days a week** .

 

**Role and Responsibilities:**

* Ensure 100% Quality assurance at the Skid line manufacturing through inspection, testing, and sub-component testing/inspection. Assist in hiring personnel needed to support this effort.

* Partner with Install Quality team (field) to understand real time (daily) what items are escaping the plant and instituting immediate mitigation plans including addressing any inventory in the pipeline not yet installed.

* Implement permanent corrective actions working with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply chain, or SQE as per relevance on each issue.

* Provide quality input into the new equipment being purchased for the scaling of Delaware manufacturing. Include inputs for quality assurance into equipment design, and verification of process steps. Understand and provide input into the planned operation, what can be bypassed, maintenance plans, calibration or drift of the equipment, automation that can fail and be undetected leading to quality escapes.

* Participate and understand results from testing in the plant; Functional test, Tommy test, FIT, etc. Drive pareto of failures to help cross functional problem solving of test failures.

* Implement a 100% functional test (new) on skid final product assembly; electrical continuity, communications integrity, piping assurance, start up simulation, etc. to assure 100% QA prior to shipping to customer.

* Ensure skid components and systems have latest FW revision prior to shipping to the W/H, or out of W/H to field.

* Work with CIG and Manufacturing Engr, and NPI to implement workload being removed from the customer install side and being moved into skid assembly. Provide oversight to ensure best quality achievement; ensure work instructions are clear, operators trained, workstations have proper tools, and judgement criteria.

* Collaborate with Supplier Quality / Suppliers to achieve zero-defect flow (“dock-to-stock”) for all purchased, contract manufacture parts, materials, and Bloom Energy manufactured parts.

* Drive component and design failures back to the earliest point of detection in the process.

* Ensure manufacturing process have Control plans with CTQ, and POA built in to each station.

* Work collaboratively with Design teams to DFM, through a “registration system”, and Pokeyoke assembly methods for highest quality assurance.

* Drive test excellence in the manufacturing plan to ensure that equipment and test stations are certified with robust qualification programs, that are documented and controlled for changes with proper accuracy and gage R&R techniques.

* Drive yield task forces to achieve company wide targets at each manufacturing point under this scope, with cross functional teams driving top pareto issues to RCCA.

* Ensure early engagement with the product engineering team to teach and perform early stage risk assessments (DFMEA et.al.)

* Design for manufacturability and reliability improvements during the early design stages of product development.

* Work with Engineering NPI and the manufacturing engineering teams to perform PFMEA, write work instructions, and establish quality check-points to guarantee zero-defect quality in production.

* Develop and implement formal, comprehensive process documentation including process flow diagrams, Process FMEAs, process control plans, operations method Sheets, manufacturing quality charts (MQCs) and etc.

* Lead critical problem solving task forces with emphasis on cross functional inputs, accountability, time to RCCA, and ensurance of mitigation of inventory, or field units at risk.

* Troubleshoot product issues by reviewing engineering drawings and design requirements. Drive a rigorous resolution process for product quality, reliability and design issues.

* Perform data-driven root cause failure analyses for design, manufacturing, and administrative problems.

* Perform process audits to monitor, continuously improve, and sustain superior product quality.

* Demonstrate the ability to interface and work collaboratively across departments internally and with suppliers and customers, (including Purchasing, Quality, R&D, Manufacturing, Product Engineering, Marketing and Finance), while building strong and cooperative working relationships.

* Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) Reduction: Establish and govern site COPQ metrics (scrap, rework, sorting, and warranty risk); lead cross-functional yield-improvement blitzes targeting measurable cost reductions and scrap minimization.

* Process Capability & Zero-Defect Mentality: Drive process capability (C\_p / C\_{pk} \ge 1.33) across critical-to-quality (CTQ) operations (welding, brazing, ceramic stack assembly, plumbing/gas-delivery, and electrical integration).

 

**Skills and Experience:**

* More than 10 years of increasing responsibility in the areas of Quality, and Manufacturing .

* Experience implementing company-wide ISO 9001 procedures and TS16949 standards and related process documentation. Possess working knowledge of process capability and control requirements, methods and systems.

* Demonstrated track record of building, restructuring, or significantly scaling a manufacturing quality team during rapid production ramp-up

* Proven successful application of multi-discipline engineering problem solving techniques.

* Understand the critical elements of modern Manufacturing Statistical Process Control, (e.g., practical working knowledge and experience with SPC, Process Capability, Cp, Cpk, etc.)

* Understand the critical elements of modern Reliability Engineering, (e.g., MCF, MTBF, MTT, etc.)

* Certification in a recognized problem-solving methodology such as six-sigma Black Belt, 8D, or Global Problem Solving.

* Strong verbal/active listening/written communications.

* Demonstrate planning and leadership skills.

* Expert with metrology, calibration, and Gage R & R’s.

records.title: Director of Practice and ASC Operations
records.description:
**Director of Practice and ASC Operations**

Reporting to: Chief Operating Officer

**About the Role**

Lead the day-to-day business operations of a multi-provider pain management practice and ambulatory surgery center (ASC). Your initial priorities will be to make it easier for patients and referring offices to reach us, convert more referrals into scheduled visits, and make better use of clinic and procedure capacity.

**A core part of the role is using data, technology, and automation to improve how the practice and ASC operate as they grow.** You’ll use call, referral, and scheduling data to see where patients get stuck and where capacity goes unused. You’ll then redesign workflows, improve how teams use existing systems, and automate repetitive steps such as routing callbacks or flagging referrals that need follow-up. You’ll measure whether those changes improve access, reduce manual work, and free up staff time.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll lead staff, set clear expectations, and work directly with physicians and the ASC Director of Nursing to improve how the practice and surgery center operate. We welcome leaders from healthcare and other complex service businesses. You’ll bring experience leading a team, using data to identify problems, and carrying changes through to measurable results.

**What You Bring**

**Required**

* Progressive operations leadership experience with direct responsibility for hiring, coaching, developing, and managing the performance of a team.
* Experience running a complex, customer-facing operation and managing the drivers of financial performance, such as labor, capacity, productivity, and operating expenses.
* A track record of personally leading workflow improvements that produced measurable, sustained results in access, service, efficiency, or cost.
* Experience using data and KPIs to identify bottlenecks, prioritize action, and verify that changes improved performance.
* Experience using technology or automation to simplify workflows, reduce manual work, and help staff adopt new ways of working.
* Ability to lead changes that span teams, take ownership when progress stalls, and work hands-on with frontline staff to resolve problems.
* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

**What success looks like**

* **Better patient access.** Make it easier for patients to connect with us and stay engaged throughout their care. Answer more calls live, return messages promptly, and offer convenient online scheduling for eligible visits. Use technology alongside personal outreach to keep patients informed, respond to their needs, and support them throughout their care.
* **Growth and capacity.** Grow completed visits and procedures by strengthening relationships with referring providers, making it easy to refer patients, and keeping referring offices informed. Convert more referrals into completed visits and procedures through timely scheduling, better use of clinic and ASC capacity, and fewer avoidable cancellations.
* **Stronger financial performance.** Labor and supply costs managed to budget, with timely resolution of operational issues affecting collections.
* **Less manual work and clearer accountability.** Use technology and automation to simplify workflows. Set clear ownership for follow-up and use data to track whether changes improve performance and hold over time.

**Preferred**

* Experience in physician practice management, ambulatory surgery, or another regulated service environment.
* Experience coordinating operations across locations or across teams with distinct professional responsibilities.

**Candidates from outside healthcare are encouraged to apply.** Leadership experience and a record of improving operations are essential. Physician practice management experience is optional.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

records.title: Director, Central Laboratory Operations
records.description:
By clicking the “Apply” button, I understand that my employment application process with Takeda will commence and that the information I provide in my application will be processed in line with Takeda’s Privacy Notice and Terms of Use. I further attest that all information I submit in my employment application is true to the best of my knowledge.

**Job Description**
-------------------

OBJECTIVES/PURPOSE

 

* Builds and leads Takeda’s new Central Laboratory Operations group, defining the vision, operating model, organizational design, capabilities, and ways of working required to deliver enterprise technical and operational oversight of central laboratory services across global clinical development programs.
* Establishes the foundational infrastructure for central laboratory oversight, including processes, vendor strategy, systems, and metrics, so that central laboratory solutions are technically sound, operationally executable, globally compliant, and inspection-ready from study design through database lock and study closeout.
* Provides leadership of the Sample Management group, ensuring its in-trial activities interface effectively with central laboratory operations. Biorepository and biobank activities are out of scope for this role.
* Partners with Clinical Science, Clinical Operations, Translational Medicine, Translational Biomarkers and Bioanalytics, Data Management, Biometrics, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Procurement, and external laboratory providers to deliver consistent, scalable central laboratory capabilities across the portfolio.

ACCOUNTABILITIES

 

**Building the Central Laboratory Operations Group (primary focus)**

* Define and execute the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap to stand up the Central Laboratory Operations group, including mission, scope, service model, phased capability build, and measures of success.
* Design the organizational structure, roles, and resourcing plan; recruit, onboard, develop, and lead a high-performing team of central laboratory technical and operational experts.
* Establish the central laboratory operating model and oversight framework, including standards, decision rights (RACI), governance forums, escalation pathways, and interfaces with Clinical Operations, Translational Medicine, Translational Biomarkers and Bioanalytics, Data Management, Biometrics, Quality, and Procurement.
* Develop the foundational processes, SOPs, work instructions, templates, and training needed to standardize central laboratory startup, conduct, and closeout across studies, and transition existing study-level central laboratory activities into the new group without disruption to ongoing studies.
* Develop the business case, budget, and resource forecasts for the group, and secure leadership alignment and sponsorship for the phased build-out.
* Lead the central laboratory vendor strategy, including evaluation, selection, and qualification of central laboratories and will consult in evaluation and selection of specialty laboratories as appropriate, technical capability assessments, quality and compliance reviews, contracting input with Procurement, service-level expectations, KPIs, issue escalation, and ongoing vendor governance.
* Provide technical oversight during clinical development planning and protocol design by assessing laboratory feasibility, test menus, specimen requirements, reference ranges, turnaround times, and the operational impact of study endpoints and schedules.
* Establish central laboratory systems and data capabilities, including laboratory information management systems, electronic data capture interfaces, data transfer specifications, edit checks, result reconciliation, traceability, and data readiness for analysis, database lock, and regulatory submission.
* Build quality and regulatory compliance into the group from inception, including ICH-GCP, applicable GCLP principles, CLIA/CAP or equivalent laboratory requirements, data integrity, inspection readiness, audits, deviations, CAPAs, and vendor change controls. Lead IVDR requirements for each protocol.
* Establish portfolio-level central laboratory metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting for quality, timeliness, cost, risk, capacity, data delivery, and vendor performance; use trends and root-cause analysis to drive risk mitigation and sustained improvement.
* Drive modernization through standardized processes, automation, digital integration, data analytics, and emerging laboratory technologies as the group matures.

**Sample Management Group Oversight**

* Provide leadership of the Sample Management group, including setting priorities, allocating resources, approving goals, and supporting talent development; day-to-day sample management execution remains with the Sample Management lead.
* Define the handoffs between central laboratory operations and sample management (e.g., laboratory manuals, collection kits, sample shipment to central laboratories) so roles, responsibilities, and escalation paths are clear.
* Ensure appropriate sample management resourcing and integration at the study level to ensure end-to-end sample mgmt support during study conduct
* Serve as the senior escalation point for sample-related issues that affect central laboratory testing, study timelines, or data quality.

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, COMPETENCIES AND SKILLS

* Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Clinical Laboratory Science, Biomedical Science, Pharmacy, or a related field; advanced

degree such as MS, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent is preferred.

* 10+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, central laboratory, diagnostic laboratory, or other regulated life-

sciences environment, with significant leadership responsibility for global clinical laboratory delivery.

* Proven track record of building a new function, team, or capability from the ground up, including defining strategy, operating

model, organizational design, processes, and governance.

* Demonstrated people leadership experience, including recruiting, developing, and managing teams and overseeing managers in

a matrixed global environment.

* Strong technical knowledge of central and specialty laboratory operations, service models, test menus, analytical platforms,

specimen requirements, reference intervals, laboratory workflow controls, and fit-for-purpose testing within clinical

development.

* Experience selecting, qualifying, contracting with, and governing global central laboratory vendors, including KPI/SLA

management, issue escalation, audits, CAPAs, and continuous improvement.

* Working knowledge of ICH-GCP, applicable GCLP principles, CLIA/CAP or equivalent laboratory standards, IVDR where

applicable, data integrity expectations, and global health authority inspection requirements.

* Strong knowledge of laboratory informatics and clinical technology, including LIMS, laboratory data standards, electronic data

capture interfaces, data transfer specifications, reconciliation, traceability, and data quality controls.

* General familiarity with clinical study sample management sufficient to lead the Sample Management group and manage

interfaces with central laboratory operations.

* Excellent strategic thinking, change leadership, risk management, communication, negotiation, vendor-management, and

executive presentation skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders across functions.

**This position is currently classified as “remote” in accordance with Takeda’s Hybrid and Remote Work policy**

records.description:
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer

Directly Supervises: Executive Operations Coordinator, Administrative Manager, Administrative Assistants, Revenue Cycle Manager, Operations Manager, and other operational employees assigned by the Chief Executive Officer

Schedule: Full-time; 40 hours per week, with scheduling flexibility based on operational needs

Compensation: As stated in the signed offer or compensation agreement

Work Arrangement: Primarily remote, with weekly on-site presence required at Elevation's Homewood and Matteson offices

COMPENSATION AND HOURS

* This is a full-time, salaried-exempt position scheduled for 40 hours per week. The employee will receive the salary stated in the signed offer or compensation agreement and is not eligible for overtime compensation.

* If time reporting is required for attendance, workload, leave, or administrative purposes, the employee must accurately record actual hours worked. Time entries do not change the established salary.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Director of Operations ensures that Elevation Individual & Family Therapy's administrative and operational functions are organized, accountable, compliant, and aligned with client-service and financial goals. The position reduces the CEO's involvement in routine operations by resolving matters within the role's authority, ensuring assigned work is completed, and presenting recommendations when executive approval is required.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

1. OPERATIONAL LEADERSHIP AND STAFF ACCOUNTABILITY

* Set priorities, deadlines, performance expectations, and coverage plans for assigned staff across both locations.

* Conduct regular supervision meetings and monitor attendance, responsiveness, accuracy, productivity, professionalism, and follow-through.

* Review required reports and promptly address missed deadlines, repeated errors, unresolved concerns, and incomplete work.

* Provide training, coaching, written expectations, and documented corrective feedback; coordinate performance improvement or disciplinary processes with the Executive Operations Coordinator and CEO.

* Assign each operational concern to an appropriate owner, monitor it through resolution, and escalate only matters requiring executive, legal, financial, clinical, or regulatory authority.

2. ADMINISTRATIVE AND CLIENT-SERVICE OPERATIONS

* Oversee phone and voicemail coverage, new-client inquiries, intake follow-up, insurance verification, required paperwork, scheduling, check-in, and appointment confirmation.

* Monitor re-engagement, no-show and cancellation outreach, copay collection, approved payment-plan workflows, and records requests.

* Ensure administrative staff consistently follow approved scripts, workflows, response-time standards, documentation requirements, and escalation procedures.

* Oversee office calendars, room assignments, supplies, equipment, routine facility concerns, and administrative coverage.

* Coordinate with clinical leadership when an operational concern affects client care, provider scheduling, documentation, or referrals.

3. REVENUE CYCLE OVERSIGHT

* Directly supervise the Revenue Cycle Manager, establish performance expectations, review results, provide coaching and accountability, and ensure timely follow-through on revenue-cycle priorities.

* Hold the Revenue Cycle Manager accountable for routine billing operations and supervision of assigned billing staff; coordinate cross-department priorities and escalate unresolved financial, payer, staffing, or compliance risks to the CEO.

* Review reports related to claims, denials, payment posting, insurance follow-up, patient balances, accounts receivable, and collections.

* Ensure billing concerns are assigned, documented, and resolved within established timelines.

* Identify administrative or clinical workflow failures that contribute to denials, delayed billing, inaccurate balances, or lost revenue.

* Coordinate communication among RCM, administrative, clinical, and collections staff and escalate material payer, financial, or compliance concerns.

4. POLICIES, SOPS, AND EHR WORKFLOW IMPROVEMENT

* Identify processes requiring a written policy, SOP, checklist, script, workflow, quality check, or escalation procedure.

* Draft and update operational policies and SOPs with the employees and subject-matter experts responsible for the work; coordinate approval by the appropriate leader.

* Maintain version control, review dates, distribution, training, employee acknowledgment, and monitoring of approved procedures.

* Evaluate EHR and technology workflows for intake, scheduling, documentation tracking, billing, records, client communication, and reporting.

* Identify duplicate entry, inconsistent data, preventable delays, and unnecessary manual work; recommend and coordinate approved templates, reports, alerts, tracking tools, automations, and vendor requests.

* Test approved changes, document the revised workflow, coordinate staff training, and monitor implementation while protecting confidentiality and system access.

5. HR, CREDENTIALING, AND COMPLIANCE COORDINATION

Directly supervise the Executive Operations Coordinator by establishing priorities, monitoring deadlines and accuracy, reviewing performance, and ensuring timely completion of assigned HR administration, credentialing, compliance, records, onboarding, offboarding, and policy-related responsibilities. The Executive Operations Coordinator or other assigned personnel retain responsibility for completing the detailed administrative work and maintaining required records.

* Ensure employee performance, attendance, conduct, onboarding, offboarding, training, personnel documentation, and policy-acknowledgment processes are coordinated appropriately and escalated to the CEO when executive authority or protected reporting is required.

* Review credentialing, recredentialing, payer enrollment, licensure, renewal, training, and compliance trackers; ensure assigned staff follow up on incomplete or at-risk items.

* Coordinate provider status changes with HR, billing, clinical leadership, scheduling, and provider-directory workflows.

* Monitor completion of corrective actions and escalate material delays, expirations, privacy concerns, payer or government inquiries, suspected fraud, client-safety issues, or other significant risks immediately.

* Support audits, internal reviews, payer requests, and corrective-action plans without acting as Elevation's attorney or sole clinical compliance authority.

6. BUDGET AND EXPENSE MONITORING

* Assist the CEO with preparing and monitoring approved administrative and operational budgets.

* Review actual operational expenses against approved amounts, including administrative and billing staffing costs, overtime, office supplies, software subscriptions, vendor charges, and upcoming renewals.

* Identify unusual spending, recurring overages, duplicate services, avoidable expenses, and practical opportunities for cost savings.

* Coordinate with billing and collections personnel to identify preventable revenue leakage related to denials, delayed claims, workflow errors, missed collections, or unresolved client balances.

* Maintain organized records of approved operational purchases and recurring expenses and submit purchase or budget-adjustment requests with the cost, purpose, priority, and recommendation.

* Provide the CEO with a monthly summary of significant budget variances, anticipated expenses, and recommended corrective or cost-saving actions.

7. REPORTING AND LEADERSHIP COLLABORATION

* Provide a concise weekly CEO report covering accomplishments, unresolved matters, staff concerns, revenue cycle issues, credentialing/compliance risks, budget concerns, and policy, SOP, or EHR project status.

* Provide a monthly operational summary identifying trends, recurring problems, performance patterns, completed improvements, and recommended priorities.

* Present significant concerns with relevant facts, actions already taken, and a recommended solution rather than forwarding unorganized information.

* Directly supervise the Administrative Manager and Administrative Assistants. Establish priorities, monitor performance, and maintain formal accountability while using the Administrative Manager's workflow knowledge and assigned functional ownership to support training, quality, office operations, and consistent administrative processes.

8. GROWTH INITIATIVES AND PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION

* Lead the operational assessment of CEO-directed growth opportunities, including new services, programs, partnerships, and location expansions. Work with clinical leadership, revenue cycle, and other relevant staff to assess demand, staffing, costs, reimbursement where applicable, space and technology needs, and implementation risks. Clinical leadership guides clinical program design.

* Present the CEO with a recommendation, estimated costs and resources, and a proposed timeline. The CEO decides which opportunities move forward.

* Lead the rollout of approved initiatives. Build the launch plan, assign responsibilities and deadlines, coordinate training and workflow changes, track milestones, and report progress and early results to the CEO.

ROLE BOUNDARIES AND DECISION-MAKING AUTHORITY

The Director of Operations owns operational follow-through but does not personally perform every task within the functions overseen. The position may assign and prioritize routine work, require status updates, provide coaching and corrective feedback, implement approved procedures, coordinate across departments, and resolve routine administrative or client-service concerns within established policies.

CEO approval is required before hiring, termination, suspension, compensation changes, material policy changes, unapproved contracts or purchases, new recurring expenses, significant balance waivers, banking or debt decisions, public statements, or substantive responses to legal, government, payer, or regulatory matters. The Director of Operations monitors and recommends but does not replace bookkeeping, payroll, accounting, or executive financial authority.

SCHEDULE AND CAPACITY

* Periodic on-site presence at both Elevation offices is required to observe day-to-day workflows, the office environment, staff performance, client-service operations, and implementation of policies and procedures. The timing and frequency of visits will be based on operational needs and CEO direction.

* The regular schedule will be established by the CEO and will generally total 40 hours per week. Some evening or weekend work may be necessary based on operational needs. The employee must maintain agreed-upon availability during core business hours for supervision, meetings, and time-sensitive matters.

* Continuous after-hours availability is not expected; after-hours contact should generally be limited to urgent matters that cannot reasonably wait. Occasional schedule fluctuations do not change the position's established salary.

* The Director of Operations must notify the CEO when workload or competing priorities cannot reasonably be completed within the established 40-hour schedule and recommend what should be delegated, postponed, or reprioritized.

* Unless otherwise approved, the role should generally carry no more than two major operational improvement projects at one time. Major launches count toward this limit unless the CEO approves an exception.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* At least three years of relevant operations, healthcare administration, office management, or employee-supervision experience.

* Demonstrated ability to supervise employees, address performance concerns, analyze operational data, and independently move work to completion.

* Strong judgment, initiative, organization, problem-solving, discretion, emotional maturity, and written and verbal communication skills.

* Ability to draft clear policies, SOPs, reports, checklists, and workflows and to protect confidential client, employee, financial, and business information.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Outlook, spreadsheets, cloud-based systems, and the ability to learn and improve EHR and business platforms.

* Working knowledge of HIPAA and healthcare confidentiality expectations; reliable transportation and ability to work from both Elevation locations as required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare administration, management, human resources, or a related field; behavioral health or healthcare operations experience; and experience with revenue cycle, credentialing, compliance, EHR workflow improvement, SOP development, reporting, dashboards, or automations.

records.title: Director Supply Chain Operations
records.description:
**Job Description**
-------------------

**Job Requisition Number** 37994

Summary:

The Operations Director provides strategic and operational leadership for system-wide Supply Chain operations, including logistics, distribution, inventory management, procedural support, supplier services, and Workday ERP initiatives. The role drives standardization, technology-enabled improvement, regulatory compliance, and reliable service across acute, ambulatory, and non-acute settings to support high-quality patient care.

Responsibilities:

1. Lead system-wide Supply Chain operations across logistics, warehousing, distribution, fleet, mailroom, equipment services, and acute, ambulatory, procedural, and non-acute inventory programs.
 
2. Serve as the operational lead for Supply Chain ERP initiatives, including Workday implementation and optimization, requirements analysis, data validation, configuration, enhancement requests, and operational readiness.
 
3. Develop and execute the Supply Chain operations vision, strategic plan, annual operating plan, standards, policies, and procedures in alignment with organizational objectives and best practices.
 
4. Lead and develop the Supply Chain operations team, promoting accountability, engagement, professional development, customer service, and continuous improvement.
 
5. Improve operational and financial performance through metrics, analytics, Lean Six Sigma, process standardization, automation, inventory optimization, labor productivity, cost reduction, and service-level improvement.
 
6. Manage supplier and service-provider performance, including vendor access and credentialing, product backorders and recalls, outsourced services, and improvement initiatives.
 
7. Collaborate with clinical, finance, information services, facilities, executive leadership, and other stakeholders to implement technology and operational solutions that improve visibility, decision-making, and organizational performance.
 
8. Ensure regulatory compliance, ethical operations, risk management, emergency preparedness, business continuity, and product shortage response in accordance with DNV, Joint Commission, CMS, OSHA, and other applicable requirements; perform additional responsibilities as assigned.

Other information:

"1. Healthcare experience and advanced knowledge of logistics, warehousing, distribution, inventory management, procedural supply operations, and operational excellence.
 
2. Demonstrated expertise in ERP systems including implementation, optimization, testing, business process design, and change management.
 
3. Proficiency in Lean Six Sigma methodologies and continuous improvement principles.
 
4. Advanced data analytics capabilities with the ability to interpret operational and financial performance metrics.
 
5. Advanced Excel skills including complex data manipulation, reporting, and analysis.
 
6. Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively across all organizational levels and facilitate cross-functional collaboration.
 
7. Proven expertise in project management, operational transformation, and leading large-scale organizational initiatives.
 
8. Working knowledge of supply chain automation technologies, inventory management systems, business intelligence tools, and healthcare operational best practices."

"Education: Bachelor's degree from a four-year accredited university or college required; master's degree highly preferred.

Certification: CMRP, CSCP, CPIM, Lean Six Sigma Green Belt/Black Belt, RN, or another relevant credential preferred.

Experience: Seven years of progressive supply chain, logistics, distribution, healthcare operations, or related experience required.

Supervisory Experience: Lean Six Sigma, operational excellence, or process improvement leadership experience preferred. Five years of leadership experience overseeing logistics, distribution, inventory management, warehouse operations, procedural supply operations, or related healthcare operational functions required."

Full Time

FTE: 1.000000

 
 

Status: Onsite

records.title: Director Destination Care Operations
records.description:
**Job Summary and Responsibilities**

The Director of Destination Care Operations drives the day-to-day operational success of CommonSpirit Health’s destination care program in partnership with clinical, financial, and internal and external stakeholders – serving patients traveling 150 or more miles for specialty care, from neighboring communities across the United States to international markets. The Director advances program performance, team excellence, and a concierge-caliber patient experience, ensuring every patient experiences frictionless care from first inquiry through return home. This role is suited to a self-driven leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and brings strong team leadership, process improvement skills, and comfort leading teams through change. The ideal candidate leads with adaptability, resourcefulness, and a collaborative spirit, and is deeply committed to delivering an exceptional experience for every destination care patient. This is an in-person, onsite role.

* Oversees the day-to-day operational performance of the destination care program, ensuring consistent and high-quality service delivery across all phases of the patient journey. Oversees referral intake and coordination workflows, ensuring timely and accurate routing, follow-up, and communication with referring providers and patients.
* Ensures patients, families, and referring partners experience seamless, concierge-caliber service from initial contact through post-discharge follow-up; conducts regular patient and family rounding to assess experience, identify service gaps and recovery opportunities, reinforce service standards, and gather patient stories that reflect the destination care experience.
* Delivers and ensures culturally informed service, communication, and care coordination across diverse domestic and international patient populations. Partners with clinical leadership and clinical advisory resources to support patient care operations and ensure the clinical needs of the destination care population are addressed. Identifies and leads process improvement and workflow optimization initiatives to advance operational efficiency, service quality, and patient satisfaction; develops and maintains operational protocols and standards that support consistent program delivery.
* Establishes and maintains documentation standards and data integrity practices across the team to support accurate program reporting, operational decision-making, and continuity of patient care. Serves as the escalation point for the team and provides availability for complex or time-sensitive situations as they arise. Manages the destination care program budget and is accountable for financial performance against established targets.
* Sets clear performance expectations, invests in professional growth, and builds and sustains a high-performing team culture grounded in service excellence, operational consistency, and continuous improvement; establishes clear standards and ensures consistent adherence across the team, addressing performance gaps directly and constructively.
* Oversees onboarding, cross-training, and workflow consistency across the program. Leads change management efforts within the team to support adoption of new workflows, service standards, and program initiatives.

**Job Requirements**

Required

* Bachelors Other Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, or a related field. and 5 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, upon hire and
* Experience managing and developing teams in a complex, matrixed healthcare organization, with direct accountability for program performance outcomes, upon hire and
* Experience delivering high-touch, patient-centered services for complex or high-acuity patient populations, including programs such as transplant, oncology, specialty referral, or equivalent tertiary or quaternary care settings, upon hire and
* Experience with electronic health record and hospital information systems; proficiency with productivity suites including Google Workspace and Microsoft Office., upon hire or

Preferred

* Masters Other Master’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Nursing, or a related field and 7-9 years 7 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, upon hire and
* Experience with international patient programs, embassy-sponsored care, or global sponsor coordination., upon hire and
* Clinical background including Registered Nurse (RN) licensure or equivalent clinical operations experience, upon hire and
* Experience in a dedicated destination care, international patient services, or specialty referral program at an academic medical center or large health system, upon hire and
* Experience building or expanding programs, including policy and operational protocol development, upon hire and
* Experience preparing and delivering financial and operating performance reports and presentations for leadership, upon hire and
* Experience with referral management, patient access, financial counseling, registration, or admissions workflows, upon hire and
* Experience managing program operations across multiple facilities or markets within a large health system., upon hire
* Certified Case Manager, upon hire or
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Certification, upon hire or
* Project Management Professional, upon hire or
* Registered Nurse: TX, upon hire

Where You'll Work

Baylor St. Luke’s Medical Center is an 1,045 bed facility located in the Texas medical center. A joint venture with Baylor College of Medicine, Baylor St. Luke’s is an internationally recognized leader in research and clinical excellence that has given rise to breakthroughs in cardiovascular care, neuroscience, oncology, transplantation, and more. The hospital is home to the Dan L Duncan Comprehensive Cancer Center, a nationally-accredited and NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center. Our new McNair Campus is designed around the human experience—modeled on evidence-based practices for the safety of patients, visitors, staff, and physicians. The 27.5-acre campus represents the future of healthcare through a transformative alliance focused on leading-edge patient care, research, and education.

 **Pay Range** 
$60.24 - $89.60 /hour

records.title: Global Director, Supplier Quality
records.description:
**Job Title:** Global Director, Supplier Quality

**Job Location:** Southfield, MI

**What we offer:**

VeoneerSafety Systemsis the world leader in Automotive Electronic Safety Systems. Veoneer’s scalable, best-in-class restraint control systems are mitigating the effects of a car crash. To date, we have delivered more than 1 billion devices to car manufacturers globally.
 
 
Veoneer Safety Systems has an international and collaborative team of 2,700 employees in 11 countries. We empower our people and are dedicated to their professional development and growth*.* 
 
Veoneer Safety Systems – Protect Everyone in Every Crash.

**What you'll do:**

The Global Director of Supplier Quality leads the global SQ organization, setting strategy, standards, and accountability for supplier readiness, performance, and continuous improvement.

The role combines global Supplier Quality leadership (80%) with North America Engineering Quality and Operational Quality leadership (20%).

**Key Responsibilities for Supplier Quality** (80% of role)

**Strategic Leadership & Global Deployment**

* Set global SQ strategy aligned with corporate, customer, sourcing, and manufacturing objectives.
* Define and execution of Supplier Quality Policies, Standards, Processes, Methods and Systems.
* Owner of Veoneer Supplier Manual (VSM), Supplier Quality Project (SQP) – APQP & PPAP, Supplier Non-Conformance Material (NCM) Management.
* Align cross-functional priorities, resources, and accountability; establish SQE oversight of workload, open issues, owners, overdue actions, and escalations.
* Monitor supplier quality targets, initiatives and indicators to ensure compliance to Veoneer Supplier Quality related policies, standards and reporting.

**Supplier Development & Standards Compliance**

* Oversee new supplier assessment, qualification, and development with Purchasing and Engineering; improve assessment models and ensure teams close risks and capability gaps before sourcing and production approval.
* Set common supplier requirements, risk-based audit and development expectations, and change controls; ensure existing suppliers improve capability and sustain company and customer compliance.
* Representing quality in Supplier Sourcing Board.

**Supplier Performance & Major Quality Issues**

* Lead major supplier escalations with supplier executives and cross-functional teams, ensuring containment, exposure assessment, production and customer protection, and verified permanent corrective actions.
* Drive common KPIs and improvement targets for supplier PPM, repeat defects, corrective-action aging, disruptions.
* Require leadership reviews and improvement plans for systemic issues, sharing lessons learned across suppliers.
* Supplier Scorecard (VS051 rating) and drive continuous improvement for supplier quality performance.

**Supplier APQP / PPAP & Safe Launch**

* Ensure on time and effective supplier APQP, PPAP, and Safe Launch for new programs, suppliers, and changes, including risk reviews, capability verification, and readiness-gap closure before production release.

**Quality Tools, Talent Development & Training**

* Set expectations for consistent SQE application of core quality tools, process audits, and structured problem solving to strengthen prevention and corrective-action effectiveness.
* Assess global SQ team capabilities and set development priorities with regional managers to strengthen technical expertise, expand skills, and build future leaders through training, mentoring, and succession planning.
* Supplier Quality talent review and succession plan.

**Regional Leadership: Engineering Quality & Operational Quality** (20% of role)

* Represent Quality Leadership team in regional activities across RDE, Manufacturing and Supplier Quality teams.
* Align regional priorities, governance, performance reviews, and escalations with global Engineering Quality and Operational Quality leaders and standards.
* Guide development and launch readiness, quality system execution, major issue resolution, and lessons learned while retaining local execution accountability.

**What you'll bring:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering.

**Experience:** Minimum 15 years in supplier quality, including supplier qualification, development, major issue resolution, and talent development. Electronics experience required; automotive SQ experience strongly preferred. Experience leading a multinational organization is preferred.

**Skills:**

* Global SQ leadership and effective matrix-team management.
* Cross-functional influence, supplier executive engagement, and timely decision-making.
* Strong supplier APQP, PPAP, change management, and Safe Launch knowledge.
* Advanced PFMEA, control plan, MSA, SPC, capability, audit, and 8D expertise; proven data-driven problem resolution and daily management.
* Strong commodity expertise for IC, PCB and/or mechanical parts is preferred.
* Ability to work effectively across cultures and time zones.
* Experience in other Quality domains is preferred

**Location:** Physical location Markham, Ontario, Canada or Southfield, Michigan; global scope across North America, Europe, India, and Asia.

**Travel:** International travel will be required 8-10 times per year.

**Reporting / Collaboration:**

* Reports to SVP Manufacturing & Quality.
* Solid-line responsibility for tech-center SQEs; dotted-line functional leadership of plant SQEs, with plant leadership retaining local operational accountability.
* Partners with Purchasing, Operations, Engineering, Industrialization, Program Management, and supplier leadership.

records.title: Director, Quality (Mentor, OH or Plymouth, MN onsite based)

postedPay.title: Director, Quality (Mentor, OH or Plymouth, MN onsite based)

records.description:
**Position Summary**
The Director, Quality is responsible for leading multiple manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality resources in the execution of the overall STERIS Quality System. This position is principally responsible for manufacturing/service site or functional quality system execution to drive product/service quality improvement and ensure compliance with, as appropriate, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, MDSAP, FDA QMSR CFR Part 820/211, EU MDR, and other applicable standards. Supporting the GI Reprocessing business, this role provides quality leadership for products, processes, and services that help healthcare providers safely clean, disinfect, and reprocess gastrointestinal endoscopes and related equipment. The Director will champion a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, helping ensure the delivery of safe, effective, and reliable solutions that support infection prevention, patient safety, and customer confidence. The Quality Director will lead teams of quality managers and engineers responsible for product and service quality, supplier quality, new product/service support, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality system execution. This leader will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Commercial teams to drive operational excellence, mitigate risk, support innovation, and enhance quality performance across the GI Reprocessing portfolio.
  
  
Preferred onsite location: Mentor, OH, with consideration for candidates based in Plymouth, MN or Conroe, TX.
  
  
**What You’ll Do As a Director Quality**

* The Director, Quality will have responsibility for the following: Leads manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality staff in the execution and continuous improvement of the STERIS Quality System. Operates with a focus on the following objectives:

+ Ensures site level compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
+ Drives strategies and methods to continuously improve capital, consumable and service product quality performance.
+ Establishes clear and consistent quality measurement systems in order to monitor and drive results.
+ Leads quality planning and the execution of assigned New Product/Service Development (NPD) projects to achieve targeted quality deliverable adherence.
+ Drives targeted supplier quality improvement efforts and oversees supplier evaluation, approval, and control for assigned manufacturing sites.
+ Assists in the continuous improvement and standardization of quality system procedures and monitor effectiveness.
+ Supports the reliability function by integrating design for reliability tools and techniques within the local projects.
+ Leads quality planning efforts through cross-functional teaming at a site level.

* Supports the New Product/Service Development process and projects to ensure projects attain cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
* Directs local staff on planning sequential and concurrent quality activities. Establish planning and monitoring tools and techniques.
* Provides Quality viewpoints and opinions in planning and specifying existing and future products.
* Assists in the development of the Quality budget. Helps to ensures resources are adequate to fully support the Quality System.
* Takes ownership of all local quality issues, projects, and development activities. Works closely with the site’s Senior Management Teams to provide strategic direction and development of the manufacturing sites product quality strategies and tactics.
* Manages and provide direction to a teams of quality professionals both at corporate and manufacturing sites, with responsibility for hiring, performance management, appropriate staffing, and deployment of resources.
* Assures that local sites maintain and improve operational and quality systems to remain in a state of compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
* Works closely with the regulatory function to ensure compliance to appropriate ISO and FDA standards; plans for and assists in the management of external audits.
* Leads manufacturing and service site quality teams to ensure alignment to operations, support of Lean efforts and drive quality improvement performance for products, services, and processes across the sites.
* This individual has autonomy to perform the duties of Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) on behalf of STERIS legal manufacturing entities under the EU MDR. This individual shall suffer no disadvantage within the organization in relation to proper fulfilment of his or her duties in lieu of article 15 of the EU MDR.

**Required**
**The Experience, Skills, and Abilities Needed**

* Bachelor’s Degree (Engineering or related technical field)
* Minimum 10 years of experience with increased responsibility leading quality system and product quality improvement efforts. Exceptional leadership manifested through organizing and motivating teams toward their respective goals by employing hands-on management.
* Must fulfil the experience requirements listed in Article 15 of the EUMDR (PRRC).
* A solid quality foundation indicated by a demonstrated understanding of Lean/Six Sigma, quality system, and product/process improvement methodologies.
* Solid business acumen and proven ability to build and lead process and product improvement strategies and results.
* Strong expertise in analytical methods, quality systems, and continuous improvement methods.
* Excellent interpersonal, as well as verbal and written communication skills in order to develop and maintain rapport and effective internal and external relationships to support business success.
* The ability to work hard and deliver results under pressure, as well as the willingness to address and shift priorities in rapidly changing markets.

**Preferred**

* Advanced degree.
* Experience with statistical analysis software and Visio.
* Experience in medical device industry.

**Other**

* Excellent problem-solving skills.
* Focus on identification of potential issues and continuous improvement.
* Experience working on cross-functional teams and on own initiative.
* Demonstrated excellent organizational, oral, and written communications skills.
* Must have PC experience, as well as working familiarity of desktop applications including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

**What STERIS Offers**
We value our employees and are committed to providing a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, well-being, and financial future.
  
  
**Here Is a Brief Overview Of What We Offer**

* Market competitive pay
* Extensive paid time off and (9) added holidays
* Excellent healthcare, dental, and vision benefits
* Long/short term disability coverage
* 401(K) with company match
* Maternity and parental leave
* Additional add on benefits/discounts for programs such as pet insurance
* Tuition reimbursement and continued educational programs
* Excellent opportunities for advancement in a stable long-term career

Pay range for this opportunity is $144,500.00 - $187,000.00. This position is eligible for bonus participation.
  
  
Minimum pay rates offered will comply with county/city minimums, if higher than range listed. Pay rates are based on a number of factors, including but not limited to local labor market costs, years of relevant experience, education, professional certifications, foreign language fluency, etc.
  
  
STERIS offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits portfolio. Click here for a complete list of benefits: STERIS Benefits
  
  
Open until position is filled.
  
  
STERIS is a leading global provider of products and services that support patient care with an emphasis on infection prevention. WE HELP OUR CUSTOMERS CREATE A HEALTHIER AND SAFER WORLD by providing innovative healthcare and life sciences products and services around the globe. For more information, visit www.steris.com.
  
  
If you need assistance completing the application process, please call 1 (440) 392.7047. This contact information is for accommodation inquiries only and cannot be used to check application status.
  
  
STERIS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity to ensure that persons are recruited, hired, trained, transferred and promoted in all job groups regardless of race, color, religion, age, disability, national origin, citizenship status, military or veteran status, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, and any other category protected by federal, state or local law. We are not only committed to this policy by our status as a federal government contractor, but also we are strongly bound by the principle of equal employment opportunity.
  
  
The full affirmative action program, absent the data metrics required by
  
  

* 60-741.44(k), shall be available to all employees and applicants for employment for inspection upon request. The program may be obtained at your location’s HR Office during normal business hours.

Saluda Medical is a commercial‑stage medical device company focused on developing treatments for chronic neurological conditions using its novel closed‑loop neuromodulation platform. The company’s proprietary technology senses and measures neural responses to stimulation and automatically adjusts therapy based on real‑time neurophysiological feedback.
  
  
Saluda Medical’s first product, the Evoke® System, is designed to deliver known, consistent, and personalized spinal cord stimulation therapy by objectively measuring neural responses and maintaining therapy within a prescribed therapeutic window. Saluda Medical is headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
  
  
At Saluda, we challenge boundaries. We innovate and think beyond the conventional. Our focus is to revolutionize the standard of care in neuromodulation to positively impact patient’s lives.
  
  
The Quality Director reports to the VP QA and is responsible for managing the company’s quality activities at the Bloomington, Minnesota site.
  
  
What You’ll Do:
  
  

* Manage all quality control (QC) activities, to include receiving inspection and product release from the site.
* Manage all quality assurance activities in the distribution facility, to include non-conformance reports (NCR) and supplier quality for our contract manufactured and OEM acquired products.
* Ensure activities performed in the facility are compliant to global regulatory requirements for which we claim compliance, as well as Saluda business expectations.
* In partnership with the head of US Distribution and Customer Service, be a vocal advocate for a strong culture of quality and compliance at the site.
* Build strong working relationships with other cross-functional leadership at the site to include Supply Chain, Distribution & Customer Service, Clinical, Sustaining Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs.
* In partnership with the head of US Distribution and Customer Service, ensure products distributed from the facility are handled appropriately and distributed to customers accurately and in a timely manner.
* Provide direct leadership to inspectors, technicians, quality specialists and engineers utilizing an inclusive and empowering leadership approach.
* Manage distribution, contract manufacturing and OEM-related quality challenges as they arise.
* Develop and ensure the implementation of a site inspection readiness plan.
* Participate internal and external audits to ensure the site’s quality system is effective.
* Manage and lead quality improvement projects in all areas of responsibility.
* Organize Supplier Change Assessment Board meetings and ensure submitted change request has the required information for the Change Assessment Board.

What You’ll Bring:
  
  

* Bachelor of Science degree or higher in a life sciences or engineering discipline
* At least 5+ years of experience in medical device quality with 2+ years of leadership experience.
* Proven ability to execute and maintain quality systems, with direct experience in post-market quality, distribution quality, or supplier quality.
* Strong relationship builder and communicator with diverse work teams
* Experience building strong relationships with global colleagues.
* Ability to work on-site 4+ days a week.
* Prior experience with returned product analysis and oversight of U.S.
* FDA 21 CFR Part 806 reporting obligations.

Our Core Values:
  
  

* People – Our first responsibility is to the patients we serve.
* Integrity – Do the right thing
* Pioneering – Lead Boldly, Change Lives, Disrupt the Status-Quo
* Performance – Win together – Deliver with Excellence.

*Saluda Medical embraces diversity and equal opportunity. We are committed to building a team representative of a variety of backgrounds, perspectives and skills. We believe people are the source of our inspiration and innovation.*
*Saluda Medical does not accept non-solicited resumes or candidate submittals from search/recruiting agencies not already on Saluda Medical’s approved agency list. Unsolicited resumes or candidate information submitted to Saluda Medical by search/recruiting agencies not already on Saluda Medical’s approved agency list shall become the property of Saluda Medical.*

records.title: Global Director of Quality
records.description:
General Summary
  
  
The Global Director of Quality is responsible for oversight of Quality Management and Continuous Improvement Programs for Team Industrial Services globally. The position is ultimately responsible for all corporate and Divisional Quality and Continuous support personnel. The successful candidate provides the necessary management and oversight to ensure the implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of TEAM’s Quality Management System (QMS) as well as the supplemental Quality Control and Technical programs. Position is responsible for managing and coordinating all Quality support activities relating to the execution of the Quality Management System (QMS) for Team Corporate, Product and Service Line, Engineering and Manufacturing, and Operations. Global Director of Quality is responsible for operating on a cost-effective basis within the framework of company approved policies, objectives, and budgets.
  
  
**Essential Job Functions**

* Maintains a safe, secure and healthy environment by adhering to Company/Customer safety and quality standards and practices and to legal regulations, alerting others regarding potential hazards or concern
* Adheres to and is a champion of TEAM’s Core Values
* Establish a continuous improvement culture across the enterprise utilizing known methods and concepts such as Lean, Six Sigma, FMEA, Kaizen, Poka-yoke, CAPA, 8D, etc.
* Maintains contact with district, division and corporate levels to promote and instill a “Quality Culture” throughout the organization.
* Ensure TEAMs QMS is globally consistent and regionally precise based on local requirements.
* When necessary, provide training to affected personnel, including customers, to obtain maximum process efficiency, productivity, cooperation, and morale.
* Leads the Enterprise management review to evaluate quality objectives, assess the adequacy and effectiveness and continuing suitability of the existing QMS and identify opportunities for improvement.
* Manage the Supplier Quality Management program and supports third-party and Customer assessments.
* Ensures company-wide targets and objectives are established and action plans are developed and tracked to achieve them.
* Development and implementation of performance monitoring and measurement system of leading and lagging KPIs to evaluate performance across the entire supply chain – Supplier – Order Intake - Engineering – Manufacturing – Installation – Service – Warranty.
* Development and implementation of system of associating and tracking non-conformances with costs for supplier claims, internal issues and customer escapes. This includes understanding the company’s Cost of Poor Quality and Non-Conformance Costs.
* Stay up-to-date on industry trends, including Quality-related initiatives.
* Develops medium to long-term operating strategies and recommendations for plans and programs for increasing TEAM’s Quality performance.
* Prepare capital expense and operating budgets and ensure cost-effective departmental operations.
* Support sales efforts when necessary, including the completion of pre-qualification surveys and submission of controlled quality documents to customer representatives.
* Have a general understanding of all company products and services that are available to our customers, and how TEAM’s Quality program applies to these areas.
* Ensures the Enterprise external certifications (ISO-9001, Nuclear, Aerospace, etc.) are maintained.
* Other duties as assigned

**Job Qualifications**

* Requires a bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field. Master’s degree preferred. Continuous Improvement Methodology certifications such as Six Sigma is preferred.
* Experience in Oil and Gas, Lean Manufacturing, Petrochemical, or a Field Service Industry is a must.
* 15 years’ experience in Quality or Operational Excellence related function.
* Experience with problem solving methods such as A3, FMEA, etc. preferred.
* Experience in introducing/implementing a solid warranty tracking system that captures accurate Customer and or Field related issues.

records.description:
Apogee Architectural Metals
  
  
Apogee Enterprises, Inc. (NASDAQ: APOG), founded in 1949 and headquartered in Minneapolis, MN designs and delivers architectural products and services that enclose and enhance commercial buildings. www.apog.com
  
  
Apogee Architectural Metals is a segment of Apogee specializing in aluminum framing, windows, storefront, curtainwall, and entrance systems. We provide integrated capabilities, including design, engineering, extrusion, finishing, fabrication and assembly, across North America. Through our brands including Alumicor, EFCO, Linetec, Tubelite, and Wausau, we deliver quality, consistency, and value-added services throughout our portfolio.
  
  
**Position Summary**
The Director, Quality is a senior quality leader accountable for transforming quality performance, capability, and culture across the business. Reporting to the VP, Operations, this leader will set the quality agenda, lead the Quality organization, and establish the operating discipline, systems, and leadership routines required to deliver consistent customer and operational outcomes. This role requires a proven quality leader who can move beyond compliance to build a scalable quality operating model, elevate accountability across sites, and influence leaders at all levels to adopt new standards, behaviors, and ways of working.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Set and execute the quality strategy, operating model, governance routines, and performance expectations needed to improve quality outcomes across sites
* Lead, coach, and develop Quality Managers and site quality teams to strengthen capability, accountability, decision-making, and execution discipline
* Build a scalable quality operating system that integrates QMS standards, metrics, technology, problem solving, and leadership routines into daily operations
* Use customer feedback, quality data, audit findings, and operational trends to identify systemic issues, prioritize action, and eliminate recurring failure modes
* Partner with the VP, Operations, site leaders, and functional leaders to align quality priorities with operational performance, customer commitments, and business objectives
* Lead significant customer, product, process, or operational quality issues with clear escalation, root-cause discipline, corrective action, and organizational learning
* Lead quality transformation initiatives that reduce variation, improve process capability, strengthen operating discipline, and deliver measurable customer and business impact
* Influence leaders across operations, engineering, supply chain, commercial, and functional teams to remove barriers and adopt new standards, behaviors, and ways of working
* Report quality performance, transformation progress, risks, recommendations, and business impact to the VP, Operations and senior leadership
* Develop and maintain enterprise-wide Quality Management Systems (QMS), ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory, industry, customer, and company standards.
* Lead supplier quality strategies, including qualification, performance management, audits, and corrective action processes to ensure consistent raw material and supplier performance.
* Ensure data integrity and leverage digital quality tools, analytics, and technology solutions to improve visibility, decision-making, and process control.
* Own customer quality performance, including complaint management, warranty reduction initiatives, customer audits, and key customer quality relationships.

**Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities**

* Strong quality leadership with the ability to connect quality strategy, operational execution, customer outcomes, and business performance
* Ability to lead managers and teams while influencing cross-functional leaders in a matrixed, multi-site organization
* Strong communication and change leadership skills, including creating clarity, building commitment, managing resistance, and sustaining adoption
* Enterprise mindset with the ability to challenge current-state practices, address systemic issues, and raise the standard for quality performance
* Talent builder and operating leader who can align resources, develop people, and deliver measurable results through others

**Education And Experience**

* Education

+ Bachelor's degree in Quality Management, Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred

* Experience

+ 10+ years of progressive quality, operations, or manufacturing leadership experience, including accountability for quality strategy, performance, systems, governance, and standards
+ Experience leading quality managers and teams in a complex, multi-site manufacturing environment
+ Proven success transforming quality systems, operating discipline, metrics, governance, and leadership routines
+ Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders, lead enterprise-level change, and drive adoption across functions, teams, and sites
+ Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) Development and Implementation Experience. Experience in TQMS (Total quality management system; this is more driven and aligned with our AMS and Lean CI activities). This also help to target few key organizations I like to target. Supplier Quality Management and Audit Programs Management. Policy Development and Deployment Experience preferred to form a strategy and deploy/implementation.

**Work Environment/Travel Requirements**

* Frequent exposure to manufacturing environment
* Overnight travel requirements will be variable based on projects and business activities, expected up to 50% depending on home location
* Physical Requirements

+ Ability to work in both office and manufacturing environments.
+ Lift up to 10 lbs.

records.title: Director of Quality Assurance
records.description:
Elevate is committed to providing the highest quality commercial roofing, wall and lining systems to solve our customers’ challenges, grounded by a 45-year legacy of proven experience. Our mission is to deliver solutions that save time, perform reliably and protect our communities. We are devoted to building partnerships rooted in trust in reflection of our Elevate promise that Nobody Covers You Better™.
  
  
Elevate is part of the Amrize family of brands. Visit ElevateCommercialBP.com to learn more.
  
  
We’re seeking a Director of Quality Assurance who’s ready to be part of a people-first company offering best-in-class products, exceptional training, and deep industry pride—all built to help our partners and team succeed.
  
  
**About The Role**
The Quality Assurance Director strategically leads the development, implementation, and maintenance of comprehensive quality evaluation and control systems across the organization. This includes overseeing the design and analysis of inspection and testing processes, ensuring the precision and accuracy of products and equipment, driving root cause analysis for incidents, and establishing compliance with reliability standards and documentation requirements to uphold the highest levels of product quality and operational excellence
  
  
**What You'll Accomplish**

* Strategic Oversight - Overseeing and directing the overall operations of quality assurance within a company to ensure continuous improvement and compliance. This involves defining and promoting a quality mindset across the entire company.
* Quality Management System - Developing and implementing quality management systems to ensure product and service quality, and maintaining and improving quality standards, policies, and procedures.
* Compliance & Regulatory Oversight - Ensuring compliance with industry standards, regulations, and company policies, and coordinating with regulatory bodies and external auditors.
* Quality Control, Claim Mgmt, Supplier Quality - Overseeing quality control processes to ensure products meet quality standards, and conducting regular quality audits and inspections to identify and address quality issues.This also includes establishing and enforcing quality standards, testing materials and products, and developing raw material and in-process product inspection standards.
* Continuous Improvement - Leading continuous improvement initiatives to enhance product quality and operational efficiency, and implementing best practices to reduce defects and improve processes. This can involve applying tools such as CAPA, SPC charts, Root Cause Analysis, and FMEA, and leading Six Sigma or Lean initiatives.
* Leadership & Team Development - Leading and mentoring the quality assurance team, fostering a culture of high performance and professional development, and ensuring the team has the necessary skills and resources. Responsible for generating a culture of collaboration across the organization.
* Budget & Financial Management - Achieving financial objectives by preparing the quality assurance budget, scheduling expenditures, analyzing variances, and initiating corrective actions.
* Customer Experience - Gathering customer feedback through gemba and data collection on quality andperformance, ensuring products meet or exceed customer expectations, and implementing changes based on feedback
* Demonstrate a commitment to communicating, improving and adhering to health, safety and environmental policies in all work environments and areas.
* Promote a culture of safety and exhibit these behaviors.

**What We're Looking For**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Mgmt, or related discipline from an accredited university or college.
* At least 8 y+ years of relevant quality, continuous improvement, manufacturing experience including at least 5 years management or direct/indirect leadership experience.
* 3+ years of QMS / ISO9001 or similar experience required.
* CMQ/QE, CQE, CQA are all preferred.
* Six Sigma certification preferred.

**Additional Requirements**

* Successful candidates must adhere to all safety protocols and proper use of Amrize approved Personal Protection Equipment ("PPE"), including but not limited to respirators.
* Employees that are required to wear respirators must be clean shaven where the respirator seal meets the face in order to pass the qualitative and quantitative fit tests.

**What We Offer**

* Competitive salary
* Retirement Savings: Choose from 401(k) pre-tax and/or Roth after-tax savings
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan
* Medical, Dental, Disability and Life Insurance
* Holistic Health & Well-being programs
* Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) & Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) for health and dependent care
* Vision and other Voluntary benefits and discounts
* Paid time off & paid holidays
* Paid Parental Leave (maternity & paternity)
* Educational Assistance Program

The Director of Quality, Barlett Operations is responsible for cGMP Operations of the facility inclusive of manufacturing quality, repair quality, distribution quality, quality inspection and quality systems. This role will ensure quality systems and processes are established, maintained, and continuously improved to consistently deliver right first-time quality, safeguard patient safety, and ensure customer satisfaction. The Director of Quality will ensure that the site is inspection ready at all times, manage and facilitate site audits and inspections, lead execution of commitments to regulators, and ensure that quality and/or compliance issues are corrected in a timely manner. This role will lead site initiatives aimed at building and sustaining a strong culture of quality and will work collaboratively with other functions at the site to achieve quality and business objectives. This position is the default Quality Management Representative for the Bartlett campus and reports dotted line to Top Management at the Bartlett campus.
  
  
**Job Duties**

* Leadership of the Site Quality organization and serves as site quality management representative ensuring efficient and flawless execution of quality systems and processes to ensure product quality and compliance with global and site policies and procedures, FDA regulations, and other applicable regulations, standards and guidance.

This includes validation and maintenance of the Site Master Validation Plan, calibration, equipment maintenance, critical component evaluations, and quality inspections.

Acts with appropriate levels of urgency commensurate with risk and escalates issues to management.
