records.description:
Direct Biologics is a market leading innovator and science-based cGMP manufacturer of regenerative biologic products. Direct Biologics is hiring a hands-on QC leader for our Poway, CA testing laboratory in the greater San Diego area. You will lead a team of analysts to execute release and stability testing for a late-stage extracellular vesicle biologics program as part of a broader multi-product pipeline, and prepare the QC function for commercial operations.

We are currently looking for a Director of QC, responsible for:

* Responsible for strategy and execution of late-stage to commercial cGMP testing laboratory readiness, owning key decisions in method transfer, validation, and life-cycle management.
* Drives phase-appropriate regulatory and compliance initiatives for a portfolio of cell therapy extracellular vesicle products (early clinical through commercial stages). Presents plans to senior leadership and leads QC workstream for inspection readiness.
* Leads interactions with health authorities related to internal and outsource testing programs, including in-process, characterization, drug substance and drug product release, and stability.
* This working leadership position requires hands-on participation in routine and non-routine testing activities. The individual must maintain their own training and qualification, work independently at the laboratory bench, execute test methods, troubleshoot problems, perform investigations, and write reports when needed to meet business and regulatory commitments.
* Collaborates with R&D and Analytical Development team to introduce method lifecycle improvements and new technologies to the QC laboratory.
* Accountable for timely execution and documentation of routine laboratory tests. Ensures the on-time closure of sampling plans, protocols, laboratory investigations, CAPAs, change control records, and other QMS commitments.
* Develops and communicates departmental resourcing plans to serve broad company goals, including personnel, budget, and timelines. Adjusts plans and priorities according to executive leadership resourcing decisions.
* Leads Quality Control operations:
* + Hire, onboard, train, qualify, and assist professional development of QC team members.
* + Ensure timely execution of STAT and release testing.
* + Manage stability sample inventory and pull schedule, coordinating sample transit with cGMP warehouse, outsource sample submission, and timely internal testing.
* + Ensure timely purchase and qualification of supplies, materials, and equipment.
* + Maintain equipment use, calibration, maintenance, and cleaning records and coordinate related activities.
* + Communicate testing timeframes, expected start/finish dates, and testing outcomes to internal and external stakeholders.
* + Author/approve policies, procedures, and work instructions for accuracy and compliance.
* + Author/approve ROA, COA, trend reports, and stability reports.
* Responsible for QC data/records to ensure content adheres to established cGMP quality standards.
* + Maintain risk register, support internal and mock audits, and show steady compliance progress in collaboration with QA team members.
* + Collaborate with IT to ensure data Integrity and storage of original source data in accordance with part 11 requirements.
* Ensure strict adherence to EPA, OSHA, and FAA safety and clean environmental guidelines.
* Occasional travel by air and/or car may be required to participate in on-site vendor activities, such as method transfer, vendor meetings, and vendor quality audits.
* Excels in a fast-paced environment. Independently prioritizes activity based on importance and urgency, manages time well, anticipates challenges, and delivers progress in line with program goals.
* Strong attention to detail and related understanding of CFR, compendial, and other regulatory requirements.

  
  
**Requirements**

**Skill Requirements:**

* Top expert in preparing cGMP clinical stage testing laboratories for commercial launch, with evidence of leading a QC readiness workstream for a late-stage or commercial biologic product.
* Extensive knowledge of domestic and global compliance requirements for commercial release testing programs.
* Recent hands-on experience with one or more of the following: human cell culture techniques, cell-based potency assays, protein assays (plate based ELISAs, immunostaining-based assays, fluorescence microscopy), quantitative PCR, RNA and protein isolation and quantification methods.
* Familiarity with cGMP Quality Control testing, qualification, and validation of analytical test methods with internal and outsourced contexts.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills in cross-functional team setting.
* Must be highly flexible to respond to urgent needs and directional changes in a start-up environment but also have the attention to detail required to execute studies that will be reviewed by the FDA and other regulatory authorities.
* Lead GMP QC investigations and provide solutions to issues including OOS, deviations and/or CAPA.
* Ability to maintain lab equipment including qualification and calibration.
* Knowledgeable about statistical modeling for quality control applications.
* Technical understanding and working knowledge of contemporary molecular biology, cell biology, microbiology and/or biochemistry.
* Track record leading efficient and cost-effective QC operations while maintaining scientific rigor and GMP compliance. Demonstrated ability to optimize resources, streamline processes, and overcome challenges in a lean operating model.

**Qualifications Requirements:**

* Advanced degree in analytical chemistry, biotechnology, cell and molecular biology, biochemistry, or other related field is preferred.
* Minimum of 8 years biotech based-work experience in cell culture, biochemical, or molecular biology GMP QC testing. Experience with late-stage advanced therapy products is preferred.

records.description:
Overview:

**Valley Behavioral Health** is seeking an experienced **Director of Quality and Accreditation** to join our team!

Offering the highest quality of treatment in the area, **Valley Behavioral Health** focuses on providing their patients with the tools and knowledge needed to live happy, healthy lives. Regardless of the level of care, patients receive personalized treatment by a multi-disciplinary team of therapists, social workers, psychiatrists, psychiatric nurses, and other caring mental health professionals.

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced **Director of Quality and Accreditation** to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
  + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
  + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
  + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
  + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
  + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
  + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
  + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
  + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
  + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observations and the electronic medical record, as applicable.
  + Lead Root-Cause Analyses and conduct timely and regular evaluation of serious incidents, complaints, grievances and related investigations to:
    - Identification of events, trends and patterns that may affect client health, safety and or treatment efficacy,
    - Committee evaluation findings and recommendations submitted to agency management for corrective action,
    - Implemented actions, outcomes, trends analyzed over time
  + Develop corrective action plans for the resolution of areas of regulatory vulnerability or those which could compromise patient safety in collaboration with other facility leaders.
  + Ensure proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + Ensure proper reporting of incidents and adverse clinical outcomes to duly authorized enforcement agencies or regulatory agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + In conjunction with assigned corporate Division Quality Director, initiate and lead communications with regulatory agencies as appropriate.
  + Develop sustainable performance improvement practices through analysis of data and prioritization of efforts to improve survey readiness and consistency of care delivery using expected best-practices.

records.title: Site Quality Director
records.description:
**Why Us?**

At Par Health, we believe great healthcare is built on getting the essentials right. We’re looking for passionate, talented individuals who share our commitment to improving lives. With a global workforce, we lead with pride and purpose—prioritizing quality and safety while fostering a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and teamwork. Elevating the Essentials isn’t just our tagline, it’s the higher standard we live by every day.

**Job Description Summary**

The Site Quality Director is responsible for ensuring cGMP compliance and product quality at the Raleigh, NC facility while supporting broader site quality initiatives aligned with company objectives. This role provides strategic leadership in the development, implementation, and oversight of the site quality systems to ensure that all manufacturing, testing, packaging, storage, and distribution activities meet regulatory standards and deliver the highest product quality. The Site Quality Director leads and mentors quality teams, oversees daily quality operations, and serves as a key partner to site leadership by providing guidance on quality and compliance across the organization.

**Job Description**

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* **Manages all aspects of Site Quality System including but not limited to: CAPA, exceptions, document management, complaint investigation handling, change control, supplier quality, OOS investigations, stability programs, and regulatory inspection readiness.**
* **Support a quality program which instils personal accountability for accuracy, consistency, and completeness for all operations**
* **Provides direction and leadership for the successful execution of quality activities, such as:**
* **Ensures health authority inspection (FDA, EU, Health Canada and others) readiness through development of compliance enhancement plans, internal audit program, and industry intelligence.**
* **Customer complaint investigation, including interaction with customers and resolution of critical issues.**
* **Manages the supplier quality program to fulfill regulatory and site needs.**
* **Conducts and/or administers new employee, ongoing, and directed training on GMP topics to ensure compliance to regulations. Manages site training compliance program.**
* **CAPA program to effectively identify and correct problems that impact product quality or compliance.**
* **Validation activities for new, altered, or modified equipment, facilities, or manufacturing processes.**
* **Customer audit process (approximately 50/yr.) to include preparation, hosting, and responding to issues noted – also, utilize input from customer audits and a continuous improvement tool.**
* **Documents management and label control to fulfill regulatory and business needs**
* **Stability program for both API products manufactured at the site.**
* **Approves highly technical investigations involving product impact.**
* **Sets direction and policies for cGMP compliance activities.**
* **Schedules employees through subordinates, performance appraisals, and performance management of team members.**
* **Budgets and adherence for areas of functional responsibility.**
* **Directly interacting with key customers relating to technical issues, potential non-compliance activities, or service issues impacted by quality/compliance.**
* **Resolution of critical quality issues that could impact production, customer service, quality, or compliance.**
* **Interprets regulatory guidance to determine site course of action for compliance.**
* **Technical expert in multiple quality functional areas, such as validation, product investigations, quality systems, and establishing compliance plans, etc.**

**DEPARTMENT** **SPECIFIC/NON-ESSENTIAL** **FUNCTIONS:**

* **Other duties as assigned with or without accommodation.**
* **Participates in a certified 5S Workplace System to ensure good housekeeping and organization.**

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:**

**Education:**

**BS Chemistry, Engineering, Life Science or related.**

**Experience:**

**7-10 years leadership experience in a chemical or pharmaceutical manufacturing environment, preferably specific to Quality and/or manufacturing related functions.**

**Preferred** **Skills/Qualifications:**

* **Working knowledge of chemical, pharmaceutical or bio-pharmaceutical manufacturing.**
* **Must have knowledge and understanding of applicable global regulations, GMP and compendial requirements.**
* **Must have thorough knowledge and understanding of QA regulations as they apply to this type of facility.**
* **Experience in driving improvements in quality systems and quality performance is preferred.**
* **Certification as a Six Sigma Black or Green Belt and/or as a Certified Quality Engineer is considered a plus.**
* **Must have high technical ability and excellent** **interpersonal/communication** **skills. Requires excellent oral and written skills and good negotiation skills to effectively communicate and influence the outcome of quality related plans, programs, and activities throughout the business unit.**
* **Must have the ability and experience to drive cost reduction while continuously improving performance, as well as the ability to lead employees in making these changes.**

**RELATIONSHIP WITH OTHERS/ SCOPE:**

* **This position reports to the Interim Head of Quality, Generics.**
* **This position will have frequent communication and working relationships with departments and plant managers.**
* **Interacts with internal Staff (Department and Plant Managers) on all Site management issues. Advises Staff on compliance issues. Report on overall performance and critical quality issues to Corporate Quality. Interacts with Corporate Quality personnel, R&D, and quality and managers within the organization. Works with Commercial team on customer issues. External contacts include regulatory authorities, state, federal and international (FDA, OSHA, EPA, NCDENR), suppliers, customers and community contacts.**
* **Financial responsibilities include managing multi-million payroll and operating budgets. Also recommends major purchases and capital expenditures that are necessary to maintain operations of QC laboratory and to maintain or improve the site’s GMP compliance and performance.**

**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

* **70% Office Environment**  
  **30% Laboratory and Plant environment including exposure to raw materials and finished products**
* **Must be willing and able to wear PPE including hard-hat, steel-toed shoes, safety glasses, and any other devices or equipment as specified for the position.**
* **Some travel is required, both domestically and internationally.**

**DISCLAIMER:**

**The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this** **classification.** **They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of employees assigned to this position.**

**EEO Statement:**

We comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws prohibiting discrimination and harassment, and provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or genetic information, or any other classification protected by federal, state or local law. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

records.title: General Manager/President – Precision Manufacturing
records.description:
**Company Overview**

American Photonics, a portfolio company of BlueRock Global, is a precision optical manufacturer serving the aerospace, defense, industrial, medical, scientific, and commercial markets.

We are strengthening our manufacturing capabilities, investing in operational improvements, and expanding into higher-value precision optics and infrared applications.

We operate in a technically demanding manufacturing environment where quality, precision, accountability, and reliable execution are essential. Our focus is on building a stronger, more capable manufacturing business positioned for sustainable, profitable growth.

**Job Overview**

American Photonics is seeking an accomplished General Manager to lead overall business performance, manufacturing operations, and organizational development.

This is the senior on-site executive position, with direct responsibility for operating P&L performance and leadership across Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Sales, Supply Chain, and supporting business functions.

The ideal candidate has successfully led a technically complex manufacturing business, improved financial and operational results, developed accountable leadership teams, and executed meaningful business improvements.

We are looking for a decisive, hands-on leader who understands both the financial and operational sides of manufacturing. This individual must be equally comfortable reviewing business performance, resolving production challenges, developing customer relationships, and working directly with employees on the manufacturing floor.

Reporting to ownership, the General Manager will have responsibility for translating strategic objectives into achievable operating plans, establishing clear accountability, and delivering measurable results. The position will work closely with BlueRock's corporate resources while maintaining ownership of day-to-day business execution.

**Duties**

* Assume accountability for operating P&L performance, including revenue, gross margin, EBITDA, operating expenses, working capital, and achievement of financial objectives.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, budgets, forecasts, workforce plans, and capital investment priorities aligned with business objectives.
* Lead Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Sales, Supply Chain, and business operations to ensure coordinated execution and achievement of company objectives.
* Improve manufacturing performance through effective production planning, scheduling, labor utilization, material readiness, equipment effectiveness, and capacity management.
* Identify and resolve operational inefficiencies, production bottlenecks, excess costs, scrap, rework, quality issues, and sources of margin erosion.
* Establish clear departmental objectives, performance metrics, reporting standards, and management accountability for results.
* Strengthen job costing, pricing discipline, inventory control, purchasing practices, and financial visibility to support profitable decision-making.
* Lead and develop department managers, establish clear responsibilities and decision-making authority, address performance gaps, and build a capable, accountable leadership team.
* Partner with Sales and Engineering to evaluate customer opportunities, improve quoting accuracy, assess technical and manufacturing feasibility, and support profitable business growth.
* Build and maintain effective relationships with key customers, suppliers, strategic partners, and other business stakeholders.
* Improve ERP utilization, operational reporting, inventory accuracy, manufacturing documentation, and process controls to support efficient and scalable operations.
* Evaluate manufacturing capabilities, equipment investments, facility requirements, and process improvements based on operational needs, financial returns, and long-term business value.
* Maintain effective quality management systems, product traceability, corrective action processes, workplace safety standards, and compliance with applicable customer and regulatory requirements.
* Provide ownership with timely, accurate reporting on financial performance, operational results, business risks, and progress against established priorities.
* Lead organizational and operational changes with sound judgment, clear communication, and a consistent focus on employee engagement, accountability, and execution.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in precision, high-tolerance, or technically complex manufacturing environments.
* At least five years in a senior manufacturing leadership role, such as General Manager, Business Unit Leader, President, VP of Operations, or equivalent, with substantial financial and operational accountability.
* Demonstrated responsibility for a manufacturing business or business-unit P&L, including budgets, profitability, cost management, and operating performance.
* Proven success improving manufacturing profitability, productivity, operational efficiency, delivery performance, or organizational effectiveness, supported by measurable results.
* Experience leading cross-functional manufacturing teams, including Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and related business functions.
* Demonstrated ability to develop managers, establish performance expectations, manage organizational change, and hold teams accountable.
* Experience managing manufacturing operations involving complex processes, demanding quality standards, and customer-specific requirements.
* Strong business judgment, financial acumen, and the ability to make timely decisions based on operational and financial information.
* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant executive manufacturing experience.
* Ability to work full-time, on-site in Sarasota, Florida.

**Preferred**

* Leadership experience in precision optics, infrared optics, photonics, optical components, precision machining, aerospace, or defense manufacturing.
* Experience improving or scaling a small to mid-sized manufacturing business, particularly within an entrepreneurial or private-equity-backed environment.
* Experience with ERP implementation, systems modernization, manufacturing cost accounting, or operational restructuring.
* Experience leading manufacturing capacity expansion, capital equipment investment, new product introduction, or business improvement initiatives.
* Familiarity with ISO 9001 quality management systems, ITAR/export-control requirements, and regulated manufacturing environments.

**Compensation** will be determined based on the candidate’s relevant experience, qualifications, demonstrated capabilities, and the responsibilities of the position.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

American Photonics is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, experience, performance, and business needs, without regard to any status protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

Join us to lead innovative manufacturing processes that make a difference! We value energetic leaders who thrive on strategic growth, operational excellence, and inspiring teams to achieve their best every day.

Pay: From $1.00 per year

Application Question(s):

* Describe your experience leading precision, engineered, regulated, or technically complex manufacturing.
* This is an on-site in-person position, would commute be an issue?
* What is your earliest available start date?
* Describe the most recent manufacturing company you led, including its products, approximate revenue, employee count, and functions reporting to you.
* Describe the scope of your direct P&L responsibility, including the financial results and capital decisions you owned.
* Provide one example of a manufacturing business, market, customer base, or product line you helped grow. What actions did you lead, and what measurable results followed?
* Compensation is based on experience, demonstrated results, and capabilities. What are your salary expectations for this role?

Work Location: In person

records.description:
**Compensation Range**

$240,000 - $280,000 / Year

**Overview**

**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!** Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our Bakery business, lead great people, and strengthen the systems behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests have loved for decades.

**As the VP, Quality Assurance & Food Safety**, you’ll report to the Bakery President and lead food safety, quality assurance, sanitation, and technical services across two bakery plants totaling more than 160,000 square feet and supporting more than 600 staff members. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact: setting the strategy, rebuilding organizational trust, strengthening audit readiness, and elevating Good Manufacturing Practices through disciplined root cause analysis and corrective action. You’ll operate at both the executive and plant levels, bringing the leadership, technical expertise, and influence needed to create lasting change.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **A Trusted Executive Leader:** You build credibility through transparency, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through, earning the confidence to influence decisions at every level.
* **A Strategic, Hands-On Quality Leader:** You set the vision while staying connected to operations, understanding risk, removing barriers, and translating strategy into consistent execution.
* **An Audit and Compliance Expert:** You build a culture of year-round readiness where issues are identified early, corrective actions are effective, and findings are sustainably closed.
* **A Disciplined Problem Solver:** You look beyond the immediate issue, using data, risk assessment, and root cause analysis to solve systemic problems and prevent recurrence.

**Responsibilities**

* Set and lead the Bakery division’s Quality Assurance and Food Safety strategy across both facilities, establishing clear expectations for risk management, performance, and accountability.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to the Bakery President and executive leadership, providing clear perspective on food safety and quality risks, audit readiness, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Ensure trust and confidence in the function through technical credibility, transparency, strong partnerships, and consistent execution.
* Strengthen compliance and operational discipline across GMPs, HACCP, SQF, AIB, sanitation, allergen controls, environmental monitoring, traceability, supplier quality, microbiological testing, and recall readiness.
* Establish sustained audit readiness and ensure findings have clear ownership, effective corrective actions, and lasting resolution.
* Ensure highly systematic and disciplined adherence to product and process standards on a real-time basis to guarantee our cakes are beautiful and delicious.
* Build greater rigor around root cause analysis and corrective and preventive actions, addressing systemic issues rather than symptoms.
* Provide leadership across product and process quality, customer complaints, foreign-material controls, product holds, specifications, labeling, formulas, recipes, and Technical Services.
* Establish meaningful metrics and use data to identify trends, prioritize risk, and hold the organization accountable for results.
* Lead significant food safety, quality, sanitation, and regulatory matters with urgency, sound judgment, and appropriate escalation.
* Build and develop a high-performing Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Sanitation, and Technical Services organization with the talent and capabilities needed for long-term success.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Research and Development, and Human Resources to strengthen ownership and accountability for food safety and quality across the business.
* Prioritize resources and investments against the greatest risks and opportunities while effectively managing the function’s budget.

**Qualifications**

* 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Sanitation, or Technical Services within food manufacturing, including senior-level, multi-site responsibility.
* Demonstrated success leading food safety and quality strategy, organizational transformation, culture improvement, and high-performing technical teams.
* Deep expertise in GMPs, HACCP, preventive controls, sanitation, microbiological risk, allergen management, environmental monitoring, traceability, recalls, supplier quality, AIB, SQF, and food safety management systems.
* Extensive experience leading regulatory, certification, customer, and internal audits from preparation through corrective action and sustainable closure.
* Expertise in root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, risk assessment, and incident investigation.
* Proven ability to build organizational trust, strengthen accountability, influence senior leaders, and lead through significant change.
* Bachelor’s degree in microbiology, chemistry, food science, food safety, biology, engineering, or a closely related discipline.

**What we prefer:**

  

* Leadership experience within the bakery or dessert industry; experience in similarly complex food-manufacturing environments will also be considered.
* Master’s degree in a related technical or business discipline.
* Relevant certifications such as SQF Practitioner, HACCP, PCQI, or Certified Food Scientist.
* Bilingual English/Spanish.

**Benefits**

* Eligible to participate in an annual incentive bonus program
* Eligible for an annual long-term equity award in accordance with company Plan and approval process.
* Medical, Dental & Vision
* Access to a company car or car allowance
* Eligible for benefits on the first day of the month following date of hire
* Flexible vacation
* 5 days of sick time per year (first year prorated)
* Tuition Reimbursement of $2,500 for qualified programs
* Adoption Assistance Benefit of $2,500
* 25%-35% discount when dining as a guest
* Reusable gift card loaded annually for your dining enjoyment

**About the Company**

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery creates over 35,000 delicious cheesecakes per day across our two facilities in Calabasas, CA and Rocky Mount, NC plus other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees, and third-party bakery customers.  
  
The Cheesecake Factory Bakery is a subsidiary of The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated. Recognized as a Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® since 2014, The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated is a global $3.8 billion public company with more than 370 casual dining restaurants and over 48,000 staff members.  
  
We are an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming workplace for all. We welcome applicants from a wide variety of identities, ideas, perspectives, backgrounds and experiences to apply. The Cheesecake Factory offers reasonable accommodation to job applicants with disabilities.  
  
#SoCheesecake #LifeAtCheesecake  
  
To notify of a non-compliant job posting, please send a notice to ats@thecheesecakefactory.com.

records.title: VP Distribution Operations
records.description:
**Meet Vestis®:** For the People Who Make It All Work
  
At Vestis®, we provide uniforms, workplace supplies, and professional cleaning that help businesses simplify their workday and keep their teams safe, confident, and focused on what matters most. More than a provider, we are a partner in productivity, trusted to keep you running.
  
Join us and build a career supporting the people who make it all work.
  
  
Overview
  
The Vice President of Distribution Center Operations will lead the product distribution strategy and drive an economically competitive operation that delivers both best-in-class customer experience and distribution cost advantages across all facilities supporting Vestis Rental and Direct Sale customers.
  
This leader will influence and reinforce a portfolio of core values and accountability standards centered on safety, workforce engagement, customer experience, operational efficiency, and innovative solutions that support business goals. This role is responsible for deploying strategies and actionable plans that deliver measurable performance improvement.
  
This leader will also define and advance the technology roadmap for Distribution Center Operations, identifying opportunities to leverage artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, automation, advanced analytics, and other emerging technologies to improve safety, productivity, quality, service, capacity, and cost.
  
The Vice President will promote data-driven performance visibility, real-time corrective action, and strong cross-functional collaboration. This leader will work effectively with business partners to identify, address, and resolve operational issues.
  
This role will set goals and oversee key metrics related to customer fill rates, customer satisfaction, footprint utilization, inventory management, optimization and total DC cost, along with other key measures tied to Distribution Center Operations.
  
Responsibilities/Essential Functions
  

* Set and deliver the overall vision and distribution strategy for national and international distribution centers to ensure end-to-end customer needs are met at the lowest possible cost.
* Lead a high-performing team of supply chain practitioners, with direct and indirect responsibility for an organization of more than 600 employees.
* Partner with Human Resources to design and implement workforce strategies for each distribution center location, including the evolution of workforce skills needed to support increasingly automated and technology-enabled operations.
* Define objectives, establish key performance metrics, and create a regular review cadence across safety, quality, fill rate, customer satisfaction, inventory management, budget performance, and other critical operating areas.
* Implement metrics, processes, and operating routines that drive accountability and ensure results.
* Improve costs year over year through disciplined operational execution and continuous improvement.
* Drive performance improvement through the use of continuous improvement methodology.
* Build strong cross-functional partnerships to identify, escalate, and resolve operational issues and improvement opportunities.
* Set the strategic direction and oversee major projects across national and international locations, including distribution center layout changes, equipment needs, space utilization, capital expenses, major repairs, and related operational requirements.
* Manage domestic and international direct and indirect reporting teams to ensure processes and procedures are consistent across all facilities.
* Lead the annual budgeting process in partnership with DC Operations and Direct Sale Finance Teams and Sales Leadership.
* Stay current on information, technology, and trends affecting functional areas; promote innovation and make appropriate recommendations to executive leadership.
* Develop and execute a multi-year distribution technology and automation roadmap, including the evaluation and adoption of AI, robotics, material-handling automation, advanced analytics, and emerging distribution technologies where they provide measurable operational and financial value.
* Evaluate opportunities to automate manual and repetitive processes across receiving, put-away, inventory movement, picking, packing, sortation, shipping, and related distribution workflows.
* Establish business cases and success measures for major automation and technology investments, including productivity improvement, service impact, safety, capacity, labor requirements, operating cost, capital requirements, and return on investment.
* Partner with Information Technology, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, Human Resources, and external technology partners to successfully pilot, scale, and operationalize new distribution technologies across the network.
* Use data, predictive analytics, and AI-enabled decision support to improve demand and capacity planning, inventory positioning, workforce planning, asset utilization, operational visibility, and decision-making.
* Build a culture of innovation in which technology augments the workforce, improves safety and efficiency, and prepares the distribution organization for future operating requirements.
* Set the overall strategy for operational performance planning to drive quality standards and efficiency.
* Oversee and monitor safety and security in accordance with national and international requirements for facilities and employees. Ensure proper training and adherence to company requirements.
* Drive employment decisions and recommendations, including hiring, retention, improvement plans, transfers, promotions, corrective actions, terminations, and pay adjustments.
* Manage employee performance and support improvement through coaching, mentoring, and formal performance reviews.
* Recommend, plan, and implement employee training and skill development activities.
* Lead communication on company and departmental issues, priorities, and goals. Provide oversight of employee growth and development through weekly team meetings, regular one-on-one meetings, coaching, performance management, training, and company-sponsored learning opportunities.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities
  

* Demonstrated understanding of technical issues within a global distribution framework.
* Strong understanding of modern distribution technologies, including warehouse automation, robotics, AI, machine learning applications, advanced analytics, and automated material-handling solutions.
* Ability to translate emerging technology into practical operational use cases and measurable business outcomes rather than implementing technology for technology’s sake.
* Strong understanding of automation investment strategy, including business-case development, scalability, change management, operational readiness, and return on investment.
* Ability to lead transformation in environments where automated and traditional operations may need to coexist across different facilities.
* Strong project leadership and cross-functional leadership experience.
* Ability to think, plan, and execute strategically.
* Ability to influence and build consensus with executive leadership.
* Comfortable operating in ambiguity.
* Decisive and persuasive, with a strong sense of urgency and a proven ability to drive results.
* Strong organizational skills.
* Excellent analytical skills and technical capabilities.
* Willingness and ability to travel extensively, both nationally and internationally.

Working Environment/Safety Requirements
  
Role is based in Lawrenceville, GA.
  
Requires up to 50% travel across the U.S. and Canada.
  
Work includes distribution center, plant, and office environments, including corporate office interaction in Roswell, GA.
  
Must comply with all company safety, security, and site-specific requirements.
  
Experience/Qualifications
  

* 15 years of experience leading a large workforce in a high-volume, fast-paced global distribution or manufacturing network.
* Bachelor’s degree in business, supply chain operations, engineering, or a related field required; MBA preferred.
* Recognized thought leader and expert within business, supply chain, logistics, and/or global distribution disciplines.
* Experience developing, implementing, and delivering long-term distribution and supply chain strategies.
* Deep understanding of the work apparel business, including financials, products, services, and market dynamics.
* Technologically adept, with the ability to envision and oversee the implementation of technology-based solutions.
* Demonstrated experience developing or executing distribution automation, robotics, AI, advanced analytics, or digital transformation initiatives within complex, high-volume operations.
* Experience evaluating automation technologies and building investment recommendations based on operational benefit, scalability, capital requirements, and return on investment.
* Experience leading technology-enabled operational change at scale, including the people, process, training, and change-management requirements associated with automation.

Headquartered in Roswell, GA, Vestis® is the second largest provider in the industry with over 300,000 customer locations and approximately 20,000 teammates across North America. Vestis® is a leader in the B2B uniform and workplace supplies category. Vestis® provides clean and safe uniform services and workplace supplies to a broad range of North American customers from Fortune 500 companies to locally owned small businesses across a broad set of end markets. The Company’s comprehensive service offering includes a full-service uniform rental program, cleanroom and other specialty garment processing, floor mats, towels, linens, managed restroom services, first aid supplies and more.
  
  
Vestis® is an equal-opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. records.title: Sr. Director, Quality Operations
records.description:
**The Asahi Kasei Group operates with a commitment of creating for tomorrow. Our business sectors,** ***Materials, Homes, and Health Care*** **, contribute to the development of society by anticipating the changing needs of those around the world. We look for candidates that offer a fresh perspective and a variety of skills to help us achieve our commitment.**
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  
  
Asahi Kasei Therapeutics is the global specialty pharmaceutical business of Asahi Kasei. We are a commercial-stage company committed to positively impacting health by expanding therapeutic options that improve the lives of patients around the world. Drawing upon our strong heritage of scientific innovation, we aim to help reshape care in transplantation, nephrology, immunology, infectious diseases and other underserved conditions.  
  

**Job Description:**

  

The Senior Director of Quality Operations is a strategic and hands‑on leader responsible for ensuring the quality and compliance of all GMP/GDP activities executed internally and by external partners for the company’s products, supporting both clinical trials and commercial distribution, working with the VP of QA, QC and AD

  

This role provides oversight across CDMOs and testing labs, ensuring timely product disposition, investigation management, and quality support throughout the product lifecycle.

  

The base compensation range for this role is $230-260K. Base Compensation is influenced by many factors including, but not limited to: time in the role, previous experience, skills, knowledge, performance, work requirements, internal equity, and business / economic conditions.

  

The Senior Director QA Operations is accountable and responsible to:

* Ensure that the company's global Quality Management System (QMS), processes, and procedures required in the development, manufacture, supply and distribution and related activities are established, maintained and continuously improved in compliance with applicable laws and regulations, including but not necessarily limited to GMP and GDP.
* Provide global and independent Quality Management support, and in particular GMP and GDP oversight, leadership, expertise, reviews and as required quality approvals.
* Assure a satisfactory state of control and compliance with the AKTX QMS, and applicable GMP and GDP standards, authorizations, internal policies, procedures and protocols related to product for clinical trials and commercial manufacturing,
* Actively identify and communicate compliance issues or risks, develop and oversee plans to rectify issues or mitigate risks.

The Senior QA Director works in close collaboration with AKTX functional heads and process owners leading the development, supply and distribution of AKTX medicinal products.

  

**Tasks and responsibilities/accountabilities**

* Take an active role in development and delivery of AKTX strategy, objectives and targets.
* Support development of the QA unit and its way of working, budget, and deliverables in accordance with agreed corporate and individual objectives.
* Lead QA Operations and provide strategic leadership to QA operations staff by driving development, performance, coaching initiatives and ensuring optimal resource allocation to achieve organizational goals and deliver on targets, and objectives
* Collaborate within QA and with process owners, management and departments to establish, maintain and continually improve a fit-for-purpose, robust and effective global QMS.
* Act as owner of assigned business and quality management processes within the QMS and drive and ensure their suitability and effectiveness, and continual improvements.
* Provide oversight across CDMOs and service providers for clinical and commercial programs, ensuring timely product disposition, investigation management, and quality support throughout the product lifecycle.
* Serve as the quality lead in cross-functional CMC teams, partnering with MTO, QC/AD, Regulatory, Clinical, PAM and Supply Chain to ensure end-to-end GMP compliance
* Represent QA in governance and escalation forums for manufacturing investigations, supplier issues, or product quality events
* Own and continuously improve core quality systems including batch release, deviation/CAPA and change control and ensure scalability.
* Provide Quality Oversight, and support of:
  + Suppliers and other third parties involved in outsourced activities or procured material and services to AKTX, including development and follow up of quality and service agreements.
  + Assigned projects related to product and process development, supply and distribution of medicinal products.
  + Assigned computerized systems and other infrastructure within AKTX group.
* Support, and as agreed lead,
  + the management/coordination of regulatory inspections and audits by partners, related to AKTX QMS, and GMP and GDP activities.
  + inspection readiness and QA support during audits and health authority inspections at CDMOs
  + internal audits and audits of engaged suppliers and vendors for outsourced activities and of procured services, including planning, and delivery of the audit program.
  + investigations related to product complaints, issues, deviations, and other findings to identify root causes, corrections, risk mitigations, corrective or preventive actions in collaboration with related experts within the field.
* Support, as applicable, writing, review and approval of governing documentation such as protocols, applications and regulatory files related to Quality Management, and in particular GMP and GDP.
* Lead by example through ensuring own compliance with AKTX policies, values and procedures as well as promoting own team and wider AKTX to do so.
Maintain a contemporary knowledge of current industry trends, standards and methodologies within the area  

  

**Delegations**

* Authority to execute management approvals (or rejection) of governing, controlling and compliance documents and records, such as but not limited to procedures, protocols, reports, statements and methods, for processes owned by the QA unit and managed within AKTX QMS.
* Authority to execute quality and compliance (QA) approvals, consent or rejections of batches of medicinal products for use in clinical studies or intended for commercial distribution.
* Authority to execute quality and compliance (QA) approvals, consent or rejections of proposed changes, investigations of product complaints, deviations, or issues, and resulting corrections or corrective and preventive actions, related to supply, product or process development of medicinal products.
On behalf of AKTX, authority to approve Quality Agreements, including associated schedules, amendments and equivalent, with engaged suppliers, service providers, license partners and other third parties.  

  

**Competence requirements for the position (education and experience)**

* Bachelor's or Master's Degree in relevant applied sciences, e.g. pharmacy, medicine, chemistry, biology and/or engineering (pharmaceutical, chemical or biotechnology).
At least 10 years working experience in quality management, assurance or control, supply chain, regulatory affairs and/or product or process development of medicinal products or other life-science related industry (e.g. medical devices).

records.title: Vice President of Manufacturing & Operations
records.description:
For more than three decades, Design West Technologies Inc. has been a trusted Department of War (DoW) partner, delivering mission-critical engineering and rugged manufacturing solutions supporting our nation's warfighters. Building on this defense heritage, DWT is embracing a growth-oriented, start-up culture aligned with evolving DoW opportunities. Based in Tustin, CA, DWT seeks an experienced Vice President of Manufacturing & Operations to lead manufacturing, production, supply chain, facilities, and operational functions. The ideal candidate brings proven aerospace, defense, or complex manufacturing leadership experience, combining strategic vision with hands-on execution to drive growth, organizational transformation, operational excellence, and accountability.

### **Position Overview**

As VP of Manufacturing & Operations, you will provide strategic leadership while maintaining hands-on engagement across daily manufacturing execution, production performance, and operational priorities. You will develop and scale DWT's manufacturing capabilities, integrating people, processes, technology, and resources to drive operational excellence and sustainable growth. You will have executive accountability for manufacturing performance, P&L, capacity, supply chain, quality, safety, and customer delivery while ensuring operational capabilities support current and future business objectives.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Manufacturing & Operations Excellence**

  

* Lead manufacturing functions, including production, planning, engineering, facilities, maintenance, and warehouse operations.
* Scale manufacturing capabilities, capacity, and infrastructure to support new program launches, increased customer demand, and long-term business growth.
* Drive operational excellence through Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and 5S, improving throughput, productivity, automation, equipment utilization, and capacity while establishing KPIs, corrective actions, and scalable processes.

**Supply Chain Management**

* Lead Supply Chain, Procurement, and Production Planning to ensure alignment with business objectives and customer commitments.
* Optimize procurement, supplier performance, material availability, lead times, and inventory while controlling excess and obsolete materials.
* Align production schedules with customer demand, program requirements, and manufacturing capacity while strengthening supply chain resilience through proactive risk mitigation

**Quality, Safety & Compliance**

* Partner with Quality and Engineering leadership to ensure manufacturing processes meet customer, regulatory, and quality requirements while promoting safety and accountability.
* Ensure compliance with AS9100, ISO 9001, ITAR, OSHA, and government-contracting requirements while driving audit readiness, corrective actions, defect reduction, and continuous improvement.

**Financial & Business Strategy**

* Own manufacturing P&L performance, including operating budgets, financial forecasts, labor costs, cost controls, capital expenditures, margins, and profitability, ensuring financial accountability and alignment with business objectives.
* Partner with the President and Finance leadership on operating plans, financial forecasts, capital investments, and performance metrics.
* Drive margin improvement through operational efficiency, automation, resource optimization, and process redesign while supporting strategic growth and business expansion.

**Cross-Functional & Organizational Leadership**

* Partner with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to align operational priorities, resources, and manufacturing objectives with business strategy.
* Collaborate with Engineering and Program Management to support production readiness, program execution, customer commitments, and new business opportunities.
* Build high-performing teams through clear accountability, coaching, mentoring, succession planning, and leadership development while fostering collaboration, trust, and continuous improvement.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or related field.
* 12–15+ years of progressive manufacturing and operations leadership experience, including at least five years in senior leadership overseeing multiple functions.
* Proven experience managing complex manufacturing operations, P&L, budgets, capital investments, production planning, capacity, quality, delivery, and supply chain.
* Demonstrated success in Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, operational strategy, business growth, organizational transformation, and cross-functional leadership.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in aerospace, defense, electronics, precision, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments, preferably involving PCBA, microelectronics, ruggedized electronics, cable and harness assemblies, or complex electromechanical products.
* Experience scaling operations, integrating acquisitions, or leading organizational transformation. MBA, Master's degree, or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification preferred.

**Are you ready to join our team?**

At DWT, we value teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement as we build for the future.

Eaton’s Electrical Sector America’s business is curretly hiring for a VP of Continuous Improvement & Lean. This role can be based at Eaton’s Cleveland or Pittsburgh office. Relocation within hiring country is offered. 50 percent travel is anticipated.

Reporting directly to the SVP of Operations, Electrical Sector – Americas (ESA), the VP of CI & Lean is the senior executive accountable for the vision, strategy, and results of the Eaton Continuous Improvement System (ECIS) across the $16B ESA business, spanning 60 manufacturing sites and 14 divisions. This role sets the multi-year Lean transformation agenda, builds continuous improvement into the sector's strategic and annual profit plans, and holds the business accountable for measurable improvement in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth.

The VP leads and develops the ESA CI team, defines the sector-wide operating model, standards, and governance the team deploys, and serves as a strategic advisor to the ESA leadership team. Rather than leading deployment within a division, this role directs CI resources to the highest-value opportunities, owns the sector's CI talent pipeline, and shapes a Lean leadership culture at the executive level. The VP also represents ESA in enterprise CI forums, partnering with Corporate CI & Quality to align standards and scale best practices across Eaton.

**Job Responsibilities:**
-------------------------

* Defines the multi-year ESA Lean and continuous improvement vision, strategy, and roadmap, and integrates it into the sector's strategic plan and annual profit plan.
* Owns the ECIS operating model for ESA: sets the standards, maturity expectations, and governance that the CI team deploys across divisions, functions, and sites.
* Leads, coaches, and develops the ESA CI team; sets objectives, allocates CI resources, and holds the team accountable for results.
* Chairs the Divisional CI Council across all ESA divisions and leads sector-level performance reviews, establishing the operating cadence that links CI results to business performance.
* Accountable for the ESA cost-out and productivity commitments delivered through CI; builds the sector project pipeline and validates financial impact.
* Serves as strategic advisor to the SVP of Operations and the ESA leadership team, prioritizing the transformation initiatives with the greatest business value.
* Sponsors large-scale, cross-divisional transformations (e.g., footprint changes, acquisition integrations, and Lean in office and transactional processes).
* Builds the sector CI talent strategy: capability standards, certification pathways (e.g., ASCEND X, PME), succession planning, and rotation of high-potential leaders through CI roles.
* Coaches ESA executives on Lean leadership behaviors and role-models a culture of accountability and continuous improvement from the top.
* Sets sector maturity targets and owns the EBSA and OpA assessment strategy; reviews results with leadership and directs closure of systemic gaps.
* Represents ESA in enterprise CI forums; partners with Corporate CI & Quality to shape Eaton-wide standards and scale proven practices across sectors.
* Manages the ESA CI function budget and champions digital and data analytics tools that accelerate improvement.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

Required Qualifications:  

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution.
* Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Quality, or Operations
* Minimum 5 years leading leaders (managers or directors) at a multi-site, division, or business-unit level
* Proven track record leading Lean transformations that delivered measurable financial results, preferably in a multi-division manufacturing environment
* Professional experience in a global matrixed organization
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc

Preferred Qualifications:  

* Master's degree or MBA preferred

Position Success Criteria:  

* Expert-level command of Lean and Six Sigma; Master Black Belt or Black Belt certification required
* Experience designing, governing, and maturing a business operating system and maturity model at scale
* Strong business and financial acumen: builds cost-out and productivity plans, quantifies impact, and ties CI results to the P&L
* Experience designing CI talent, certification, and capability programs across a large, multi-site organization
* Applies Lean to both manufacturing and office/transactional processes
* Executive presence; a trusted advisor who influences, challenges, and aligns senior executives
* Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing teams of senior CI leaders

records.description:
About Us

  

Skydweller Aero Inc. is a transatlantic, cutting-edge aerospace company developing solar-powered aircraft solutions capable of perpetual flight while carrying heavy and powerful payloads. Building on technology from the longest continuous renewably powered flight program in history, this fast-growing company is creating a new class of unmanned aircraft. It combines the persistence of geosynchronous satellites with the sensing capabilities and flexibility of a large airborne platform. Skydweller Aero Inc. has its global and US headquarters in Oklahoma City, with European operations headquartered in Spain.

Role Summary

  

As Skydweller prepares to move from development toward aircraft production, we are looking for an experienced manufacturing executive to build and lead our production organization. This role is based in **Oklahoma City, OK** and reports to the Chief Operating Officer.

The Vice President, Manufacturing & Production will own all aircraft production operations: final assembly, systems integration, avionics installation, production testing, factory operations and aircraft delivery. You will lead the organization as we scale from prototype and low-rate initial production into sustained manufacturing.

We are looking for a hands-on aerospace manufacturing leader with a proven track record of building production organizations, improving factory performance and delivering complex aircraft in FAA-regulated environments.

**Why join:** Most manufacturing leadership roles optimize an existing production system. This one builds it. You will establish the manufacturing organization, develop the factory workforce, and scale production of one of the most ambitious autonomous aircraft programs in aerospace.

Responsibilities

  

**Production leadership**

  

* Lead all aircraft production and manufacturing operations.
* Drive safe, efficient and repeatable aircraft production.
* Build and lead a high-performing manufacturing organization, with clear management systems, metrics and operating rhythms.
* Foster a culture of accountability, safety, quality and continuous improvement.

  

**Assembly and integration**

* Oversee final assembly, systems and electrical integration, avionics installation and aircraft completion.
* Ensure aircraft are built to engineering, quality and regulatory requirements.
* Drive production readiness and resolve manufacturing constraints and bottlenecks.

  

**Production planning and execution**

* Own execution of the Master Production Schedule.
* Lead production planning, labor allocation and resource management.
* Set capacity plans that support production-rate growth.
* Monitor factory performance and drive throughput, productivity and efficiency improvements.

  

**Production testing and acceptance**

* Lead production acceptance testing and ground test operations.
* Coordinate production readiness with Engineering, Quality, Flight Operations and Program Management.
* Ensure aircraft move smoothly from production through acceptance and delivery.

  

**Regulatory compliance and quality**

* Ensure compliance with FAA Part 21 production requirements and the company quality management system.
* Maintain production configuration control and manufacturing documentation discipline.
* Support internal, regulatory and customer audits and certification activities.
* Partner with Quality leadership to improve first-pass yield.

  

**Growth and scale-up**

* Develop the manufacturing infrastructure, facilities and staffing plans needed for higher production rates.
* Implement lean manufacturing and operational excellence initiatives.

  

**People leadership**

* Recruit, develop and mentor production leaders and technical staff.
* Establish workforce development and skills-training programs.
* Build strong partnerships across Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Flight Operations and Program Management.

  

Success Measures

You will be measured on aircraft delivery performance, production schedule attainment, factory throughput, labor productivity, manufacturing cost, quality and first-pass yield, safety, production-rate readiness, and workforce development and retention.

Required Qualifications

  

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Aerospace, Operations or a related technical field.
* 15+ years of progressive aerospace manufacturing leadership experience, including 10+ years leading production organizations in aerospace, defense, aviation or another highly regulated industry.
* Proven experience scaling manufacturing from development, prototype or low-rate production to higher-rate production.
* Experience leading large, cross-functional manufacturing organizations.
* Strong understanding of production planning, factory operations, quality systems and manufacturing performance metrics.
* Experience implementing lean manufacturing and operational excellence initiatives.
* Excellent communication, leadership and organizational skills.

  

Preferred Qualifications

  

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business or Operations.
* FAA Part 21 production experience and experience with certified aircraft manufacturing programs.
* Experience leading final assembly and aircraft integration organizations.
* Experience supporting aircraft certification, conformity and production acceptance.
* Background in autonomous aircraft, UAS, defense aviation or advanced aerospace systems.
* Experience building greenfield or fast-growing manufacturing operations.
* Composite aircraft manufacturing experience.
* AS9100 quality system experience.

records.description:

* Lead major initiatives that improve processes across departments, especially where work, systems, and ownership break down between teams.

* Lead on-site discovery with leaders and frontline teams to understand how work really gets done.

* Make structured problem solving a habit at every level of the organization.

records.description:
Director of Operations, North America

**About Us:**

We are committed to finding smart solutions that enable an intelligent and seamless world. Our success as a world-class leader in technology has evolved from humble beginnings. In 1896, the enterprising father and son team of A.J. and George A. Briggs partnered with S.A. Buffington, a Chicago lawyer, to establish Chicago Telephone Supply Company (later to become CTS).

Today, CTS is a leading designer and manufacturer of sensors, actuators, and electronic components for suppliers and original equipment manufacturers. We have over 20 locations in 12 countries and more than 3,500 employees. Our innovative sensing, connectivity, and motion solutions offer a diverse range of products across diversified end markets including transportation, medical, aerospace and defense, and industrial. We are at the forefront of supporting innovating life-changing technology, focusing on quality to keep people safe, healthy, and happy.

**Position Summary**

The Operations Director, North America provides strategic and operational leadership for the regional manufacturing network, ensuring safe, compliant, cost-effective, and customer-focused execution across assigned sites. This position requires a hands-on, execution-focused leader who can standardize operating processes, improve performance variability across sites, coach plant leadership teams, and convert strategic business priorities into measurable operational and financial results. This role is accountable for safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, customer responsiveness, capital execution, and people development across the North America plants.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the North America manufacturing operations network, establishing clear priorities, standard work, operating cadences, and performance expectations across assigned sites.
* Own regional operational performance and operational excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, customer responsiveness, and employee engagement metrics.
* Partner with business unit leadership, plant managers, supply chain, quality, engineering, finance, HR, and commercial teams to align operating plans with customer demand and business objectives.
* Establish and reinforce standardized operating processes across the region while allowing appropriate site-level flexibility based on product, customer, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive a disciplined daily, weekly, and monthly management system to review performance, identify gaps, assign accountability, and ensure timely corrective actions.
* Translate operational actions into financial outcomes by improving margin performance, controlling costs, optimizing resources, and partnering with finance on budgeting and forecasting.
* Provide leadership, coaching, and development for plant managers and site leadership teams, building a strong succession pipeline and culture of accountability.
* Champion a zero-harm safety culture and ensure compliance with company EHS standards and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Ensure customer requirements are met or exceeded, including on-time delivery, responsiveness, quality performance, and timely resolution of escalations.
* Lead continuous improvement and Lean deployment across the region, including visual management, standard work, 5S, value stream improvement, structured problem solving, and waste reduction.
* Reduce performance variability between sites by deploying common metrics, operating reviews, best-practice sharing, and targeted improvement plans.
* Drive structural cost improvement through labor efficiency, material yield, scrap reduction, inventory optimization, manufacturing productivity, and capacity utilization.
* Review and approve capital project proposals, support business cases, and ensure approved capital expenditures are implemented on time, on budget, and with expected returns.
* Support digital manufacturing, automation, data transparency, and ERP-enabled process improvements where they improve operational control, productivity, and decision-making.
* Ensure manufacturing equipment, facilities, and processes are maintained and utilized effectively to produce high-quality products at competitive cost.
* Maintain strong governance of quality management systems, audit readiness, corrective actions, and certification requirements applicable to assigned sites.
* Support new product introductions, transfers, footprint changes, and capacity expansion projects through disciplined planning and cross-functional execution.
* Establish strong communication routines with site and regional teams to reinforce priorities, escalate risks, and ensure alignment on business-critical actions.
* Ensure compliance with corporate policies, business unit procedures, internal controls, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

**Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Strong multi-site manufacturing leadership experience with demonstrated ability to deliver results through plant leadership teams.
* Deep knowledge of Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, structured problem solving, visual management, standard work, and daily management systems.
* Strong business acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, P&L management, productivity analysis, labor planning, capital investment justification, and margin improvement.
* Demonstrated ability to standardize processes across sites while adapting execution to local operating realities and customer requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence across operations, supply chain, quality, engineering, finance, HR, and commercial functions.
* Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to engage shop-floor teams, plant leadership, executives, and customers.
* Ability to prioritize competing objectives, manage risk, lead through change, and make timely decisions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Proven track record of building high-performing teams, developing leaders, improving retention, and creating succession plans for critical operations roles.
* High integrity, sound judgment, and commitment to safety, quality, compliance, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business Administration, or a related field required; master’s degree or MBA preferred.
* Minimum of 12 to 15 years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including leadership of complex plant operations.
* Minimum of 5 years of multi-site operations leadership experience preferred, with accountability for regional performance across multiple plants or business units.
* Experience leading manufacturing operations in North America, including cross-border or multi-country operating environments, preferred.
* Experience with P&L ownership, operating budgets, capital planning, productivity programs, operational KPI management, and financial performance improvement required.
* Demonstrated experience with Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or equivalent continuous improvement systems required; certification preferred.
* Experience with ERP systems, manufacturing data, automation initiatives, and digital operations tools preferred.
* Experience in automotive, electronics, sensors, mechatronics, industrial manufacturing, or similarly regulated manufacturing environments preferred.
* Bilingual English/Spanish capability preferred, particularly for roles supporting Mexico operations.

**Physical Demands**

* Must follow applicable safety requirements while visiting manufacturing areas, including use of required personal protective equipment.
* Ability to work several hours at a computer and participate in meetings across multiple time zones.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed, approximately 35% to 50% depending on business requirements.

**Working Environment**

* Plant, office, and travel-based environment across North America manufacturing locations.

The Professor of Practice & Manufacturing Extension Program Director provides leadership for the Center for Manufacturing Excellence's (CME) manufacturing extension and industry engagement activities. The position connects University expertise, educational resources, faculty, and students with manufacturers throughout Mississippi and the region to strengthen organizational performance, workforce capability, operational excellence, and competitiveness. As a Professor of Practice, the individual also contributes to CME's academic mission through teaching, applied scholarship, student engagement, and curriculum development. The position is practice oriented and is not expected to conduct traditional academic research. The rank of the Professor of Practice appointment will be determined based on the selected candidate’s qualifications and relevant professional experience.

  

The Manufacturing Extension Program Director role will develop, lead, and grow a comprehensive manufacturing extension program responsive to the needs of manufacturers and other industry partners. Working collaboratively with CME faculty and staff, industry, and economic and workforce development partners, the incumbent identifies industry needs and develops training, technical assistance, professional education, applied projects, and other services to address those needs.

  

The position will emphasize industry engagement, operational excellence and continuous improvement, applied problem solving, external funding, professional and graduate education, and measurable extension impact. ***Ready to be part of our team?***
