**Summary:** The Plant Manager is the senior site leader with full accountability for overall plant performance, overseeing all operations across the entire site, including continuous panel line manufacturing and ancillary processes. This role is responsible for aligning people, processes, and strategy to ensure the site produces high-quality products at standard manufacturing costs in a safe, efficient, and profitable manner.

Success is achieved through the direct leadership and development of subordinate managers and supervisors, while building a strong, engaged organization capable of delivering reliable operational and business results.

**Essential Duties**

**Operational Performance & KPI Accountability**

* Own and drive plant performance against key metrics, including safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, and employee engagement.
* Translate corporate and regional objectives into clear plant-level goals, priorities, and operating plans.
* Ensure disciplined execution of daily management systems, standard work, and KPI reviews.
* Hold leaders and teams accountable for results while removing barriers and providing necessary resources.
* Ensure customer requirements are met through effective production planning, quality control, and on-time delivery.

**Organizational Leadership & People Development**

* Provide visible, values-based leadership that sets clear expectations for behavior, performance, and accountability across all levels of the plant.
* Lead, coach, and develop managers and supervisors, ensuring they are equipped to lead teams, solve problems, and deliver results through others.
* Build a high performing leadership team through effective hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, and succession planning.
* Foster an inclusive, respectful, and engaged workplace culture where safety, quality, and continuous improvement are shared responsibilities.
* Communicate effectively and consistently with employees, reinforcing vision, priorities, and alignment to company objectives.
* Partner with Human Resources to address employee relations matters, labor strategy (where applicable), and workforce planning.

**Safety, Quality & Compliance Leadership**

* Champion a proactive safety culture by modeling safe behaviors, enforcing standards, leading incident investigations, and driving corrective actions.
* Ensure compliance with all regulatory, environmental, safety, and labor requirements.
* Maintain adherence to quality standards and lead continuous improvement efforts to reduce defects and variability.
* Act as the site authority for audits, inspections, and regulatory interactions.

**Continuous Improvement & Change Leadership**

* Lead lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives that improve performance and build organizational capability.
* Drive root-cause problem solving and data-driven decision making.
* Lead change initiatives effectively by engaging stakeholders, communicating clearly, and sustaining improvements over time.
* Balance short-term operational execution with long-term capability and talent development.

**Financial & Strategic Stewardship**

* Maintain full accountability for plant financial performance, including labor, operating costs, and capital investments.
* Participate in budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning. • Identify and mitigate operational and business risks to ensure continuity and stability.
* Evaluate and prepare CAPEX recommendations.
* Serve as the primary site representative to corporate partners, customers, and external stakeholders.

**General Responsibilities**

* Maintain accurate records and reporting across all operational areas.
* Participate in meetings, training, and development activities as required.
* Follow the Group Code of Conduct and Group Compliance.
* Follow Compliance requirements per “KNA-SOP-1705 Compliance Roles and Responsibilities.”
* Performs all other duties as assigned.

* 10 years of manufacturing experience, ideally in a continuous product environment.
* Knowledge and practice of modern manufacturing techniques.
* Knowledge of labor laws.
* Knowledge of the construction industry.
* Know the operation of the panel producing equipment and accessory equipment.
* Ability to calculate figures/amounts.
* Good oral and written communication skills.
* Ability to train and instruct employees.
* Good analytical problem-solving skills.
* Strong Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
* Proven track record of lean manufacturing experience.
* Must be highly proficient in all Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and Outlook.

**Personal Attributes**

The successful candidate will exhibit the following attributes:

**Senior Site Leadership**

* Serves as the visible, accountable plant leader, shaping performance, culture, and behavior.
* Builds long-term organizational capability while balancing operational urgency with people and succession needs.

**People-Centered, Results-Driven**

* Delivers results through strong managers and supervisors, not direct control.
* Sets clear expectations, fosters accountability and trust, and coaches leaders to manage performance fairly and effectively.

**Operational & Strategic Focus**

* Aligns KPIs and execution with business objectives, customer commitments, and financial results.
* Uses data, standard work, and problem-solving while maintaining both short-term execution and long-term excellence.

**Comfort with Complexity**

* Makes sound decisions in dynamic, ambiguous environments with competing priorities.
* Leads calmly and decisively through disruptions, pressure, and change.

**Influence-Based Leadership**

* Is visible on the factory floor, approachable, and accessible to team members, fostering open dialogue and trust.
* Builds alignment through credibility and relationships rather than authority.
* Effectively influences cross-functional partners and gains buy-in at all organizational levels.

**Change & Continuous Improvement**

* Champions continuous improvement as a performance system and leadership mindset.
* Engages teams in change and sustains gains through embedded leadership routines.

**Safety, Values & Integrity**

* Models personal accountability for safety, quality, and ethical behavior.
* Treats safety, respect for people, and values as non-negotiable standards.

**Executive Presence**

* Communicates clearly and confidently across all levels.
* Represents the site professionally with corporate leaders, customers, and external stakeholders.

**Physical Demands:** The physical demands described here represent those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform key responsibilities.

**Body Movement & Posture:** Standing or walking for extended periods, frequent bending, stooping, crouching, or kneeling, climbing stairs or ladders, crawling, or working in confined spaces.

**Manual Dexterity & Handling:** Using hands and fingers to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects, operating machinery or tools with precision, repetitive motion tasks (e.g., packaging, sorting).

**PLANT MANAGER**

**Icon Fixtures | Multi-Facility Manufacturing Operations | St. Louis Area (Hazelwood, MO)**

About Icon

Icon Fixtures designs and builds custom fixtures, millwork, and full environments for retail, restaurant, hospitality, banking, and museum clients across North America and internationally, from single-store orders to 100+ location rollouts. Our in-house production centers on custom wood cabinetry and architectural millwork, along with metal fabrication and solid surface components.

The Role

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Plant Manager to lead manufacturing, warehouse, and assembly operations across three local facilities. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, you will oversee approximately 30 employees through supervisors and team leaders, with significant room to grow the organization as we expand.

This is a role for a builder. The right leader will establish the scheduling systems, standards, and leadership structure that allow Icon to scale without sacrificing quality.

What You Will Do

* Lead manufacturing across all three facilities, including woodworking, cabinetry, millwork, metal, solid surface, finishing, and assembly.

* Build and own production schedules that reflect project deadlines, material availability, labor capacity, and equipment, and identify problems before they affect delivery.

* Run warehouse and assembly operations: receiving, inventory control, material flow between facilities, and preparation for shipment and installation.

* Coordinate material purchasing and production priorities with project management, engineering, and logistics.

* Develop supervisors and team leaders into a management team that runs daily operations independently; recruit, train, and retain skilled employees.

* Set and enforce quality standards against shop drawings and specifications, and reduce defects, rework, and waste.

* Manage labor costs, overtime, and operating budgets; track KPIs and report on performance, capacity, and staffing.

* Lead lean and continuous improvement initiatives, including facility layouts, workflows, and equipment utilization.

* Own safety and facilities: OSHA compliance, combustible dust and dust collection (NFPA 652/664), finishing and spray booth compliance, and preventive maintenance.

What You Bring

* 7+ years of manufacturing leadership, preferably in custom manufacturing, cabinetry, millwork, architectural woodworking, or commercial fixture production.

* Experience managing multiple departments or facilities and 30+ employees through supervisors and team leaders.

* Strong command of project-based production scheduling, labor planning, and manufacturing costs.

* Experience overseeing warehouse, inventory, material handling, and assembly operations.

* Ability to read and interpret shop drawings, production drawings, and specifications.

* Familiarity with ERP systems and production tracking tools.

* A proven record of developing people and building accountability.

Preferred Qualifications

* Retail store fixture manufacturing experience.

* Knowledge of CNC panel processing, edgebanding, and cabinet construction; familiarity with metal fabrication and solid surface.

* Experience implementing lean manufacturing.

* Experience scaling operations during periods of rapid growth.

What Success Looks Like

* Consistent, efficient operations across all three facilities.

* Projects delivered on schedule and within production budgets.

* Reliable schedules and predictable workflow.

* Reduced waste, rework, and unnecessary overtime.

* Strong department leaders and an accountable workforce.

* High standards of workmanship, quality, and workplace safety.

Why Icon

You will have significant influence over Icon’s manufacturing operations, workforce development, and future growth, with the opportunity to grow into a Director-level role. We are looking for a hands-on, results-oriented leader who understands custom manufacturing, develops people, and takes ownership of operational performance.

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
**Compensation Range:**

$122,800 - $204,600

**Plant Manager**

Department: Operations / Manufacturing

Reports To: Director of Operations

Direct Reports: Production Managers, Facilities Manager, and other assigned manufacturing leadership

Scope: Three manufacturing buildings / multi-product HVAC manufacturing operation

**Position**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, and day-to-day execution of manufacturing operations across three buildings within a large HVAC manufacturing facility. This position provides hands-on leadership to ensure the plant safely produces high-quality products on schedule, at the required volume and cost, while developing a strong culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

The Plant Manager is responsible for coordinating production activities across multiple manufacturing processes and buildings, including assembly, sheet metal fabrication, welding, piping/refrigeration, testing, material flow, and final product completion.

The successful candidate will establish clear operating standards, drive cross-functional accountability, develop manufacturing leadership, remove operational constraints, and ensure the plant has the people, processes, equipment, and infrastructure required to support current production and future growth.

This position is expected to be highly visible on the manufacturing floor and serves as the primary operational leader responsible for translating business objectives into daily execution.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Plant Leadership & Operational Execution**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for manufacturing operations across all three buildings.
* Establish daily, weekly, and monthly operating priorities aligned with business requirements.
* Ensure production plans are executed safely, efficiently, and according to customer commitments.
* Maintain strong communication and coordination between buildings and manufacturing departments.
* Establish clear ownership and accountability for production performance.
* Lead daily plant operating reviews and ensure corrective actions are completed.
* Identify and remove constraints affecting throughput, capacity, quality, or delivery.
* Maintain appropriate production capacity, staffing, equipment, and infrastructure to support business growth.
* Ensure standardized processes are consistently followed across all buildings.
* Maintain a strong management presence on the manufacturing floor.

**2. Production Management**

* Lead Production Managers and ensure effective management of production personnel.
* Establish production priorities based on customer demand, capacity, material availability, and schedule requirements.
* Ensure production schedules are achieved while balancing labor, equipment, materials, and testing capacity.
* Monitor production flow from fabrication through final assembly and testing.
* Develop and maintain effective production metrics and visual management systems.
* Identify bottlenecks and implement corrective actions to improve throughput.
* Ensure appropriate escalation processes are in place when production performance is at risk.
* Coordinate production activities between the three buildings to maximize overall plant capacity.

**3. Safety, Environmental & Compliance**

* Establish safety as the facility’s highest operational priority.
* Partner with EHS leadership to maintain a strong safety culture across all three buildings.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental regulations, company requirements, and applicable industry standards.
* Drive accountability for safe work practices at all levels of the organization.
* Ensure timely investigation and corrective action following incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions.
* Support programs designed to reduce injuries, ergonomic risks, environmental impacts, and workplace hazards.
* Ensure employees receive appropriate safety training and understand their responsibilities.

**4. Quality**

* Partner with Quality leadership to ensure products meet customer, engineering, and company requirements.
* Establish accountability for first-time quality and defect prevention.
* Drive reduction of scrap, rework, warranty issues, and production defects.
* Ensure quality issues are rapidly escalated and contained.
* Support root-cause analysis and corrective-action processes.
* Promote quality at the source rather than relying on downstream inspection.
* Maintain compliance with the plant's quality management system and ISO requirements.

**5. Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead the implementation and sustainability of Lean Manufacturing Principles throughout all three buildings.
* Establish a culture of continuous improvement and employee involvement.
* Drive 5S, visual management, standardized work, problem solving, waste elimination, and flow improvements.
* Support Value Stream Mapping and improvement of end-to-end product flow.
* Establish measurable improvement targets for productivity, quality, delivery, inventory, and cost.
* Partner with Lean/Manufacturing Engineering leadership to prioritize improvement projects based on business impact.
* Ensure Lean improvements are sustained through management systems and standard work.
* Develop frontline leaders capable of independently identifying and solving operational problems.

**6. People Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Develop a high-performing manufacturing leadership team.
* Establish clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Coach and develop Production Managers, Supervisors, and other manufacturing leaders.
* Identify organizational capability gaps and work with Human Resources to develop staffing and development plans.
* Support workforce planning and hiring activities necessary to meet production requirements.
* Establish effective onboarding and training processes for new employees.
* Develop succession plans for key manufacturing positions.
* Promote employee engagement, teamwork, ownership, and accountability.
* Address performance issues promptly and consistently.

**7. Capacity & Business Growth**

* Develop manufacturing capacity plans to support current and future customer demand.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Finance, Materials, and other functions to identify capacity requirements.
* Evaluate labor, equipment, floor space, testing, utilities, and infrastructure requirements.
* Support capital planning and justification for new equipment and facility improvements.
* Ensure new production areas and buildings are effectively integrated into the overall manufacturing system.
* Develop ramp-up plans for new products, programs, and production transfers.
* Ensure the plant can scale production without compromising safety, quality, or delivery performance.

**8. Cross-Functional Leadership**

Work closely with:

* Director of Operations
* Production
* Materials
* Production Planning
* Logistics
* Quality
* EHS
* Lean / Manufacturing Engineering
* Facilities
* Maintenance
* Engineering
* Finance
* Human Resources
* Supply Chain
* Sales / Customer teams

Ensure cross-functional issues are identified early, assigned to the appropriate owner, and driven to resolution.

**9. Facilities, Equipment & Infrastructure**

* Partner with Facilities and Maintenance leadership to ensure buildings, utilities, production equipment, cranes, test infrastructure, and other critical assets support production requirements.
* Establish preventive and predictive maintenance expectations.
* Ensure critical production equipment has appropriate contingency plans.
* Support capital equipment selection, installation, commissioning, and production launch.
* Ensure facility expansion projects are integrated into manufacturing operations with minimal disruption to production.

**10. Performance Management & Accountability**

Establish and maintain a plant operating system based on measurable performance.

Key performance indicators should include:

Safety

* Recordable incident rate
* Lost-time incidents
* Near misses
* Safety observations
* Corrective-action closure

Quality

* First-pass yield
* Scrap
* Rework
* Customer defects
* Warranty / quality escapes

Delivery

* On-time delivery
* Schedule attainment
* Production attainment
* Manufacturing lead time
* Test-bay utilization / throughput

Productivity

* Labor productivity
* Units per labor hour
* OEE where applicable
* Direct labor efficiency
* Throughput

Cost

* Manufacturing cost
* Labor variance
* Scrap cost
* Overtime
* Cost of poor quality

Lean

* 5S performance
* Kaizen completion
* Standard work compliance
* Improvement savings
* Value-stream performance

The Plant Manager will ensure performance is reviewed routinely and that corrective actions have clearly identified owners and due dates.

**Leadership Expectations**

The Plant Manager is expected to:

* Lead from the floor rather than from the office.
* Establish a culture of accountability without creating a culture of blame.
* Make decisions based on facts and data.
* Escalate issues early rather than allowing problems to become emergencies.
* Develop leaders instead of personally solving every problem.
* Maintain a strong focus on safety and quality while driving production.
* Create alignment between the three buildings rather than allowing them to operate as independent plants.
* Establish consistent standards and expectations across the operation.
* Communicate clearly with employees, leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Demonstrate urgency while maintaining disciplined problem solving.
* Build an organization capable of supporting significant business growth.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field preferred.
* 7+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 3+ years of plant or multi-department manufacturing management experience.
* Experience managing large manufacturing organizations, multiple production areas, and facilities.
* Experience in HVAC, refrigeration, industrial equipment, sheet metal, welding, assembly, or related manufacturing strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience managing significant production growth or plant expansion.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Demonstrated experience managing safety, quality, delivery, and cost performance.
* Strong financial and business acumen.
* Experience developing and leading supervisors and managers.
* Strong communication and organizational skills.
* Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth manufacturing environment.

records.description:
Description:

LALA US Omaha Dairy manufactures yogurt smoothies and pourable sour cream. The facility provides a clean work environment, well-lit, highly automated production facility and career advancement opportunities. LALA US provides a competitive total compensation package including:

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401k with company match
* Vacation and Personal time off
* 10 paid holidays
* Company-paid life, AD&D, short-term disability and long-term disability insurance
* Employee Assistance Program

The Plant Manager is a senior leader responsible for planning, directing, and controlling activities of a plant to accomplish budgeted operational and financial objectives. Directs all functions at the plant including production, quality control, finance, purchasing, inventory control, manufacturing, engineering, and employee relations. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, data-driven leader capable of scaling production capacity, optimizing labor efficiency, managing complex capital projects, and building a high-performing, engaged workforce.

This role is responsible for the achievement of all operational financial goals. The responsibility also includes establishing and managing operational policies and procedures, creating and maintaining a safe and quality-minded work environment, and fostering the development of a well-trained and motivated work force at all levels.

**Core Responsibilities**

**1. People leadership, talent development & labor relations**

* Recruit, mentor, and evaluate department manager, superintendent and shift supervisors, establishing clear accountability and succession plans.
* Foster positive employee relations, high retention, and strong shop-floor morale through transparent communication, town halls, and recognition programs.
* Manage collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance resolution, and constructive relationships with union leadership.

**2. Production & operational execution**

* Direct multi-shift manufacturing operations to consistently achieve daily, weekly, and monthly production schedules and On-Time In-Full delivery targets.
* Monitor and improve key performance indicators, including Overall Equipment Effectiveness, scrap rates, yield, labor variance, and cycle times.
* Optimize production scheduling, capacity planning, and bottleneck management in partnership with Supply Chain and Materials teams.

**3. Financial management & P&L ownership**

* Develop, manage, and justify the annual plant operating budget, focusing on direct/indirect labor costs, raw material utilization, and overhead absorption.
* Track, analyze, and drive corrective actions on manufacturing cost variances, specifically Material Usage Variance, Labor Efficiency Variance, Scrap/Yield losses to protect margins.
* Partner with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain to investigate unfavorable material usage variances caused by Bill of Materials inaccuracies, machine calibration drift, or substandard raw materials.
* Conduct monthly financial variance reviews with corporate finance to identify cost-saving opportunities and mitigate inflationary pressures.

**4. Continuous improvement & operational excellence**

* Embed Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies (CILA, Centerline, 5S, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, TPM, SMED) into daily floor operations.
* Lead cross-functional continuous improvement events aimed at eliminating waste, reducing changeover times, and improving throughput.
* Leverage Manufacturing Execution Systems and ERP data to drive predictive decision-making and real-time floor visibility.

**5. Environmental, health, and safety leadership**

* Champion a zero-incident safety culture by enforcing strict adherence to OSHA regulations, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures, and company safety policies.
* Lead root-cause investigations for all near-misses, recordable incidents, and environmental excursions, ensuring timely corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
* Oversee environmental compliance, including EPA permitting, hazardous waste disposal, emissions monitoring, and sustainability targets.

**6. Quality assurance & regulatory compliance**

* Partner with the Quality Manager to reduce Customer Complaints, Cost of Poor Quality, and internal rework.
* Ensure the facility maintains strict compliance with industry quality standards (GMP, & SQF).
* Lead internal, customer, and third-party regulatory audits with zero major non-conformances.

**7. Maintenance, reliability & facilities management**

* Partner with the Engineering manager to achieve the goals on the Preventive and Predictive Maintenance programs to maximize asset reliability and minimize unplanned downtime.
* Ensure spare parts inventory management is optimized to balance carrying costs with equipment uptime requirements.
* Maintain physical plant infrastructure, utilities, security, and building compliance.

**Core Competencies & Attitudes**

* **Unbeatable attitude & resilience**: Maintains an optimistic, "can-do" mindset in the face of complex operational challenges, viewing equipment breakdowns, supply chain disruptions, and cost variances as solvable problems rather than roadblocks.
* **Passion for manufacturing excellence:** Brings genuine energy, pride, and enthusiasm to the shop floor, inspiring teams to take ownership of their craft and strive for world-class production standards.
* **Relentless focus on results:** Operates with a strong bias for execution and goal attainment, consistently driving teams to hit SQCDME targets and protect plant profitability.
* **Hands-on mindset:** Leads from the shop floor rather than behind a desk; actively walks the floor to observe processes, engage with operators, and solve problems at the source.
* **Extreme ownership & accountability:** Takes full responsibility for plant outcomes to engage the team can be focused on results.
* **Data-driven curiosity:** Approaches operational bottlenecks and cost variances (like Material Usage Variance) with analytical rigor, relying on root-cause data rather than guesswork.
* **Action & sense of urgency:** Responds swiftly to equipment downtime, safety hazards, and quality escapes while keeping teams calm and focused under pressure.
* **Servant leadership & empathy:** Listens actively to frontline workers, removes roadblocks for supervisors, and treats every team member with fairness and respect.
* **Continuous growth & adaptability:** Embraces change, challenges "*the way we've always done it"* and encourages calculated experimentation to improve efficiency.

**Core Soft Skills**

* **Multi-level communication:** Ability to translate complex operational metrics into strategic business updates for corporate executives, while communicating daily goals clearly and respectfully to frontline operators.
* **Conflict resolution & de-escalation:** Skilled at mediating disputes between competing departments and resolving shop-floor personnel conflicts calmly and fairly.
* **Emotional Intelligence:** Reads the moral and stress levels of the workforce, maintaining composure during crises like major line breakdowns, customer audits, or supply chain disruptions.
* **Cross-functional Influence:** Builds strong partnerships without direct authority over supporting teams to secure resources and align priorities.
* **Coaching & talent multiplication:** Focuses on developing future leaders by delegating effectively, giving constructive feedback, and empowering supervisors to make independent decisions rather than micromanaging.
* **Active listening:** Creates psychological safety on the plant floor so operators feel comfortable reporting near-misses, quality issues, or process inefficiencies early.
* **Stakeholder & customer relationship:** Represents the facility professionally during high-stakes customer visits, supplier negotiations, and community or regulatory inspections.

Requirements:

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Industrial, Mechanical, Chemical), Operations Management, Supply Chain, or Business Administration.
* **Experience:** 10+ years of progressive manufacturing experience, with at least 5 years in a Plant Manager, Assistant Plant Manager, or Operations Manager role overseeing 100+ employees.
* **Financial expertise:** Demonstrated experience managing a multi-million-dollar plant P&L, standard costing. Demonstrate understanding of managing budgets and controlling costs.
* **Systems proficiency:** Advanced working knowledge of SAP, MES platforms, and demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
* **Methodology expertise:** Proven track record of implementing Lean tools and driving measurable improvements in OEE, scrap reduction, and productivity. Working knowledge of Six Sigma, LEAN and/or Continuous Improvement principles, especially as they apply to a manufacturing environment

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Business Administration or master’s in engineering management.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification.
* Desirable food/beverage manufacturing plant operations experience, dairy experience strongly preferred

**Work Environment & Physical Demands**

* Split between an office environment and an active manufacturing floor with exposure to moving mechanical parts, varying noise levels, and temperature fluctuations.
* Requires regular walking/standing on the production floor and occasional travel (<5%) to corporate headquarters, conferences, suppliers, or sister facilities.

LALA US is an equal opportunity employer. This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an at-will relationship.

As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. Penn Aluminum is part of The Marmon Group, a Berkshire Hathaway Company. The Marmon Group comprises four autonomous companies consisting of 15 diverse, stand-alone business sectors and more than 185 independent manufacturing and service businesses. These businesses operate more than 350 manufacturing, distribution and service facilities, and employ more than 20,000 people worldwide.

Penn Aluminum is a premier manufacturer of aluminum drawn tubing and extruded shapes, providing high quality, engineered solutions to our customers. With strategically located production facilities, we are well positioned to support our customers throughout North America and beyond.

We are seeking a results-driven Director of Operations to lead our aluminum extrusion operations in Murphysboro, IL and Harlingen, TX. Our plants produce precision extruded and drawn tubing and custom profiles for Transportation, HVAC, Electrical, and Consumer Durables markets. Penn is investing over $60M in a state-of-the-art Murphysboro extrusion line that will double our tonnage output and open new markets, and this leader will be central to its success. The ideal candidate combines strong leadership, extrusion expertise, and a proven record of sustaining lean manufacturing across multiple sites.

* Multi-Site Operational Leadership: Provide strategic direction and oversight for safe, efficient, cost-effective production at Murphysboro and Harlingen, aligning standards, best practices, and performance metrics across both sites.
* Production Management: Oversee Murphysboro’s four extrusion presses, drawn benches, coil draw lines, cut-to-length, and fabrication, and Harlingen’s 2750T press with draw and heat treat processes.
* Lean & Continuous Improvement: Deploy and sustain lean methodologies (Kaizen, 5S, Value Stream Mapping, Six Sigma) to drive operational excellence.
* Strategic Planning: Partner with the President and executive team on long-term strategy, multi-site capacity planning, capital justification, and budget control.
* Resource Management: Optimize labor, materials, and equipment across both sites to maximize throughput, minimize waste, and improve OEE.

* Leadership: Proven ability to manage complex operations and large teams across multiple locations.

* The ability to make a direct impact on safety, customer satisfaction, and operational performance

records.description:
**Experiencing together a unique human adventure**

Animal health is key to the health of the planet. Working at Virbac means taking part in a unique human adventure in which the engagement of each individual contributes to its evolution. Encouraging internal mobility between positions and countries, offering individual development plans and building a partnership based on trust between managers and employees are as many perspectives of motivation for our teams. We also offer them a work environment conducive to exploring new territories and balancing their professional and personal lives. Finally, fostering their engagement to animal health also means listening to them and helping them to acquire new skills, preparing them for the challenges of tomorrow and encouraging them to contribute to an ever more responsible approach to our business.

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

Virbac Animal Health is seeking a Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology to join our Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) team. The Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology develops, implements, maintains, and improves robust manufacturing processes and facility infrastructure for right-first-time manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs. To plan, schedule, organize, and manage Technology Transfer Projects, CAPEX Engineering Projects, Validation, Technical Support, Alternate Raw Materials, Packaging, Life Cycle Management, and Team Leadership.

**Qualified candidates should possess the following:**

* 8 to 12+ years of Progressively responsible experience in engineering, and production management with a cGMP/FDA-regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Demonstrated track record in CAPEX project management, facility/process design, and multi-team operational leadership across multi-site or regional organizations.
* Strong expertise in managing capital and operational expense budgets.
* Proven Leadership in process improvement , life cycle management, and technology transfers.
* In-depth knowledge of cGMP, EHS regulations, and sustainable engineering practices.
* Strong multi-team leadership, communication, and cross-functional stakeholder management abilities.

**Benefits:** 13 Company paid Holidays; 5 Floating Holidays (prorated); 15 vacation days (prorated); 5 floating holidays (prorated); 6% 401k match; competitive pay and bonus opportunity; growth opportunities within the department and much more!

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

**Area of responsibility 1: Technology Transfer Activities**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the budget, planning, and robust manufacturing (RFT for the first commercial batches) of technology transfer projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Accountable for the definition and execution of the site and regional project roadmap in alignment with business needs and capability.
* Contributes to the selection of the right technology or CMO, taking into account product needs.
* Establish robust cost estimates (CAPEX, resources, future running costs) and planning estimates to support reliable NPVs and commercial strategy.
* Leadership of scale-up batches, engineering batches, and transfer to production.
* Develops manufacturing documentation (Master Batch Records, Submission batch protocols, etc.).
* Reviews and approves transfer and submission files.

**Expected results:** Ensure the robustness and capability of the process transferred to Manufacturing

**Area of responsibility 2: CAPEX Engineering Projects**

**Main activities:**

* Support and lead CAPEX engineering projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Evaluate, scope, and implement CAPEX projects for facility infrastructure, process improvements, and product needs.
* Responsible for managing annual capital budgets and operating expenses for the department.
* Partner closely with key local and global stakeholders (Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, Finance, etc.) to align project execution with regional operational goals.
* Ensure all engineering projects are performed in full compliance with applicable cGMP standards, EHS regulations, and company sustainability objectives.
* Oversee project budgets, engineering designs, contractor selection, and commissioning/qualification timelines.

**Expected Results:** Successful, on-time, and on-budget delivery of facility, process, and product CAPEX engineering projects that enhance regional capacity, EHS standards, compliance, and efficiency.

**Area of responsibility 3:** Process Improvement & Life Cycle Management (LCM)

**Main Activities:**

* Incorporate structured process improvement concepts (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma) across existing product portfolios.
* Lead Life Cycle Management changes to maintain and optimize the existing commercial product portfolio across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Collaborate closely with global and local stakeholders, including Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, and Finance, to evaluate and execute LCM initiatives.

**Expected Results:** Drive continuous product and process enhancement, lower operational costs, ensure ongoing regulatory compliance, and extend product life cycles.

**Area of responsibility 4: Validation**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the generation, technical review, execution, and technical approval of validation deliverables (Validation Master Plan, URS, equipment qualification, process validation, cleaning validation, computer system validation)across NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Lead validation projects and teams
* Ensures risk analysis methods are applied to validation activities
* Follow industry and regulatory trends and expectations (GMP, EHS, and sustainability guidelines).
* Review SOPs and batch documentation to ensure adequacy with validation criteria.
* Ensure prompt deviation resolution, including root cause analysis when required.

**Expected results:** A thorough understanding of the validation status of the regional sites, products, and equipment, with proactive remediation plans addressing any gaps.

**Area of responsibility 5: Technical support.**

**Main activities:**

* Troubleshooting and improvement proposal of current commercial products processes (robustness, productivity, cost efficiency & compliance)
* Lean and methodological approach during trouble shooting of complex product/process deviations
* Take ownership of complex product deviation / CAPA until approval
* Contribute to solution design in collaboration with R&D, Quality Assurance, Regulatory, etc.
* Develop, apply and train teams on efficient troubleshooting and optimization methodologies (FMEA,root cause analysis, etc)

**Expected results:** Deliver strong technical and operational process mastery to support manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.

**Area of responsibility 6: Alternate Raw materials**

**Main activities:**

* Technical feasibility assessments and reporting.
* Leads the engineering or validation batches (protocols/reports)
* Coordinates with the other departments (e.g. Quality Control, Regulatory Affairs)to support raw material changes.

**Expected results:** Support strategic sourcing and continuity of supply through alternate raw material qualifications.

**Area of responsibility 7: Packaging**

* Leadership of the packaging change controls and CAPAs (eg: alternate packaging components)
* Collaborates with packaging suppliers on new packaging equipment/materials, and technical feasibility assessments…
* Creates packaging specifications, including drawings and written text areas. Prepares and provides cost estimates for new packaging materials.
* Initiates, leads and Implements packaging improvements for existing products to reduce costs and/or improve packaging and product quality.

**Expected results:** Lead packaging design and modifications to drive productivity, efficiency and cost reductions while maintaining all customer and regulatory requirements.

**Area of responsibility 6: Team Leadership**

**Main Activities:**

* Translate team missions into clear, actionable SMART objectives
* Support and coach team members to help them achieve their full potential.
* Evaluate team performance through key indicators and foster a Lean culture.
* Plan and contribute to the continuous development and training of multi-disciplinary team members.
* Implement standard management practices aligned

with Virbac values while promoting a safe, sustainable working environment.

**Expected results:** Define and implement the NORAM Engineering & MSAT vision and organizational structure in alignment with group strategy.

Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).

All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.

This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Process scale-up and technology transfer

* Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
* Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
* Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
* Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities

Process characterization and PPQ readiness

* Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
* Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
* Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification
* Partner with Analytical Development to make sure methods are phase-appropriate, validated on time and fit to support characterization and PPQ

External manufacturing and CDMO management

* Serve as Mammoth's technical lead and person-in-plant at CDMOs and contract labs for development, engineering and GMP campaigns
* Lead selection, qualification and oversight of CDMO partners for drug product manufacturing, fill-finish operations and drug product testing, including technical due diligence, capacity and capability assessment, and scale-up fit
* Provide technical oversight for engineering and GMP runs at external partners
* Develop scalable, phase-appropriate aseptic drug product processes at CDMOs, including fill-finish operations, cryogenic handling (as applicable) and cold-chain compatibility
* Assess and implement suitable container-closure systems (vials, syringes) that meet regulatory and operational requirements
* Accountable for review and approval of batch records in accordance with regulatory guidelines; review campaign plans, deviations, investigations, CAPAs and change controls in partnership with Quality
* Manage partner timelines, budgets, deliverables and quality in collaboration with internal stakeholders; drive technical decisions and escalate issues early
* Project manage external stakeholders and high-profile partner meetings (up to 10% of time)
* Contribute to technical sections of quality agreements, statements of work and budgets

Regulatory and cross-functional support

* Author and review CMC sections for IND/IMPD/CTA amendments, end-of-Phase 2 and later filings (Module 3 process description, process development history, process validation)
* Support regulatory interactions and inspections with process knowledge and data
* Provide manufacturing input to program plans, timelines and supply forecasts

Team and resource leadership

* In the early phase, deliver through external resources: CDMO technical teams, consultants and contract MSAT staff
* Build the internal MSAT function in stages tied to milestones, including hiring plans, roles and the balance of internal and outsourced work
* Set up MSAT systems and practices: tech transfer templates, process knowledge management, data trending and lifecycle documentation

### **REEQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* PhD in chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry or a related field with 10+ years of industry experience, or MS with 14+ or BS with 16+ years of experience
* 6+ years in MSAT, process development or technical operations for parenteral drug products, including at least 3 years in a leadership role
* Hands-on experience scaling up LNP or comparable complex parenteral processes (liposomes, nanoparticles, nucleic acid formulations) from early clinical to late-stage scale
* Led at least one process characterization and PPQ campaign through completion, with working command of ICH Q8–Q12 and FDA/EMA process validation expectations
* Extensive experience managing CDMOs and contract labs as the sponsor's technical lead, including tech transfer, person-in-plant oversight, deviations and change control
* Experience with fill-finish operations, aseptic processing and external manufacturing oversight
* Strong working knowledge of cryogenic storage and cold-chain management for LNP drug products
* Track record of authoring CMC regulatory sections and supporting agency interactions
* Ability to influence and direct external partners without line authority, and to make sound technical calls under timeline pressure
* Ability for frequent domestic and international travel to CDMO and contract lab sites, estimated at up to [30–40]% and peaking during engineering, characterization and PPQ campaigns
* Must be able to travel internationally on short notice and hold, or be able to obtain, a valid passport and any visas needed for partner sites
* Ability to commit to extended on-site presence at CDMOs (person-in-plant) during critical campaigns, sometimes across time zones.
* Based in the San Francisco Bay Area preferred, with ability to work onsite at our Brisbane, CA location; hybrid or remote arrangements are available
* Ability to work Pacific Time Zone hours if not located on the West Coast
* Ability to travel to Mammoth’s Brisbane, CA HQ regularly if not local

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Direct experience with mRNA/LNP or gene editing drug products
* Experience with impingement jet or microfluidic mixing scale-up, TFF and sterile filtration of LNPs
* Experience with commercial process validation and BLA/MAA preparation
* Experience building a function or team from the ground up in a small or mid-size biotech
* Working knowledge of statistical tools for DoE and process data analysis (e.g., JMP, Minitab)

### **BENEFITS**

* Company-paid health/vision/dental benefits
* Unlimited vacation and generous sick time
* Company-sponsored meals and snacks
* Wellness, caregiver and ergonomics benefits
* 401(k) with company matching

Actual base salary will be determined by relevant professional experience, applicable skills, and internal equity

**COMPANY**

Mammoth Biosciences is a biotechnology company focused on leveraging its proprietary ultracompact CRISPR systems to develop long-term curative therapies, as well as other applications such as decentralized precision diagnostics. Founded by CRISPR pioneer and Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Trevor Martin, Janice Chen, and Lucas Harrington, the company’s ultracompact proteins are designed to enable *in vivo* gene editing in difficult to reach tissues utilizing both nuclease applications and new editing modalities beyond double stranded breaks, including base editing, gene writing, and epigenetic editing. The company is building out its pipeline of potential *in vivo* gene editing therapeutics and capabilities and has partnerships with leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to broaden the reach of its innovative and proprietary technology. Mammoth’s deep science and industry experience, along with a robust and differentiated intellectual property portfolio, have enabled the company to further its mission to transform the lives of patients and deliver on the full promise of CRISPR technologies.

Stored Energy Systems (SENS) is an award-winning manufacturer of premium quality power conversion products located in Longmont, CO. **View the SENS Product Catalog**

**Summary**

SENS is seeking a manufacturing engineering leader to help build and scale the organization, processes, and technical capabilities required for our next stage of growth. Supporting the expansion of existing manufacturing operations and establishing new operations at our Broomfield Systems manufacturing factory, this leader will establish the manufacturing engineering strategy, develop a multidisciplinary team, and translate business growth plans into manufacturing capacity and reliable production processes for our fastest-growing products.

This role leads manufacturing engineering, industrialization, tooling, test systems, automation, and technical production support for our systems products, with a strong emphasis on configure-to-order assembly manufacturing. Working closely with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, the Senior Manager will establish clear priorities, strengthen new product and production transfer readiness, and deliver measurable improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and equipment reliability.

A successful candidate will combine organizational leadership with practical technical judgment, building a team that can support daily production while executing the improvements and investments needed to scale.

**Responsibilities**

* Help to build and develop the manufacturing engineering organization. Assess current capabilities, define the team structure and staffing plan, recruit talent, and develop engineers and technical leaders to support SENS’s growth.
* Establish performance measures and execution discipline. Set departmental goals, review project and operational performance, communicate risks and resource needs, and hold the team accountable for measurable improvements in manufacturing readiness, capacity, productivity, and equipment reliability.
* Establish and execute the manufacturing engineering roadmap. Translate business growth, product plans, and production requirements into prioritized initiatives for manufacturing capacity, processes, tooling, test systems, automation, and equipment reliability.
* Lead manufacturing readiness for new products and production transfers. Partner with Design Engineering, Production, Quality, and Planning & Fulfillment to establish readiness criteria and ensure processes, equipment, tooling, test capability, documentation, and training are in place before production release.
* Develop scalable manufacturing processes and standards. Establish consistent methods for process development, validation, work instructions, engineering changes, and production controls across manufacturing locations while accommodating product-specific requirements.
* Expand manufacturing capacity and improve productivity. Lead engineering efforts in capacity analysis, line balancing, factory layout, workflow, cycle-time reduction, and constraint elimination to support production demand and improve labor efficiency.
* Provide reliable technical support to Production. Establish clear support coverage, escalation processes, and problem-solving practices that resolve production issues promptly and prevent recurrence while maintaining progress on strategic projects.
* Guide manufacturing technology development. Lead technical specialists responsible for manufacturing test systems, production software, tooling, and automation. Prioritize investments based on safety, quality, capacity, reliability, and financial return.
* Improve production equipment reliability. Establish equipment ownership, maintenance strategies, critical spare requirements, and preventive and predictive maintenance practices in partnership with Production and technical support teams.
* Manage projects, capital investments, and departmental resources. Develop business cases, budgets, schedules, and resource plans; oversee implementation and production acceptance; and verify that projects deliver their expected operational and financial benefits.
* Partner with Design Engineering on manufacturability. Incorporate manufacturing feedback early in product development and engineering changes to improve assembly, testability, quality, serviceability, and cost.
* Drive safe processes and sustained quality improvement. Partner with EHS and Quality to incorporate risk assessment, error prevention, root cause analysis, and corrective action into manufacturing processes and equipment changes.
* Oversee the development and maintenance of manufacturing processes, work instructions, test procedures, tooling, fixtures, automation systems, and production software solutions.
* Be directly accountable for engineering project delivery, manufacturing readiness, equipment reliability, and validated improvement benefits, while sharing accountability with Production and Quality for labor efficiency and first-pass yield (FPY).

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline, or an additional 4 tears of manufacturing engineering experience.
* Eight or more years of experience in manufacturing engineering, production engineering, industrialization, or a related technical manufacturing role.
* Three or more years of experience directly leading engineering or technical teams, including setting priorities, developing employees, allocating resources, and managing performance.
* Demonstrated success improving manufacturing performance, with measurable results in productivity, capacity, quality, cost, or equipment reliability.
* Experience developing and improving manufacturing processes, tooling, fixtures, work instructions, and production controls, including introducing new or revised products into production.
* Ability to lead engineers and technical specialists across manufacturing processes, test systems, automation, and production support, using sound technical judgment to evaluate solutions and resolve issues.
* Practical application of Lean Manufacturing and structured problem-solving methods, including root cause analysis and corrective action.

**Senior Manager of Operations**

**Scottsdale Mint | Casper, Wyoming**  
**Employment Type:** Full-Time | Salaried

**Company Summary**

Founded in 2008, Scottsdale Mint is a U.S.-based precious metals manufacturer recognized globally for its innovation, quality, and American craftsmanship. As a privately held producer of premium gold, silver, and platinum bullion, the company serves sovereign nations, central banks, Fortune 500 companies, industrial clients, and authorized distributors worldwide.

Operating from its advanced manufacturing facility in Casper, Wyoming, Scottsdale Mint specializes in high-purity bullion, legal-tender coin programs, and custom-branded precious metal products. The company combines artistic design, scientific precision, and advanced minting technology to deliver products recognized for their quality, detail, and authenticity.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Manager of Operations is responsible for overseeing the daily performance and overall effectiveness of Scottsdale Mint's Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing departments. This position provides leadership and direction to approximately 30 employees, ensuring manufacturing operations are safe, efficient, productive, and aligned with company objectives.

The successful candidate will be a visible, hands-on leader capable of managing multiple manufacturing functions, developing departmental supervisors, establishing accountability, and improving operational performance while supporting current production requirements and future manufacturing growth.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Manufacturing & Operations Management**

* Oversee daily operations and production performance across Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing.
* Establish departmental priorities, production goals, and performance expectations in coordination with senior management.
* Coordinate labor, equipment, and resources to maximize productivity, throughput, and manufacturing capacity.
* Monitor production schedules and workflow, identifying bottlenecks and implementing solutions to improve output and efficiency.
* Coordinate with Planning & Inventory Control, Fulfillment, Maintenance, Marketing, and other departments to support production requirements and company objectives.
* Develop, monitor, and report on departmental KPIs to optimize workforce utilization and ensure production schedule adherence.

**2. Leadership & Workforce Management**

* Provide leadership, direction, and accountability to departmental supervisors and employees.
* Manage staffing levels, scheduling, attendance, and labor allocation to meet production requirements.
* Establish clear expectations for employee performance, productivity, communication, and workplace conduct.
* Conduct performance reviews, address personnel matters, and establish development objectives for direct reports.
* Develop supervisory capabilities and ensure employees receive appropriate training to perform their responsibilities effectively.
* Foster a professional work environment emphasizing teamwork, accountability, ownership, and employee development.

**3. Safety, Compliance & Operational Excellence**

* Maintain consistent operating standards, manufacturing procedures, and a strong safety culture across all assigned departments.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, company safety policies, and applicable workplace requirements.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including production output, labor efficiency, downtime, quality, and schedule attainment.
* Evaluate manufacturing processes to identify safety concerns, operational inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.
* Promote proper equipment operation, preventative maintenance, housekeeping, and organization throughout manufacturing areas.
* Ensure operational and safety issues are addressed promptly and corrective actions are implemented.
* Communicate departmental performance, challenges, and improvement initiatives to senior management.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* 5–7 years of progressive manufacturing supervisory or management experience, preferably overseeing multiple departments.
* Experience managing production teams and workforces of approximately 25–50 employees preferred.
* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Management, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent practical experience will be considered.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production workflows, labor management, and operational efficiency.
* Working knowledge of OSHA regulations and manufacturing safety requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to manage production objectives, develop supervisors, and hold employees accountable for performance.
* Strong organizational, problem-solving, and verbal and written communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and manufacturing-related reporting systems.

**Position Expectations**

The Senior Manager of Operations is expected to take ownership of the overall performance of the assigned manufacturing departments. This individual must provide consistent leadership, establish clear priorities, and ensure departmental supervisors are effectively managing their teams and achieving established objectives.

Success will be measured by the ability to meet production goals, maintain safe and efficient operations, effectively manage workforce resources, improve manufacturing performance, and develop a capable and accountable team.

* Dental insurance
* Employee discount
* Health insurance

* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

***Job Title:*** ***Senior Manager, Quality Management***

***Job Code: 48241***

***Job Location: Orange, VA***

***Job Schedule: 4/10: Employees work 10 hour days, 4 days a week***

**Job Description:**

The **Senior Manager of Quality** will be responsible for leading all aspects of Quality Assurance throughout the product development lifecycle for L3Harris’ Culpeper, VA site. This position will have responsibility for direct supervision and leadership of ~60 quality personnel. The Sr. Manager will be responsible for driving continual process and product improvement ensuring product and process integrity, leading to customer satisfaction and overall mission success while supporting division quality, delivery and cost targets. This position will lead quality personnel and collaborate frequently with Program leadership, Engineering, Manufacturing and Supply Chain personnel. This is a hands-on, highly involved leadership position. Ability to obtain a Secret clearance is required for this position.

**Essential Functions:**

  

* Responsible for the Quality Engineering and Inspection functions, supporting all business practices, including quality planning, compliance monitoring and validation for programs, hardware, software and inspection.
* Responsibility for resolving technical challenges, ensuring successful tactical execution, as well as creating and implementing the strategic vision for the Quality department.
* Develop and implement strategic Quality initiatives and programs in support of the site promoting sound and effective principles as set forth in company procedures, government standards and directives, and commercially proven methodology and ensure that the department conforms to these principles.
* Promote a strong culture of quality focused on every employee engaged and enhancing the customer experience through rigorous attention to detail and prevention of defects.
* Work closely with the program teams and the functional organizations to ensure that all phases of the product life cycle, from early customer involvement through post-delivery support, meet the requirements for mission success.
* Ensure that manufacturing engineering, operations and design engineering interact sufficiently throughout the product planning and design phases to ensure a seamless hand-off during product transition to production including design reviews and facilitating quality concurrent Engineering.
* Responsible for the maintenance of quality records that document the quality status of material/products and provide necessary information and cumulative data for internal and external Customer responses.
* Develop, review and verify compliance of all Work Package Descriptions issued for Quality tasks for proposals and ongoing contracts/projects.
* Improve the efficiency of the Quality organization through effective leadership, individual and group training, and process improvement.
* Collect and analyze key quality measures such as Cost of Poor Quality to develop zero defect plans, improve yields and reduce rework during engineering and manufacturing efforts. Report to senior leadership on business performance including action plans to improve business execution and status of strategic initiatives.
* Maintain certification and compliance efforts for AS9100 and other required certifications.
* Business travel up to 10%.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s Degree and a minimum of 12 years of prior related Quality Management experience. Graduate Degree and a minimum of 10 years of prior related experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 16 years of prior related experience.
* Active Secret US Security Clearance.

**Preferred Additional Skills:**

  

* In depth knowledge of quality and reliability methods and procedures for hardware and software systems as they apply to the aerospace or electronic industry.
* Greenbelt or Blackbelt certification and/or proven education or work history in leading and implementing projects.
* Experience with Configuration Control management practices.
* ASQ certification preferred; Experience managing AS9100 certified business.
* 5+ years Quality management or operations leadership experience.
* Strong leadership and interpersonal skills including communications, facilitation, consulting, coaching, and influencing.
* Self-motivated and possess demonstrated ability to motivate others to achieve timely results.
* Highly collaborative style, capable of working across multiple functional areas to drive results.

In compliance with pay transparency requirements, the salary range for this role in Virginia is $121,500 – $225,500. This is not a guarantee of compensation or salary, as final offer amount may vary based on factors including but not limited to experience and geographic location. Global Quality Project & Portfolio Management

PMP and/or Lean Six Sigma Green Belt and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification is a plus.

* At least 8 years of relevant industry experience in Quality, Quality Systems, Project Management, or regulated environments

OR

Master’s degree in a related field with at least 6 years of relevant industry experience.

* Advanced degree in a science, engineering, or quality‑related discipline.
* Demonstrated experience managing global Quality projects or portfolios in regulated pharmaceutical, biotech, or medical device environments.
* Experience supporting Quality Systems, QA/QC initiatives, and cross‑functional quality transformations.

Become a **Senior Manager, Demand Side Management Quality Assurance & Engineering** at Southern California Edison (SCE) and build a better tomorrow. Because you’ll oversee the quality control of program implementations and ensure their compliance, ideally your background would include Demand Side Management (DSM), such as Energy Efficiency, Demand Response, Integrated Demand Side Management, and Distributed Energy Resources.

  

As a **Senior Manager, Demand Side Management Quality Assurance & Engineering**, your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

  

**Incident Management Team Expected Participation**: Employees are expected to support emergency response and/or business continuity efforts, including readiness to serve on an Incident Management Team (IMT) when needed. Employees will participate in an on-call rotation (approximately every four to six weeks), to support IMT activations during emergency events. IMT assignments may differ from an individual’s regular responsibilities.

Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger.

The Director of Operations is responsible for overseeing daily production activities to drive efficiency, maintain quality, and ensure adherence to company standards. This role leads the development and implementation of organizational strategies, standards, and best practices to achieve world-class operational performance. Additionally, the Director of Production collaborates closely with site and business leadership, leveraging resources and expertise to ensure our products consistently meet customer expectations.

Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Responsibilities:

* Lead with a clear view of where the organization needs to be in 1-3 years; communicates strategic direction to employees and how it fits with the day-to-day actions and results being driven.
* Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Implement and maintain value streams and SCQDCT management system within the site.
* Provide coaching and support to supervisors and frontline employees to enhance skills and performance.
* Set clear and measureable performance expectations, in line with corporate goals; proactively analyze and manage all relative operations performance metrics.
* Provide timely, accurate and complete reports on the operating conditions of the company.Ensure compliance with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements.
* Ensures alignment with functional leadership (e.g., Engineering, Finance, Quality, Facilities, and Human Resources) on performance management and talent development.
* Ensure the facilities operate within the Company’s ISO and FDA quality management system.
* Participate in the development of the location’s monthly revenue forecasts.
* Monitor and adjust production output and staff levels to support the location’s revenue and cost targets.
* Participate in the development and control of the location’s budgets and quarterly forecasts.
* Working with the senior leadership team, help to develop and implement winning strategies to grow revenues and profitability.
* Ensure the site maintains maximum confidentiality in a highly proprietary operationLead relationship with key intercompany customers to ensure maximum service throughout the value chain.

Required Qualifications:

* BS degree in a technical field, preferably engineering or life sciences.
* Prior experience managing a manufacturing department/organization in a regulated environment.
* Prior experience managing an engineering team.
* Experience working within a Lean, six-sigma organization.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Prior experience managing an independent manufacturing organization.
* Familiarity with contract manufacturing, ISO and FDA quality system requirements, medical device and diagnostics manufacturing.
* Lean, six-sigma green or black belt certified.
* Experience with Nitinol products and processing
* Experience wit Wire and Tube fabrication
* MBA or relevant business management experience.

Physical Demands:

* Ability to work long hours when necessary and to have a presence with a 24/7 operation.
* Domestic travel required

Compensation:

* The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000–$204,000.
* Our company policy is that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must already be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

Resonetics offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, well-being, and financial security of our employees and their families. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; a 401(k) retirement plan; paid time off (PTO); 10 paid holidays; Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA); life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) insurance; Short-Term Disability (STD) and Long-Term Disability (LTD) insurance; accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurance. Eligibility and benefit offerings may vary based on employment status and applicable plan provisions.
